definition_zh: 图像；影像；形象；印象；意象
definition_en: a visible representation of a person or thing, a picture formed in the mind, or the way someone or something is perceived
core_image: 镜面里映出的、与原物轮廓相似的那个影子
scene: She straightened the poster and said: The image on the screen is not the thing itself, only its likeness.
sceneCN: 这里 image 是「图像、映像」（第 1 个义项：可见的再现）；句意：屏幕上的是图像，不是事物本身，只是它的相似之影。图中可辨识物件：屏幕、海报、投影仪。

pos.zh: 图像；影像；形象；意象
成像；描绘；使……形成心像（多用于医学与技术语境）

senses.title: A visible representation
senses.titleCN: 可见的再现：图像
senses.definition: a picture, statue, photograph, or other visual representation of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人、物或场景的图画、雕像、照片或其他视觉再现
senses.example: The gallery displayed an image of the city in 1900.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊展出了一幅 1900 年这座城市的图像。
senses.why: Latin imago meant 'a copy, a likeness, a statue'. The starting point is not the thing itself but a second thing made to look like it, so an image is always a representation standing in for an original.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 imago 意为“复制品、相似物、雕像”。它的起点不是事物本身，而是另一个做成与之相似的东西，因此 image 始终是替原物出场的再现。

senses.title: Exact likeness: resemblance
senses.titleCN: 相似之形：酷似某人某物
senses.definition: a person or thing that looks exactly like another, especially in the phrase the (very) image of
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人另一物长得一模一样的人或物，尤用于 the (very) image of 这一短语
senses.example: The child is the very image of her father.
senses.exampleCN: 这孩子酷似她父亲。
senses.why: If an image is a likeness, then a living person can also be called an image when the resemblance is complete. The copy has become indistinguishable from what it copies.
senses.whyCN: 既然 image 是相似之形，那么当相似程度达到极致时，一个活人也可以被称为 image。此时复制品与原物已经难以分辨。

senses.title: A reflection in a mirror or lens
senses.titleCN: 光学成像：镜中或透镜后的像
senses.definition: the reproduction of an object formed by a mirror, lens, or other optical system
senses.definitionCN: 由镜子、透镜或其他光学系统形成的物体再现
senses.example: The lens formed a sharp image on the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 透镜在屏幕上形成了一个清晰的像。
senses.why: A mirror does mechanically what a sculptor does by hand: it produces a second visible version of the thing. English recorded this sense in the early 14c., calling the reflected shape an image.
senses.whyCN: 镜子以机械方式做了雕塑家用手做的事：造出该物的第二个可见版本。英语在 14 世纪早期就记录了这一义项，把反射出的形状称为 image。

senses.title: A picture in the mind
senses.titleCN: 心像：脑中的画面
senses.definition: a picture or representation formed in the mind, especially through memory or imagination
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中形成的画面或再现，尤指通过记忆或想象
senses.example: Close your eyes and form an image of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 闭上眼睛，在脑中想象这个房间的样子。
senses.why: The mental sense already existed in Latin. The mind can hold a likeness of something absent, so the same word covers a picture that no eye can see.
senses.whyCN: 心像这一义项在拉丁语中就已存在。心智可以持有一个不在场之物的相似物，于是同一个词也覆盖了眼睛看不到的画面。

senses.title: Public impression: reputation
senses.titleCN: 公众印象：外界眼中的形象
senses.definition: the impression that a person, company, or product gives to the public, whether or not it matches reality
senses.definitionCN: 个人、公司或产品给公众留下的印象，不论其是否与事实相符
senses.example: The company spent millions to improve its public image.
senses.exampleCN: 公司花了数百万来改善公众形象。
senses.why: A public image is a likeness held in many minds rather than one. Advertising made this sense common around 1958: what people think of a thing becomes a picture that can be managed.
senses.whyCN: 公众形象是存在于许多人头脑中的相似之形，而不是一个人的心像。广告业在 1958 年前后让这一义项流行起来：人们对某物的看法变成了一幅可以被经营的画面。

senses.title: Self-image: how one sees oneself
senses.titleCN: 自我形象：自己看自己的样子
senses.definition: the picture a person has of their own appearance, abilities, or worth
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对自己外貌、能力或价值的看法
senses.example: She struggles with her body image.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己的身体形象感到困扰。
senses.why: Turn the mirror inward and the likeness being judged is one's own. Self-image is the mental picture a person holds of the person they are.
senses.whyCN: 把镜子转向内部，被评判的那个相似之形就是自己。自我形象就是一个人对自己这个人所持有的心中画面。

senses.title: A figure in language: poetic image
senses.titleCN: 语言意象：诗中的形象
senses.definition: a description or figure of speech that creates a vivid picture in the reader's mind
senses.definitionCN: 在读者心中唤起鲜明画面的描写或修辞
senses.example: The poem is built on a single striking image.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗建立在单一而鲜明的意象之上。
senses.why: Words can do what paint does: they make the mind see a shape. Rhetoric borrowed the visual word for this mental picture, and imagery became the name for a whole set of them.
senses.whyCN: 文字能做颜料做的事：让心智看见一个形状。修辞学借用了这个视觉词来指这种心中画面，imagery 则成为一整组此类画面的名称。

senses.title: An image produced by a device
senses.titleCN: 设备生成的影像
senses.definition: a visual display or file produced by a camera, scanner, satellite, or medical instrument
senses.definitionCN: 由相机、扫描仪、卫星或医疗仪器产生的视觉显示或文件
senses.example: The satellite sent back images of the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星传回了海岸的影像。
senses.why: The device does not invent the likeness; it captures light that already carries the shape of the thing. Digital imaging extends the old sense into files and screens.
senses.whyCN: 设备并不凭空发明相似之形，它捕捉的光本身就带着该物的形状。数字成像把这一古老义项延伸到了文件与屏幕。

senses.title: An embodiment: the image of a quality
senses.titleCN: 化身：某种品质的具象
senses.definition: a person or thing that seems to embody a quality completely
senses.definitionCN: 似乎完整地体现某种品质的人或物
senses.example: He was the image of calm during the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机中他就是沉着的化身。
senses.why: When a quality becomes visible in a person, that person is its image. The abstract thing now has a shape you can point to, exactly as a statue gives a god a shape.
senses.whyCN: 当一种品质在某人身上变得可见，这个人就成了它的 image。抽象之物如今有了可以指认的形状，正如雕像给了神一个形状。

intro.en: Image comes through Old French from Latin imago, the word for a likeness or statue, built on the verb imitari 'to imitate'. The deepest PIE root is a reconstruction, so it is marked as probable rather than certain.
intro.cn: image 经古法语来自拉丁语 imago，本义是“相似之形、雕像”，其词干与动词 imitari“模仿”相关。最底层的原始印欧语词根属于重构，因此只能标为“一般认为是”，而非确定事实。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'a piece of statuary; an artificial representation that looks like a person or thing'. The word entered with the object, not with abstract meaning.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“雕像；看起来像某人某物的人造再现”。这个词是随实物一起进来的，最初并没有抽象含义。

items.en: Old French image, earlier imagene (11c.), meant 'image, likeness; figure, drawing, portrait; reflection; statue'. It came from Latin imaginem, the accusative of imago.
items.cn: 古法语 image（更早作 imagene，11 世纪）意为“图像、相似物；图形、绘画、肖像；倒影；雕像”。它来自拉丁语 imago 的宾格 imaginem。

items.en: Latin imago (genitive imaginis) meant 'copy, imitation, likeness; statue, picture', and also 'phantom, ghost, apparition' and figuratively 'idea, appearance'. The phantom sense shows that an image can exist without a solid original.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imago（属格 imaginis）意为“复制品、模仿、相似物；雕像、图画”，也指“幽灵、鬼魂、幻影”，并引申为“观念、外表”。幽灵这一义项说明：image 可以没有实体原物而存在。

items.en: Imago was formed from the stem of imitari 'to copy, imitate'. The reconstructed PIE root *aim- 'to copy' is generally accepted but not directly attested, so the deepest layer is source uncertain.
items.cn: imago 由 imitari“复制、模仿”的词干构成。重构的原始印欧语词根 *aim-“复制”被普遍接受，但没有直接文献佐证，因此最深层词源标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: The sense 'reflection in a mirror' is recorded. A mirror image is the clearest everyday proof that a likeness can exist apart from the object.
items.cn: “镜中倒影”这一义项被记录下来。镜像是最清楚的日常证据：相似之形可以脱离原物而存在。

items.en: The mental sense appears in English in the late 14c. The 'public impression' sense existed in isolated cases from 1908 but became common only around 1958, through advertising and public relations.
items.cn: 心像义在 14 世纪晚期进入英语。“公众印象”义从 1908 年起有零星用例，直到 1958 年前后经由广告与公共关系行业才变得通行。

note.en: The first group is close in spelling or derivation; the second is close in meaning. Check form first, then sense.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或派生上接近，第二组在意义上接近。先看词形，再看词义。

entries.definition: to form a picture of something in the mind. It is the verb built on the same imago stem, not a synonym for image as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在头脑中形成某物的画面。它是建立在同一 imago 词干上的动词，并非名词 image 的同义词。

entries.definition: images considered as a group, especially poetic or visual imagery. It names a collection, while image names one picture.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的意象或图像，尤指诗歌意象或视觉影像。它指一组画面，而 image 指单幅画面。

entries.definition: the adult stage of an insect after its final moult, or in psychology an idealized image of a parent. Both uses preserve the Latin 'likeness' idea.
entries.definitionCN: 昆虫最后一次蜕皮后的成虫阶段；心理学中指对父母的理想化形象。两种用法都保留了拉丁语“相似之形”的观念。

entries.definition: a painting, drawing, or photograph. It is the everyday word for a made image, while image is broader and can be mental or public.
entries.definitionCN: 绘画、素描或照片。它是表示“做出来的图像”的日常词，而 image 范围更广，可以是心像或公众形象。

entries.definition: the quality of looking like someone or something, or a portrait that shows this. It stresses resemblance rather than the medium.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像某人某物的性质，或表现这种相似性的肖像。它强调“相似”，而不是媒介。

entries.definition: the opinion or feeling that others form about someone. In the public sense it overlaps with image, but impression stresses what the viewer feels.
entries.definitionCN: 他人对某人形成的看法或感觉。在公众形象义上与 image 重叠，但 impression 强调观看者的感受。

entries.definition: the outward appearance of something, often when the reality is different. It is more literary and more sceptical than image.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的外表，常暗示实质并不相同。它比 image 更书面，也更带怀疑意味。

normalIntro.en: Real word parts, real phrases, and real relatives, with no invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，不编造顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin imago is a likeness, and imitari means 'to imitate'. An image is always something made to resemble something else.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 imago 是“相似之形”，imitari 意为“模仿”。image 始终是做成与另一物相似的东西。

normal.en: imagine, imagination, imagery and image all grow from the same stem: first you make a picture in the mind, then you make one outside.
normal.cn: imagine、imagination、imagery、image 都出自同一词干：先在心中造一幅画，再在外面造一幅画。

normal.en: The phrase the very image of someone uses the oldest sense: an exact likeness, as if a person had stepped out of a portrait.
normal.cn: the very image of someone 这一短语用的是最古老的义项：一模一样的相似之形，仿佛人从肖像里走了出来。

normal.en: A mirror image is the same shape reversed. It proves that the likeness can travel without the object.
normal.cn: mirror image 是方向相反的同一形状。它证明相似之形可以脱离原物而传递。

normal.en: Public image is the likeness held in many minds at once; self-image is the likeness held in one's own mind.
normal.cn: public image 是同时存在于众多头脑中的相似之形；self-image 是存在于自己头脑中的相似之形。

abstract.en: Think of a stamp and its print: the stamp is the thing, the print is the image. The print can be copied again, and further from the original each time.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章和它印出的图案：印章是实物，印痕是 image。印痕还能再被复制，每复制一次就离原物更远一步。

abstract.en: An image is a shape that has learned to travel: into stone, into paint, into a lens, into a mind, into a reputation.
abstract.cn: image 是一个学会了旅行的形状：进入石头、进入颜料、进入透镜、进入心智、进入名声。

abstract.en: Every image has two owners, the thing copied and the mind that receives it. That is why a public image can disagree with the facts and still be real.
abstract.cn: 每一幅 image 都有两个主人：被复制的物，以及接收它的心智。正因如此，公众形象可以与事实不符，却依然真实存在。

examples.en: The documentary uses old photographs and vivid images of the harbour.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片使用了港口的老照片和鲜活的影像。

examples.en: Her public image as a strict manager hides how patient she is with beginners.
examples.cn: 她严厉经理的公众形象，掩盖了她对新手有多耐心。

examples.en: The scanner images the bone in thin slices.
examples.cn: 扫描仪把骨头切成薄层成像。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一妹纸”——手机相册里存着一张妹纸的照片 → image 图像、形象

root: 源自拉丁语 imago“相似之形、雕像、幻影”，词干与 imitari“模仿”相关；经古法语 image 于约 1200 年进入英语，核心是“照原物做出的相似之形”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of image, all built on one idea: a second visible version of something. The likeness can sit in stone, in a lens, in the mind, in a reputation, or in a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: image 的九个义项都建立在同一个观念上：某物的第二个可见版本。这个相似之形可以落在石头上、透镜里、心智中、名声上，或机器里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape made to match another shape, like a reflection standing beside its object.
core.cn: 核心意象：照着另一个形状做出来的形状，像站在原物旁边的倒影。

branches.en: REPRESENTATION AND RESEMBLANCE: a made picture and a living look-alike are both 'second versions' of an original.
branches.cn: 再现与相似：做出来的图画与活生生的酷似者，都是原物的“第二版本”。

branches.en: OPTICS: a mirror or lens produces a likeness without a maker, which is the purest physical case.
branches.cn: 光学：镜子或透镜在没有制作者的情况下产生相似之形，是最纯粹的物理情形。

branches.en: THE MIND: memory and imagination hold a picture of something absent; self-image turns that picture toward oneself.
branches.cn: 心智：记忆与想象持有不在场之物的画面；自我形象则把这幅画转向自己。

branches.en: REPUTATION AND EMBODIMENT: many minds can hold one shared likeness, and a person can become the visible shape of a quality.
branches.cn: 名声与化身：众多头脑可以共持同一个相似之形，一个人也可以成为某种品质的可见形状。

branches.en: LANGUAGE AND MACHINE: words and cameras both manufacture likenesses, one in the mind and one on a screen.
branches.cn: 语言与机器：文字与相机都在制造相似之形，一个造在心中，一个造在屏幕上。

intro.en: Image is a whole Latin noun, not a prefix plus a living English root. English builds on it with -ine, -ination, -ery and compounds such as self-image.
intro.cn: image 是一个完整的拉丁名词，并非“前缀 + 活的英语词根”。英语在它之上加 -ine、-ination、-ery 等后缀，并构成 self-image 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is imago 'likeness' and imitari 'to imitate'. English relatives include imagine, imitation and the technical term imago.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 imago“相似之形”与 imitari“模仿”。英语同族词包括 imagine、imitation，以及专业术语 imago。

items.meaning: to form a picture of something in the mind
items.meaningCN: 在头脑中形成某物的画面；想象
items.example: Imagine the room before you open the door.
items.exampleCN: 开门之前先想象一下这个房间。

items.meaning: the power or act of forming mental images
items.meaningCN: 形成心像的能力或行为；想象力（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: The design shows a great deal of imagination.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计展现出丰富的想象力。

items.meaning: existing only in the mind, not in reality
items.meaningCN: 只存在于心中的；虚构的（-ary 表示“与……有关的”）
items.example: The child invented an imaginary friend.
items.exampleCN: 这个孩子虚构了一个想象中的朋友。

items.meaning: good at forming new ideas and pictures in the mind
items.meaningCN: 富有想象力的；善于在脑中形成新想法与新画面的
items.example: She gave an imaginative answer to the question.
items.exampleCN: 她对这个问题给出了富有想象力的回答。

items.meaning: images as a group, especially in art or writing
items.meaningCN: 作为整体的意象，尤指艺术或文学中的意象（-ry 表示集合）
items.example: The poem's imagery is drawn from the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗的意象取自海洋。

items.meaning: the process of producing images, especially medical or satellite imaging
items.meaningCN: 生成影像的过程，尤指医学成像或卫星成像
items.example: Brain imaging showed a small change in blood flow.
items.exampleCN: 脑成像显示出血流的一处微小变化。

items.meaning: without images or mental pictures
items.meaningCN: 没有图像的；不产生心像的（-less 表示“没有”）
items.example: The meditation aims at an imageless state.
items.exampleCN: 这种冥想追求一种无像的状态。

items.meaning: the picture a person holds of their own appearance or worth
items.meaningCN: 一个人对自身外表或价值的看法；自我形象
items.example: Praise at the right moment can repair a damaged self-image.
items.exampleCN: 恰到好处的赞美可以修补受损的自我形象。

items.meaning: to create a new image of something, especially a disk or a brand
items.meaningCN: 重新成像；为某物（尤指磁盘或品牌）制作新的形象
items.example: The team reimaged the laptop before handing it over.
items.exampleCN: 团队在交付前给笔记本电脑重新做了系统镜像。

latinEntries.meaning: likeness, copy, statue, picture; also phantom or ghost
latinEntries.meaningCN: 相似之形、复制品、雕像、图画；也指幻影或鬼魂

definition_zh: 撞击；冲击力；影响；作用；冲击，撞击
definition_en: the force of one object hitting another, a strong effect on someone or something, or to hit or affect something forcefully
core_image: 两物相撞的那一瞬，力从接触点向四周传开
scene: The engineer points at the cracked bumper: The impact at thirty miles an hour was enough to bend the frame.
sceneCN: 这里 impact 是「撞击、冲击」（第 1 个义项：两物相碰）；句意：每小时三十英里的撞击就足以使车架弯曲。图中可辨识物件：凹陷的保险杠、裂开的车架、测速仪。

pos.zh: 撞击；冲击力；影响；作用
撞击；冲击；对……产生强烈影响

derivatives.zh: 撞击体；撞击器（天文、工程）

senses.title: A collision: one thing striking another
senses.titleCN: 碰撞：一物击中另一物
senses.definition: the act of one object hitting another with force
senses.definitionCN: 一个物体用力击中另一个物体的动作
senses.example: The impact of the two cars could be heard across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 两车相撞的声音整条街都听得见。
senses.why: Latin impactus is the past participle of impingere 'to drive or strike into'. The word begins as a physical event: something is driven against something else.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 impactus 是 impingere“推入、撞入”的过去分词。这个词最初就是一个物理事件：某物被用力撞向另一物。

senses.title: The force of a collision
senses.titleCN: 冲击力：碰撞传递的力量
senses.definition: the force or energy with which one body strikes another
senses.definitionCN: 一个物体撞击另一个物体时所带的力或能量
senses.example: The wall was designed to absorb the impact of a falling beam.
senses.exampleCN: 这面墙的设计可以吸收落梁的冲击力。
senses.why: A collision is not only an event but also a quantity. Physics measures how much momentum is exchanged at the moment of contact, and that quantity is the impact.
senses.whyCN: 碰撞不仅是一个事件，也是一个量。物理学测量接触瞬间交换了多少动量，这个量就是 impact。

senses.title: A strong effect on something
senses.titleCN: 影响：对某事的强力作用
senses.definition: a powerful effect that something has on a situation, process, or person
senses.definitionCN: 某事物对局势、过程或人产生的强大作用
senses.example: The new law had a major impact on small businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律对小企业产生了重大影响。
senses.why: The metaphor is direct: an effect arrives with force, as if one thing had struck another. Since 1817 English has used impact for a forceful impression rather than a physical blow.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很直接：影响是带着力量到来的，就像一物击中了另一物。自 1817 年起，英语用 impact 表示强烈的“作用”，而不再限于物理打击。

senses.title: A striking impression on the mind
senses.titleCN: 震撼：留在心里的强烈印象
senses.definition: a strong and lasting impression made on someone's feelings or thoughts
senses.definitionCN: 在人的情感或思想上留下的强烈而持久的印象
senses.example: The final scene made a deep impact on the audience.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一幕给观众留下了深深的震撼。
senses.why: If an effect can hit a situation, it can also hit a mind. The mental version keeps the force but loses the physical contact.
senses.whyCN: 既然作用可以击中局势，也就可以击中人心。这个心理版本保留了“力”，却去掉了物理接触。

senses.title: Environmental impact
senses.titleCN: 环境足迹：对自然的作用
senses.definition: the effect of human activity on the natural environment
senses.definitionCN: 人类活动对自然环境造成的作用
senses.example: The report assesses the environmental impact of the new airport.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告评估了新机场的环境影响。
senses.why: The effect is now measured against a system that cannot speak for itself. Impact becomes a footprint: the mark left by something pressing on the world.
senses.whyCN: 此时作用被拿来与一个无法为自己发声的系统对照。impact 变成了足迹：某物压在世界之上留下的印记。

senses.title: To hit something forcefully
senses.titleCN: 撞击：用力碰上
senses.definition: to strike something with force, or to collide with it
senses.definitionCN: 用力击中某物，或与之相撞
senses.example: The asteroid impacted the surface at high speed.
senses.exampleCN: 小行星高速撞击了地表。
senses.why: The verb keeps the Latin literal sense 'drive into'. In modern usage it is often technical: asteroids, projectiles and test dummies impact surfaces.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语“推入”的本义。现代用法多为技术语境：小行星、弹体、碰撞测试假人会 impact 表面。

senses.title: To affect something strongly
senses.titleCN: 冲击：对某事产生强烈作用
senses.definition: to have a strong effect on a situation, group, or person
senses.definitionCN: 对局势、群体或个人产生强烈作用
senses.example: Rising rents are impacting families across the city.
senses.exampleCN: 上涨的租金正在冲击全城的家庭。
senses.why: The verb extends the metaphor of a blow. An event does not merely touch a group; it lands on it and changes its shape.
senses.whyCN: 动词延伸了“打击”的比喻。一个事件不只是触碰到某个群体，而是落在它身上并改变它的形状。

senses.title: To press or drive something firmly in
senses.titleCN: 压入：把某物牢牢顶进去
senses.definition: to press something firmly into another substance, especially in dentistry or mechanics
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢压入另一物质中，尤用于牙科或机械领域
senses.example: A badly impacted tooth may need to be removed.
senses.exampleCN: 严重阻生的牙齿可能需要拔除。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, recorded about 1600: 'press closely into something'. It survives in the dental term impacted tooth, where the tooth is driven into the jaw and cannot emerge.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，约 1600 年记录为“紧紧压入某物”。它保留在牙科术语 impacted tooth 中：牙齿被顶入颌骨而无法长出。

senses.title: On impact: the instant of contact
senses.titleCN: 接触瞬间：撞击发生的一刻
senses.definition: used in the phrase on impact, meaning at the exact moment of contact
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 on impact，表示正好在接触的那一刻
senses.example: The airbag opens on impact.
senses.exampleCN: 安全气囊在撞击瞬间打开。
senses.why: An impact has a before and an after, and the phrase names the boundary between them. All the force is present in that single instant.
senses.whyCN: 一次 impact 有之前与之后，这个短语命名的正是两者之间的边界。所有的力都集中在那一瞬。

intro.en: Impact is a Latin participle turned English noun and verb. Its root pangere 'to fasten, fix' is the same one behind impinge, and the original sense of pressing something in survives in dentistry.
intro.cn: impact 是一个变成英语名词与动词的拉丁语分词。其词根 pangere“固定、钉住”也见于 impinge；最初“压入”的义项至今保留在牙科学中。

items.en: The verb is first recorded as 'press closely into something', from Latin impactus, past participle of impingere.
items.cn: 动词最早记录为“紧紧压入某物”，来自拉丁语 impingere 的过去分词 impactus。

items.en: Impingere meant 'to push into, drive into, strike against', from in- 'into' + pangere 'to fix, fasten'. Pangere is reconstructed from PIE *pag- 'to fasten'.
items.cn: impingere 意为“推入、打入、撞上”，由 in-“进入”+ pangere“固定、钉住”构成。pangere 可重构自原始印欧语 *pag-“固定”。

items.en: The noun appears with the sense 'collision, act of striking against'. It was formed from the verb, not borrowed directly from Latin.
items.cn: 名词以“碰撞、相撞的动作”义出现。它由动词构成，并非直接从拉丁语借入。

items.en: The figurative sense 'forceful impression' is recorded (Coleridge). The blow now lands on feelings and arguments rather than on bodies.
items.cn: 比喻义“强烈的印象”被记录（柯勒律治）。这一击如今落在情感与论点上，而不是落在身体上。

items.en: Impacted teeth are recorded, preserving the oldest 'pressed in' sense. The dental use is a direct survival, not a new metaphor.
items.cn: “阻生牙”被记录，保留了最古老的“压入”义。牙科用法是直接留存，而不是新的比喻。

items.en: The verb develops the sense 'strike forcefully against' by 1916 and 'have a forceful effect on' by 1935. The modern noun phrase environmental impact belongs to the later 20th century.
items.cn: 动词在 1916 年前后发展出“用力撞击”义，1935 年前后发展出“产生强烈作用”义。现代短语 environmental impact 属于 20 世纪后期。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin striking root; the near-meaning group separates physical force from effect.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语“撞击”词根；近义组区分物理力量与抽象作用。

entries.definition: to hit or encroach on something, often used of light, sound, or rights. It shares impingere and pangere with impact.
entries.definitionCN: 撞击或侵犯某物，常用于光、声或权利。它与 impact 共享 impingere 与 pangere 词根。

entries.definition: the state of being wedged or pressed in, especially of a tooth or faeces. It is the noun from impact in its oldest sense.
entries.definitionCN: 被嵌塞或压入的状态，尤指牙齿或粪便。它是 impact 最古老义项的名词形式。

entries.definition: an object that strikes a surface, used in planetary science and engineering. It is impact + -or 'thing that does'.
entries.definitionCN: 撞击表面的物体，用于行星科学与工程。它是 impact + -or“做某事之物”。

entries.definition: a change produced by an action or cause. It is neutral and does not imply force, while impact stresses the strength of the effect.
entries.definitionCN: 由行为或原因引起的变化。它语气中性，不含“力量”意味，而 impact 强调作用的强度。

entries.definition: the power to affect behaviour or opinions, often gradually. It is softer and more social than impact.
entries.definitionCN: 影响行为或观点的力量，常是渐进的。它比 impact 更柔和，也更偏社会层面。

entries.definition: the act of two objects hitting each other. It names only the physical event, not the force or the effect.
entries.definitionCN: 两个物体相互撞击的动作。它只指物理事件，不指力量或影响。

entries.definition: a sudden forceful blow or a sudden strong emotional reaction. It stresses surprise and violence more than impact does.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的强力打击，或突然的强烈情绪反应。它比 impact 更强调突然与猛烈。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases, with no invented sound-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语，不编造谐音。

normal.en: in- 'into' + pangere 'to fasten': to impact is to drive something in until it is fixed.
normal.cn: in-“进入”+ pangere“固定”：impact 就是把某物顶进去，直到它固定住。

normal.en: An impacted tooth is literally a tooth pressed in and unable to come out, which is the oldest sense of the word.
normal.cn: impacted tooth 字面上就是被压进去、长不出来的牙，这正是这个词最古老的义项。

normal.en: The phrase on impact marks the exact instant of contact, the point where before becomes after.
normal.cn: on impact 这一短语标记接触的准确瞬间，也就是“之前”变成“之后”的那一点。

normal.en: Environmental impact is the footprint left by pressure on the natural world.
normal.cn: environmental impact 是压力在自然世界上留下的足迹。

normal.en: impactful is a modern adjective for something that lands with force on people's minds.
normal.cn: impactful 是现代形容词，指某物带着力量落在人们心上。

abstract.en: Picture a hammer and a nail: the nail does not move because it wants to, but because force arrives at one point and spreads.
abstract.cn: 想象锤子与钉子：钉子移动不是因为它想动，而是因为力在一点到达并向四周传开。

abstract.en: Every impact has a contact point and a wave. The contact is the event; the wave is the effect that reaches things not even touched.
abstract.cn: 每次 impact 都有一个接触点和一道波。接触点是事件，波则是抵达那些甚至没被碰到之物的作用。

abstract.en: A word, a law, or a design can impact without any collision: the force is real, only the contact is invisible.
abstract.cn: 一个词、一条法律或一项设计可以在没有碰撞的情况下 impact：力是真实的，只是接触看不见。

examples.en: The impact of the fall broke two bones in his wrist.
examples.cn: 摔倒的冲击使他腕部两处骨折。

examples.en: Remote work has had a lasting impact on how cities use office space.
examples.cn: 远程工作对城市如何使用办公空间产生了持久影响。

examples.en: Scientists are studying how the comet will impact the moon's surface.
examples.cn: 科学家正在研究这颗彗星将如何撞击月球表面。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬拍它”——硬碰硬地拍上去 → impact 撞击、冲击力

root: 源自拉丁语 impingere“推入、撞上”的过去分词 impactus，由 in-“进入”+ pangere“固定、钉住”构成，核心是“把力集中到一点、压进去”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of impact, all built on one event: force arriving at a point. The point can be a car, a bone, a budget, a mind, or an ecosystem.
sensesIntro.cn: impact 的九个义项都建立在同一个事件上：力在一点到达。这个点可以是汽车、骨头、预算、心智，也可以是生态系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two surfaces meet and force travels outward from the contact point.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个表面相遇，力从接触点向外传开。

branches.en: PHYSICAL EVENT: collision, its force, and the instant of contact are three views of the same blow.
branches.cn: 物理事件：碰撞、其冲击力、接触瞬间，是同一击的三种视角。

branches.en: EFFECT ON SYSTEMS: a law or an airport lands on a society or an ecosystem and changes its shape.
branches.cn: 对系统的作用：一条法律或一座机场落在社会或生态系统上，并改变其形状。

branches.en: EFFECT ON MINDS: the blow is emotional; what is struck is an audience's feelings.
branches.cn: 对心智的作用：这一击是情绪性的，被击中的是观众的情感。

branches.en: VERBAL FORCE: to impact is either to hit a surface or to act strongly on a situation.
branches.cn: 动词之力：impact 要么是击中表面，要么是对局势产生强烈作用。

branches.en: PRESSING IN: the oldest branch, where a tooth or object is driven in and cannot come out.
branches.cn: 压入：最古老的一支，牙齿或物体被顶进去而出不来。

intro.en: Impact is a Latin participle, so its English family is built with -ed, -ful, -ion and -or rather than with a live prefix.
intro.cn: impact 是拉丁语分词，因此它的英语词族靠 -ed、-ful、-ion、-or 构成，而不是靠活的前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives are impingere 'to strike against' and pangere 'to fasten'. The same pangere family gives impinge and, through a different path, compact and pact.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词是 impingere“撞上”与 pangere“固定”。同一 pangere 词族还给出 impinge，并经另一条路径给出 compact 与 pact。

items.meaning: struck by force; wedged in and unable to come out
items.meaningCN: 受冲击的；被嵌住而无法长出的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The dentist found an impacted wisdom tooth.
items.exampleCN: 牙医发现一颗阻生智齿。

items.meaning: having a strong effect on people
items.meaningCN: 有强大影响力的；给人强烈印象的
items.example: The speech was short but impactful.
items.exampleCN: 这段演讲很短，却很有冲击力。

items.meaning: the condition of being firmly wedged in
items.meaningCN: 嵌塞；阻生（-ion 表示状态或过程）
items.example: Bone impaction can make the fracture harder to fix.
items.exampleCN: 骨嵌塞会使骨折更难固定。

items.meaning: an object designed to strike a surface
items.meaningCN: 撞击体；撞击器（-or 表示施动之物）
items.example: The probe released a small impactor toward the comet.
items.exampleCN: 探测器向彗星释放了一个小型撞击器。

items.meaning: relating to or producing impact
items.meaningCN: 与冲击有关的；产生冲击的（较少用）
items.example: The impactive force of the wave cracked the glass.
items.exampleCN: 波产生的冲击力震裂了玻璃。

items.meaning: happening before a collision
items.meaningCN: 撞击前的
items.example: Pre-impact braking reduced the speed by half.
items.exampleCN: 撞击前的刹车把速度降低了一半。

items.meaning: happening after a collision
items.meaningCN: 撞击后的
items.example: Post-impact fires are common in electric vehicles.
items.exampleCN: 电动车在撞击后起火很常见。

items.meaning: involving strong forces or producing strong effects
items.meaningCN: 高冲击的；高强度的（复合形容词）
items.example: Runners need high-impact shoes for road training.
items.exampleCN: 跑者进行公路训练需要高缓冲冲击的鞋。

latinEntries.meaning: to push into, drive into, strike against

definition_zh: 实施；执行；贯彻；工具；器具
definition_en: to put a plan, decision, or system into effect, or a tool or piece of equipment used for a particular job
core_image: 把图纸上的空想填实，让它真正落在手上、能运作起来
scene: The project manager holds up the schedule: We have the plan; now we must implement it before the rains come.
sceneCN: 这里 implement 是「实施、执行」（第 1 个义项：把计划落到实处）；句意：计划已经有了，现在必须在雨季到来前把它实施。图中可辨识物件：甘特图、安全帽、日历。

pos.zh: 实施；执行；贯彻；使生效
工具；器具；手段

derivatives.zh: 作为工具或手段的（较少用）

senses.title: To carry out a plan or decision
senses.titleCN: 落实计划：把决定做出来
senses.definition: to take a plan, decision, or policy and put it into action
senses.definitionCN: 把计划、决定或政策付诸行动
senses.example: The city will implement the housing plan next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市将在明年春天实施住房计划。
senses.why: Latin implere means 'to fill up, fulfil'. To implement a plan is to fill the empty space between paper and reality until the plan is full and complete.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 implere 意为“填满、完成”。implement 一项计划，就是把纸面与现实之间那段空白填满，直到计划完整落地。

senses.title: To put something into practice
senses.titleCN: 付诸实践：让方法真正运转
senses.definition: to begin using a method, system, or idea in real situations
senses.definitionCN: 开始在真实情境中使用某种方法、系统或想法
senses.example: The school implemented a new way of teaching reading.
senses.exampleCN: 学校推行了一种新的阅读教学法。
senses.why: A method is only a shape until it is used. Implementation is the step where the shape acquires users, materials and daily routine.
senses.whyCN: 一种方法在被使用之前只是一个形状。implementation 就是让这个形状获得使用者、材料与日常流程的那一步。

senses.title: To fulfil an obligation or promise
senses.titleCN: 履行承诺：把应许做完
senses.definition: to carry out a promise, duty, or legal requirement fully
senses.definitionCN: 完整地履行承诺、义务或法律要求
senses.example: The company failed to implement the terms of the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 公司未能履行协议条款。
senses.why: The old noun meant a 'filling up', especially a payment that completed what was owed. To implement a duty is to fill the debt until nothing is missing.
senses.whyCN: 旧名词义是“填满”，尤指补足欠款的支付。implement 一项义务，就是把欠下的部分补齐，直到一无所缺。

senses.title: A tool for work
senses.titleCN: 工具：干活用的器物
senses.definition: a tool, utensil, or piece of equipment used to do a particular job
senses.definitionCN: 用于完成特定工作的工具、器具或设备
senses.example: The shed is full of farm implements.
senses.exampleCN: 棚子里堆满了农具。
senses.why: The noun's modern sense grows from 'that which fills a need'. A tool is whatever supplies the missing capacity of the hand, so it was called an implement.
senses.whyCN: 名词的现代义由“填补需要之物”发展而来。工具正是补上手的不足之处的东西，因此被称为 implement。

senses.title: A means to an end
senses.titleCN: 手段：达成目的的中介
senses.definition: a person, method, or device used as a means of achieving something
senses.definitionCN: 被用作达成某事的途径的人、方法或装置
senses.example: Language is the chief implement of thought.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是思维的主要工具。
senses.why: A tool need not be physical. Anything that fills the gap between intention and result can serve as an implement, including words and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 工具不必是实物。任何填补意图与结果之间缺口的东西都能充当 implement，包括语言与制度。

senses.title: Implements of a trade: equipment
senses.titleCN: 行业器具：一整套装备
senses.definition: the set of tools and equipment needed for a profession or activity
senses.definitionCN: 某种职业或活动所需的一整套工具与装备
senses.example: The surgeon laid out her implements on a sterile cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生把器械摆在一块无菌布上。
senses.why: In the plural, the word gathers many single tools into one working set. Each item fills a particular need, and together they fill the whole task.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式把许多单一工具聚成一套工作装备。每一件填补一种需要，合起来则填满整个任务。

senses.title: To build a system into operation
senses.titleCN: 落地系统：把方案装成可运行的东西
senses.definition: in computing and engineering, to build and activate a designed system or feature
senses.definitionCN: 在计算与工程领域，把设计好的系统或功能建成并启用
senses.example: The team implemented the login feature in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在两天内实现了登录功能。
senses.why: A specification is a drawing; code is the material. Implementing fills the drawing with working parts until the system can actually run.
senses.whyCN: 规格说明是一张图纸，代码是材料。implement 就是用可运转的部件把图纸填满，直到系统真的能跑起来。

senses.title: To give practical effect to a principle
senses.titleCN: 让原则生效：把抽象变成现实
senses.definition: to translate an abstract principle or right into concrete practice
senses.definitionCN: 把抽象原则或权利转化为具体实践
senses.example: The court's ruling was implemented through local regulations.
senses.exampleCN: 法院的裁决通过地方性法规得到落实。
senses.why: A principle has no hands. Implementation lends it hands by attaching it to procedures, budgets, and officials who must act.
senses.whyCN: 原则没有手。implementation 给它安上手，把它接到程序、预算和必须行动的公职人员身上。

senses.title: Historical: a filling-up payment
senses.titleCN: 历史义：补足欠额的支付
senses.definition: in 15c. legal use, a supplementary payment that completed what was owed
senses.definitionCN: 15 世纪法律用语中，补足所欠款项的追加支付
senses.example: The final implement settled the balance of the debt.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一笔补足款结清了债务余额。
senses.why: This is the sense from which all the others descend. Something was missing, and the implement was the amount that filled the gap completely.
senses.whyCN: 这是其余所有义项所由来的本义。某处有缺口，而 implement 就是把它彻底填满的那个数额。

intro.en: Implement is built on Latin plere 'to fill', not on ponere 'to place'. That is the clean line between implement and impose, even though both begin with im-. Dates and the exact path from 'payment' to 'tool' are approximate.
intro.cn: implement 建立在拉丁语 plere“填满”之上，而不是 ponere“放置”之上。这正是 implement 与 impose 之间清晰的分界，尽管两者都以 im- 开头。具体年代以及从“补款”到“工具”的语义路径只是大致推测。

items.en: The noun is first recorded as 'supplementary payment, amount needed to complete repayment', from Late Latin implementem 'a filling up'.
items.cn: 名词最早记录为“追加支付、补足偿还所需的金额”，来自晚期拉丁语 implementem“填满之物”。

items.en: Latin implere 'to fill, fill up, make full; fulfil, satisfy' is in- 'into' + plere 'to fill', from PIE *pele- 'to fill'. The root is about fullness, not position.
items.cn: 拉丁语 implere“装满、使满；履行、满足”由 in-“进入”+ plere“填满”构成，后者来自原始印欧语 *pele-“装满”。这个词根讲的是“满”，不是“位置”。

items.en: The sense 'workman's tool, utensil of a trade' appears. The link is 'whatever may supply a want, that which fills up a need' — a tool completes a missing capacity.
items.cn: “工匠工具、行业器具”义出现。联系点是“任何能补上匮乏之物、填满需要之物”——工具补上了缺失的能力。

items.en: The verb 'to complete, perform, carry into effect' appears, chiefly in Scottish English, where the noun was a legal term for 'fulfilment'.
items.cn: 动词“完成、执行、付诸实施”出现，主要见于苏格兰英语；在那里名词是表示“履行”的法律术语。

items.en: Implementation is recorded. The modern administrative phrase 'implement a policy' belongs to the 20th century.
items.cn: implementation 被记录。现代行政短语 implement a policy 属于 20 世纪。

items.en: Impose goes back to ponere 'place' (through Old French poser), while implement goes back to plere 'fill'. Same prefix, different root: one puts a burden on, the other fills a gap.
items.cn: impose 回溯到 ponere“放置”（经古法语 poser），而 implement 回溯到 plere“填满”。前缀相同，词根不同：一个把负担放上去，一个把缺口填满。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the impl- shape; the near-meaning group splits execution from tools.
note.cn: 形近组共享 impl- 外形；近义组区分“执行”与“工具”。

entries.definition: a possible consequence or indirect suggestion. It comes from implicare 'to fold in', not from plere 'to fill'.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的后果或间接暗示。它来自 implicare“折进去”，而非 plere“填满”。

entries.definition: the process of putting a plan into effect. It is the noun from implement, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划付诸实施的过程。它是 implement 的名词形式，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: serving as an instrument or means. It is rare and mostly found in older technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 作为工具或手段的。它较少见，主要出现在较早的技术文献中。

entries.definition: to carry out a plan, order, or law. It stresses completing the action, often with authority behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 执行计划、命令或法律。它强调把行动做完，常带有权威色彩。

entries.definition: to make a law or rule obeyed. It stresses compulsion, while implement stresses the practical build-out.
entries.definitionCN: 使法律或规则得到遵守。它强调强制，而 implement 强调实际搭建与落实。

entries.definition: a handheld device used to do work. It is narrower and more physical than implement.
entries.definitionCN: 用于干活的手持器具。它比 implement 更窄，也更偏实物。

entries.definition: a machine or piece of equipment made for a purpose. It usually suggests something engineered rather than a simple hand tool.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的制造的机器或装置。它通常暗示经过工程设计的物件，而非简单手工工具。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases; the point is to keep plere 'fill' separate from ponere 'place'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语；重点是记住 plere“填满”与 ponere“放置”不同。

normal.en: im- 'into' + plere 'to fill': to implement is to fill the plan with working parts.
normal.cn: im-“进入”+ plere“填满”：implement 就是用可运转的部件把计划填满。

normal.en: complete and supplement share the same plere root, which is why implement once meant a payment that completed a debt.
normal.cn: complete 与 supplement 共享同一个 plere 词根，这正是 implement 曾表示“补足欠款”的原因。

normal.en: An implement is whatever fills a need. That is why a hoe, a scalpel and a line of code can all be implements.
normal.cn: implement 就是填补需要之物。因此锄头、手术刀和一行代码都可以是 implement。

normal.en: Implementation is the noun for the gap-closing step between decision and result.
normal.cn: implementation 是“决定”与“结果”之间那步填补工作的名词。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with impose: impose puts a burden on, implement fills the empty space.
normal.cn: 不要与 impose 混淆：impose 把负担放上去，implement 把空处填满。

abstract.en: Picture a plaster mould and its hollow: implementation is the pouring that makes the hollow solid.
abstract.cn: 想象石膏模具与其中的空腔：implementation 就是让空腔变成实体的那一次浇筑。

abstract.en: A plan is a promise with no body. Implementation gives it a body of hours, money, and hands.
abstract.cn: 计划是一句没有身体的承诺。implementation 用时间、金钱和人力给它一个身体。

abstract.en: Every tool is an answer to a missing body part: the hammer is a harder fist, the plough is a sharper finger.
abstract.cn: 每一件工具都是对身体缺失部分的回答：锤子是更硬的拳头，犁是更尖的手指。

examples.en: The government promised to implement the report's recommendations within a year.
examples.cn: 政府承诺在一年内落实报告的建议。

examples.en: Old farm implements hang on the wall of the museum.
examples.cn: 博物馆墙上挂着旧时的农具。

examples.en: Before you implement the change, test it on one small team.
examples.cn: 在推行这项变革之前，先在一个小团队里试点。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一木盆里门特”——一木盆的工具摆在门口特别显眼 → implement 工具、实施

root: 源自拉丁语 implere“装满、履行”，由 in-“进入”+ plere“填满”构成；名词先指“补足欠款”，后指“补上所需之物”，即工具，再引申为“把计划填实、执行”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of implement, all built on 'filling a gap': a payment fills a debt, a tool fills a missing capacity, and implementation fills the space between plan and reality.
sensesIntro.cn: implement 的九个义项都建立在“填补缺口”上：一笔款填平债务，一件工具补上缺失的能力，而实施则填满计划与现实之间的空白。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty space is filled until the thing is complete and can work.
core.cn: 核心意象：把空处填满，直到事情完整、可以运转。

branches.en: PAYMENT: the oldest branch, where money fills the remaining debt.
branches.cn: 支付：最古老的一支，用钱填平剩余的欠款。

branches.en: TOOLS: a device fills a missing capacity; a method or a person can fill it too.
branches.cn: 工具：装置补上缺失的能力；方法或人也可以补上。

branches.en: ACTION: a plan is filled with procedures and routines until it runs.
branches.cn: 行动：用程序与日常流程把计划填满，直到它运转起来。

branches.en: OBLIGATION AND PRINCIPLE: a duty or a right is empty until practice fills it.
branches.cn: 义务与原则：义务或权利在实践填满它之前都是空的。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: a specification is filled with working code and hardware.
branches.cn: 系统：用可运行的代码与硬件把规格说明填满。

intro.en: Implement uses the Latin prefix in- (assimilated to im-) plus plere 'to fill'. English then adds -ation, -er, -al and re-.
intro.cn: implement 使用拉丁前缀 in-（同化为 im-）加 plere“填满”。英语随后加上 -ation、-er、-al 与 re-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is plere 'fill' and implere 'fill up'. Relatives include complete, supplement, supply and expletive, all built on the same 'fill' root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 plere“填满”与 implere“装满”。同族词包括 complete、supplement、supply、expletive，它们都建立在同一个“填满”词根上。

items.meaning: the process of putting a plan or system into effect
items.meaningCN: 实施；落实（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Implementation of the new rules begins in June.
items.exampleCN: 新规则的实施从六月开始。

items.meaning: a person or organization that carries something out
items.meaningCN: 实施者；执行者
items.example: The implementer of the reform was a small agency.
items.exampleCN: 这项改革的实施者是一个小机构。

items.meaning: able to be put into practice
items.meaningCN: 可实施的；可执行的（-able 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: The proposal is ambitious but implementable.
items.exampleCN: 这个提案雄心不小，但可以实施。

items.meaning: serving as a means or instrument
items.meaningCN: 作为工具或手段的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The implemental value of the treaty was limited.
items.exampleCN: 这项条约作为工具的价值有限。

items.meaning: to put something into effect again or in a new way
items.meaningCN: 重新实施；以新方式再次落实
items.example: The team had to reimplement the schedule after the delay.
items.exampleCN: 延误之后，团队不得不重新落实进度安排。

items.meaning: to fill or pervade (rare, 19c.)
items.meaningCN: 充满；渗透（罕见，19 世纪用语）
items.example: The old text speaks of light impleting the room.
items.exampleCN: 那篇旧文说到光充满了房间。

items.meaning: to make whole or finished
items.meaningCN: 使完整；完成（com- 表示“完全”）
items.example: One more chapter will complete the book.
items.exampleCN: 再写一章就能完成这本书。

items.meaning: something added to fill a lack
items.meaningCN: 补充物；增补（sub- 表示“从下方补上”）
items.example: She takes a vitamin supplement in winter.
items.exampleCN: 她在冬天服用维生素补充剂。

latinEntries.meaning: a filling up, that which fills

definition_zh: 含义；暗示；可能的结果；牵连；逻辑蕴含
definition_en: something suggested indirectly, a likely consequence of an action or decision, or a logical relation in which one statement follows from another
core_image: 一句话或一件事折进去的部分：没摊开，却已经包在里面
scene: The reporter presses the minister: You must explain the implications of this decision for rural hospitals.
sceneCN: 这里 implication 是「（决定带来的）可能后果」（第 1 个义项：连带的结果）；句意：你必须解释这个决定对乡村医院意味着什么。图中可辨识物件：话筒、文件、乡村医院照片。

pos.zh: 含义；暗示；结果；牵连；蕴含

collocations.zh: 这项研究的意义（或影响）

senses.title: A likely consequence
senses.titleCN: 可能后果：连带出来的结果
senses.definition: a possible result or effect that follows from an action, decision, or event
senses.definitionCN: 由某个行动、决定或事件带来的可能结果或作用
senses.example: The ruling has serious implications for employers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决对雇主有严重后果。
senses.why: Implication is a folding-in. A decision folds consequences into the future the way a sheet folds other sheets inside it; they are not stated, but they travel with it.
senses.whyCN: implication 是一种“折进去”。一个决定把后果折进未来，就像一张纸把别的纸包在里面；后果没有被说出来，却随它一起走。

senses.title: An indirect suggestion
senses.titleCN: 暗示：没有明说的意思
senses.definition: something that is suggested or hinted at without being stated directly
senses.definitionCN: 没有直接说出、却被提示或暗示的内容
senses.example: The implication was that the manager had known all along.
senses.exampleCN: 言外之意是经理一直都知道。
senses.why: The literal Latin sense is 'entanglement'. A hint entangles the hearer in a meaning that is never laid out in words, so the message arrives folded.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁本义是“缠绕”。暗示把听者缠进一个从未用言语铺开的意义里，于是信息是折着到达的。

senses.title: The act of implying
senses.titleCN: 暗示行为：让意思含而不露
senses.definition: the act of conveying a meaning indirectly rather than stating it
senses.definitionCN: 以间接方式传达意义而非直接陈述的行为
senses.example: His implication of guilt was subtle but unmistakable.
senses.exampleCN: 他对罪责的暗示很微妙，却不容错认。
senses.why: Here the word names the action rather than the content. The speaker folds a claim into a remark and leaves the listener to unfold it.
senses.whyCN: 这里指称的是行为而不是内容。说话者把一个断言折进一句话里，让听者自己去展开。

senses.title: Logical implication: if P then Q
senses.titleCN: 逻辑蕴含：若 P 则 Q
senses.definition: the relation between two propositions such that if the first is true, the second must be true
senses.definitionCN: 两个命题之间的关系：若第一个为真，第二个必为真
senses.example: The proof rests on the implication that every even number has a successor.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明依赖于“每个偶数都有后继”这一蕴含关系。
senses.why: In logic, one statement is folded into another by necessity: to accept the premise is already to accept the consequence. Nothing is hidden; the connection is exact.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑中，一个陈述因必然性而被折进另一个陈述：接受前提，就已经接受了结论。这里没有隐藏，联系是精确的。

senses.title: Involvement in a crime or scandal
senses.titleCN: 牵连：被卷入某事
senses.definition: the fact of being involved in something, especially a crime or scandal
senses.definitionCN: 被卷入某事的事实，尤指犯罪或丑闻
senses.example: His implication in the fraud ended his career.
senses.exampleCN: 他牵涉这起欺诈案，终结了他的职业生涯。
senses.why: The fold becomes a net. A person named in a case is entangled in it, whether or not they acted, and the word records that entanglement.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“折”变成了“网”。被案件点名的人就被缠在其中，不论他是否真的行动，而这个词记录的正是这种缠绕。

senses.title: A necessary consequence of a claim
senses.titleCN: 必然推论：主张所带的包袱
senses.definition: a consequence that a theory, statement, or belief cannot avoid
senses.definitionCN: 一种理论、陈述或信念无法回避的后果
senses.example: The implication of his argument is that no one can be trusted.
senses.exampleCN: 他的论点隐含的结论是：没有人可信。
senses.why: If you hold one end of a folded sheet, the rest comes with it. A claim carries its unavoidable consequences in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 握住折好的纸的一端，其余部分就跟着来。一个主张也以同样的方式带着它无法回避的推论。

senses.title: Linguistic entailment
senses.titleCN: 语义蕴含：词义带出的内容
senses.definition: in linguistics, what follows necessarily from the meaning of a word or sentence
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中，由词或句子的意义必然带出的内容
senses.example: The implication of 'bachelor' includes 'unmarried'.
senses.exampleCN: bachelor 的语义蕴含包括“未婚”。
senses.why: Meaning can be folded inside meaning. Saying one thing entails another without the speaker ever mentioning it, and semantics names that entailment an implication.
senses.whyCN: 意义可以折在意义里。说出一件事就带出另一件事，而说话者从未提及后者；语义学把这种带出称为 implication。

senses.title: Connotation: the colour of a word
senses.titleCN: 言外色彩：词语附带的意味
senses.definition: an idea or feeling that a word suggests beyond its literal meaning
senses.definitionCN: 词语在字面意义之外所暗示的观念或感觉
senses.example: The word 'cheap' carries an implication of poor quality.
senses.exampleCN: cheap 这个词带有质量低劣的隐含意味。
senses.why: A word is never only its definition. Social attitudes are folded into it, and hearers unfold them without effort.
senses.whyCN: 一个词从来不只是它的定义。社会态度被折进词里，听者不费力就能展开它们。

senses.title: Archaic: an entanglement
senses.titleCN: 古义：缠绕、交织
senses.definition: the literal early sense of being twisted or folded together
senses.definitionCN: 早期字面义：被缠绕或折叠在一起
senses.example: In the old medical text, the implication of fibres was thought to cause pain.
senses.exampleCN: 在那本旧医学文献里，纤维的缠绕被认为会引起疼痛。
senses.why: Early 15c. 'action of entangling' came straight from Latin implicatio 'an interweaving'. Every modern sense is a descendant of this physical fold.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪早期的“缠绕行为”直接来自拉丁语 implicatio“交织”。所有现代义项都是这个物理折叠的后代。

intro.en: Implication is the noun of implicare 'to fold in'. The root plicare 'to fold' is what separates it from implement (plere 'to fill') and impose (ponere 'to place').
intro.cn: implication 是 implicare“折进去”的名词形式。词根 plicare“折叠”正是它与 implement（plere“填满”）和 impose（ponere“放置”）的分界。

items.en: First recorded as 'action of entangling', a direct noun of action from Latin implicatio.
items.cn: 最早记录为“缠绕的行为”，是拉丁语 implicatio 的直接动作名词。

items.en: Implicatio meant 'an interweaving, an entanglement', from the past-participle stem of implicare 'involve, entangle, embrace, connect closely'.
items.cn: implicatio 意为“交织、缠绕”，来自 implicare“卷入、缠住、拥抱、紧密连接”的过去分词词干。

items.en: Implicare is in- 'into' + plicare 'to fold', reconstructed from PIE *plek- 'to plait'. A fold is literally something turned back into itself, which is why the word came to mean 'involve'.
items.cn: implicare 由 in-“进入”+ plicare“折叠”构成，可重构自原始印欧语 *plek-“编织”。折叠就是某物被翻回自身，这正是该词后来表示“卷入”的原因。

items.en: The sense 'that which is implied but not expressed, an inference drawn from what is observed' is recorded.
items.cn: “被暗示而未明说之物、从观察中得出的推论”这一义项被记录。

items.en: Logic and linguistics give the word precise technical senses: material implication between propositions, and implicature as the pragmatic cousin of implication.
items.cn: 逻辑学与语言学赋予该词精确的技术义：命题之间的实质蕴含，以及作为语用学近亲的 implicature（会话含义）。

items.en: The plural implications is now the ordinary way to talk about the knock-on effects of a decision. The older 'entanglement' sense survives only in histories and dictionaries.
items.cn: 复数 implications 如今是谈论“决定连带后果”的普通说法。较古的“缠绕”义只保存在历史叙述与词典中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the implic- shape; the near-meaning group separates consequence from hinted meaning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 implic- 外形；近义组区分“后果”与“暗示之义”。

entries.definition: to show that someone is involved in a crime. It is the verb form that stresses entanglement, not consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某人卷入犯罪。它是强调“缠绕、牵连”的动词形式，而不是强调后果。

entries.definition: suggested but not stated; also complete and unquestioning, as in implicit trust. Both senses come from 'folded in'.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示而未明说的；也指完全的、不加质疑的，如 implicit trust。两个义项都来自“折在里面”。

entries.definition: a meaning suggested by a speaker in context rather than encoded in the words themselves. It is the pragmatic relative of implication.
entries.definitionCN: 说话者在语境中暗示、而非词语本身编码的意义。它是 implication 在语用学中的近亲。

entries.definition: a result that follows from an action. It is neutral about whether the result is expected, while implication suggests a result to be worked out.
entries.definitionCN: 由行动带来的结果。它不暗示结果是否可预期，而 implication 暗示结果需要被推想出来。

entries.definition: an idea put forward indirectly or tentatively. It is lighter and more deliberate than implication.
entries.definitionCN: 间接或试探性提出的想法。它比 implication 更轻，也更刻意。

entries.definition: a conclusion drawn from evidence. It is what the hearer does; an implication is what the evidence or words carry.
entries.definitionCN: 从证据得出的结论。它是听者所做的推理；implication 则是证据或话语所携带的内容。

entries.definition: a complex consequence that branches out from an action. It is usually heavier and more formal than implication.
entries.definitionCN: 由行动分叉出来的复杂后果。它通常比 implication 更沉重、更正式。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases; keep plicare 'fold' separate from plere 'fill' and ponere 'place'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语；记住 plicare“折叠”不同于 plere“填满”和 ponere“放置”。

normal.en: im- 'into' + plicare 'to fold': an implication is a meaning folded inside a statement.
normal.cn: im-“进入”+ plicare“折叠”：implication 就是折进一句话里的意义。

normal.en: Implication and explicit are opposites built on the same fold: one is folded in, the other is folded out.
normal.cn: implication 与 explicit 是建立在同一个“折”上的反义对：一个折在里面，一个摊在外面。

normal.en: The phrase by implication means 'by what is folded in, not by what is said'.
normal.cn: by implication 意为“凭折在里面的意思，而不是凭说出来的话”。

normal.en: Implications usually appears in the plural because one decision folds many consequences inside it.
normal.cn: implications 常用复数，因为一个决定会把许多后果折在里面。

normal.en: Implicate and implicit share the root: to implicate is to fold a person into a case; implicit means folded in and left unsaid.
normal.cn: implicate 与 implicit 共享词根：implicate 是把人折进案件里；implicit 是折在里面、没有说出。

abstract.en: Picture a letter folded small enough to fit in a pocket: the whole message is there, but you must open it to read it.
abstract.cn: 想象一封折得很小、能放进衣袋的信：整段信息都在里面，但你必须打开才能读到。

abstract.en: Implication is the shadow cast by a statement. You cannot see the object, but the shape of the shadow tells you where it stands.
abstract.cn: implication 是一个陈述投下的影子。你看不见物体，但影子的形状告诉你它立在哪里。

abstract.en: A decision is a seed; its implications are the branches that will grow from it, some of them out of sight.
abstract.cn: 决定是一粒种子；它的 implications 是从中长出的枝条，其中一些还在视野之外。

examples.en: Nobody discussed the budget implications of the new programme.
examples.cn: 没有人讨论这个新项目对预算的影响。

examples.en: By implication, the report blames the local council.
examples.cn: 言外之意，这份报告把责任归给了地方议会。

examples.en: The logical implication runs from the premise to its conclusion.
examples.cn: 逻辑蕴含从前提指向结论。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬不理开心”——硬把不开心的事折起来藏进话里 → implication 暗示、隐含的后果

root: 源自拉丁语 implicatio“交织、缠绕”，来自 implicare“折进去、卷入”，由 in-“进入”+ plicare“折叠”构成，核心是“把意思或后果折进话里”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of implication, all built on one fold: something is inside a statement or decision without being laid open. Consequence, hint, logical entailment and involvement are four ways that fold shows up.
sensesIntro.cn: implication 的九个义项都建立在同一个“折”上：某物被包在话语或决定里，却没有摊开。后果、暗示、逻辑蕴含与牵连，是这个“折”显现的四种方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet folded inward, holding more than its visible surface shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张向内折起的纸，装着比可见表面更多的东西。

branches.en: CONSEQUENCE: what a decision or claim folds into the future, whether or not anyone says it.
branches.cn: 后果：决定或主张折进未来的部分，不论有没有人说出口。

branches.en: UNSTATED MEANING: hints, acts of hinting, and the colour a word carries all stay folded inside speech.
branches.cn: 未说之义：暗示、暗示行为，以及词语携带的色彩，都折在言语内部。

branches.en: NECESSITY: in logic and semantics the fold is exact — one truth or meaning cannot be separated from another.
branches.cn: 必然性：在逻辑与语义学中，这个折是精确的——一个真理或意义无法与另一个分开。

branches.en: ENTANGLEMENT: a person can be folded into a case, which is the oldest physical sense turned social.
branches.cn: 牵连：一个人可以被折进案件里，这是最古老的物理义转向社会层面。

branches.en: LITERAL FOLD: the 15c. 'interweaving' is the root image from which all the others unfold.
branches.cn: 字面的折：15 世纪的“交织”是所有其他义项由此展开的根意象。

intro.en: Implication is im- + plicare plus -ation. English builds the family with -ed, -ive, -ure and the negative explicit.
intro.cn: implication 是 im- + plicare 再加 -ation。英语用 -ed、-ive、-ure 以及反义的 explicit 构建词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is plicare 'to fold' and implicare 'to fold in'. The same root gives explicit, complicate, duplicate, reply and employ.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 plicare“折叠”与 implicare“折进去”。同一词根还给出 explicit、complicate、duplicate、reply、employ。

items.structure: im- + plicare → Old French emplier → English imply
items.meaning: to suggest without stating; to involve as a consequence
items.meaningCN: 暗示；意味着（不说出而带出）
items.example: The letter implies that the deal is off.
items.exampleCN: 这封信暗示交易已经告吹。

items.meaning: suggested but not expressed
items.meaningCN: 隐含的；未明说的
items.example: She made an implied threat.
items.exampleCN: 她作了一个隐含的威胁。

items.meaning: to show or suggest that someone is involved in something wrong
items.meaningCN: 使牵连；表明某人卷入某事
items.example: Two officials were implicated in the deal.
items.exampleCN: 两名官员牵涉这笔交易。

items.meaning: folded in, therefore understood without being said
items.meaningCN: 含蓄的；隐含的（折在里面，故不需明说）
items.example: There was an implicit agreement not to mention it.
items.exampleCN: 存在一种不提此事的默契。

items.meaning: tending to imply or suggest
items.meaningCN: 暗示性的；蕴含的（-ive 表示倾向）
items.example: His silence was implicative rather than empty.
items.exampleCN: 他的沉默是有含义的，而非空无一物。

items.meaning: folded out; stated fully and clearly
items.meaningCN: 摊开的；明确说出的（ex- 表示“向外”）
items.example: The rules are explicit about late fees.
items.exampleCN: 规则对滞纳金有明确规定。

items.meaning: to fold things together so that they become hard to separate
items.meaningCN: 使复杂；把东西折在一起而难以分开
items.example: Extra rules complicate the process.
items.exampleCN: 额外的规则让流程变复杂。

items.meaning: to fold into two; to make an exact copy
items.meaningCN: 折成两份；复制（du- 表示“二”）
items.example: Please duplicate this key for the tenant.
items.exampleCN: 请为租户配一把相同的钥匙。

latinEntries.meaning: to enfold, entangle, involve, connect closely
latinEntries.meaningCN: 包入、缠绕、卷入、紧密相连

definition_zh: 暗示；意味着；含有……的意思；必然牵涉
definition_en: to suggest something without saying it directly, or to have something as a necessary consequence
core_image: 把意思折进话里：听者展开才看见
scene: 她没有说“不”，只是语气停顿了一下，文件夹还半开着。 She did not say no, but her tone seemed to imply that the answer had already been settled.
sceneCN: 这里 imply 是「暗示」（第 1 个义项：不明说而让人领会）；句意：她没有说“不”，但她的语气暗示答案早已定下。

pos.zh: 暗示；意味着；含有……的意思

collocations.phrase: what do you imply by that?

senses.title: To suggest without stating
senses.titleCN: 暗示：不明说而让人领会
senses.definition: to make something understood indirectly, without putting it into explicit words
senses.definitionCN: 不把话说明白，而让人间接领会某事
senses.example: Her silence implied agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 她的沉默暗示了同意。
senses.why: Latin implicare is 'to fold in'. A meaning that is implied is folded into the sentence, present but not laid out, and the listener must unfold it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 implicare 意为“折进去”。被 imply 的意思折在句子里，存在却没有铺开，听者必须自己展开。

senses.title: To involve as a necessary consequence
senses.titleCN: 意味着：必然带出某事
senses.definition: to have something as a necessary part or result
senses.definitionCN: 必然包含某物，或必然带来某结果
senses.example: Rights imply duties.
senses.exampleCN: 权利意味着义务。
senses.why: The fold here is logical rather than rhetorical. If one thing is accepted, the other is already inside it, so no additional claim is needed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“折”是逻辑的，而不是修辞的。若接受一件事，另一件已经在它里面，因此不需要额外的断言。

senses.title: To entail in logic
senses.titleCN: 逻辑蕴含：前提带出结论
senses.definition: in logic, for a statement to entail another as a matter of necessity
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中，一个陈述必然带出另一个陈述
senses.example: The premise implies the conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 前提蕴含结论。
senses.why: This is sense 02 made exact. The connection is not a hint but a rule: whenever the premise holds, the conclusion holds.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 2 个义项的精确化。这里的联系不是暗示，而是规则：只要前提成立，结论就成立。

senses.title: To hint at in conversation
senses.titleCN: 话里带刺：言语中的暗示
senses.definition: to hint at a meaning in speech, often something the speaker does not want to say openly
senses.definitionCN: 在言语中暗示某意，常是说话者不愿明说之事
senses.example: What are you implying about my work?
senses.exampleCN: 你对我的工作到底在暗示什么？
senses.why: This sense, recorded from the 1580s, is the social use of the fold. The speaker leaves a meaning inside the remark and lets the hearer draw it out.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项自 16 世纪 80 年代有记录，是“折”的社会用法。说话者把意思留在话里，让听者自己抽出来。

senses.title: To indicate by evidence
senses.titleCN: 表明：证据指向某结论
senses.definition: to suggest something as true because of evidence, without stating it openly
senses.definitionCN: 因证据而暗示某事为真，但不直接说出
senses.example: The data imply a steady rise in temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 数据表明温度在稳步上升。
senses.why: Evidence can fold a conclusion inside itself. The researcher reads the pattern and unfolds what the numbers already contain.
senses.whyCN: 证据可以把结论折进自身。研究者读出规律，展开数字中已经包含的东西。

senses.title: Of words: to mean indirectly
senses.titleCN: 词义暗含：字面之外的意思
senses.definition: of a word or phrase, to carry a certain meaning or association beyond its explicit definition
senses.definitionCN: 指词或短语在明确定义之外带有某种含义或联想
senses.example: The term 'village' implies a small, close community.
senses.exampleCN: village 一词暗含一个小而紧密的社区。
senses.why: A word carries more than its dictionary entry. Social assumptions are folded into it, and using the word brings them along.
senses.whyCN: 一个词承载的不只是词典条目。社会预设被折进其中，使用这个词就把它们一起带来。

senses.title: Of an action: to reveal indirectly
senses.titleCN: 行为透露：不说也让人明白
senses.definition: of an action or fact, to make something known without words
senses.definitionCN: 指行为或事实不用言语就使某事为人所知
senses.example: His refusal to answer implied that he had something to hide.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒绝回答，暗示他有事隐瞒。
senses.why: A gesture can fold a statement as effectively as a sentence. What is not done becomes the visible edge of what is meant.
senses.whyCN: 一个举动可以像一句话一样把陈述折起来。未做之事成了所说之意的可见边缘。

senses.title: To suggest a hidden meaning in a text
senses.titleCN: 文本暗指：字里行间的意思
senses.definition: of a text, image, or symbol, to suggest a further meaning beyond the surface
senses.definitionCN: 指文本、图像或符号在表层之外暗示更深含义
senses.example: The ending implies that the two will meet again.
senses.exampleCN: 结局暗示两人还会再见。
senses.why: A story can leave a meaning folded in its last line. The reader completes it, which is why implied endings feel stronger than stated ones.
senses.whyCN: 故事可以把一个意思折在最后一行里。读者来完成它，这正是隐含的结局比明说的结局更有力的原因。

senses.title: Archaic: to enfold or entangle
senses.titleCN: 古义：包裹、缠绕
senses.definition: the original 14c. sense of wrapping or entangling something physically
senses.definitionCN: 14 世纪最初表示物理上包裹或缠绕某物的义项
senses.example: In the old poem, mist implies the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 在那首古诗里，雾把群山包裹起来。
senses.why: Late 14c. implien meant 'to enfold, enwrap, entangle'. The modern meanings are all metaphors of this physical wrapping.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪晚期的 implien 意为“包裹、缠住”。所有现代义项都是这个物理包裹的比喻。

intro.en: Imply comes from Latin implicare 'to fold in', through Old French emplier. Its root plicare 'to fold' is unrelated to implement's plere 'to fill'. The often-confused pair imply and infer is explained by direction: the speaker folds a meaning in, the hearer carries a conclusion out.
intro.cn: imply 经古法语 emplier 来自拉丁语 implicare“折进去”。其词根 plicare“折叠”与 implement 的 plere“填满”毫无关系。常被混淆的 imply 与 infer 可由方向区分：说话者把意思折进去，听者把结论带出来。

items.en: Recorded as implien, emplien, 'to enfold, enwrap, entangle' — the classical Latin sense, not yet the modern 'suggest'.
items.cn: 记录为 implien、emplien，意为“包裹、缠绕、缠住”——这是拉丁语古典义，还不是现代的“暗示”。

items.en: Old French emplier 'to enfold' carried the Latin verb into English. The modern spelling imply reflects the Latin in- rather than the French en-.
items.cn: 古法语 emplier“包裹”把这个拉丁动词带进英语。现代拼写 imply 反映的是拉丁语 in-，而不是法语 en-。

items.en: Implicare 'involve, enfold, entangle' is in- 'into' + plicare 'to fold', from PIE *plek- 'to plait'. A fold turns a surface back into itself, so 'involve' and 'entangle' are the same gesture.
items.cn: implicare“卷入、包住、缠住”由 in-“进入”+ plicare“折叠”构成，后者来自原始印欧语 *plek-“编织”。折叠把表面翻回自身，因此“卷入”与“缠住”是同一个动作。

items.en: The sense 'to involve something unstated as a logical consequence' is recorded. This is the sense behind 'rights imply duties'.
items.cn: “作为逻辑后果而包含未明说之物”的义项被记录。这就是 rights imply duties 背后的义项。

items.en: The conversational sense 'to hint at' appears. The speaker now folds a meaning into a remark on purpose.
items.cn: 会话中的“暗示”义出现。此时说话者是有意把意思折进一句话里。

items.en: The Century Dictionary put it plainly: a speaker implies, a hearer infers. An action implies ability or preparation, but it involves consequences.
items.cn: 《世纪词典》说得直白：说话者 implies，听者 infers。一个行为 implies 能力或准备，但它 involves 后果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the impl- shape but not always the root; the near-meaning group turns on direction and strength.
note.cn: 形近组共享 impl- 外形，但词根并不总相同；近义组的关键是方向与强度。

entries.definition: to show that someone is involved in something wrong. It is the person-directed verb from the same fold.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某人卷入某事（通常指错事）。它是同一“折”词根下指向人的动词。

entries.definition: suggested but not stated. It describes the state of being folded in, while imply describes the act.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示而未明说的。它描述“折在里面”的状态，而 imply 描述“折”的动作。

entries.definition: the third-person singular of imply. The -s ending is grammar, not a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: imply 的第三人称单数形式。-s 只是语法词尾，不是另一个词。

entries.definition: to draw a conclusion from evidence. The hearer infers what the speaker implies; ferre means 'carry', so the conclusion is carried out.
entries.definitionCN: 从证据得出推论。说话者 imply，听者 infer；ferre 意为“携带”，结论是被带出来的。

entries.definition: to put an idea into someone's mind, often gently. It is weaker and less binding than imply.
entries.definitionCN: 把想法放进别人脑中，通常较温和。它比 imply 更弱，约束力也更小。

entries.definition: to involve something as a necessary consequence, especially a cost or obligation. It is more formal and more limited than imply.
entries.definitionCN: 必然带来某后果，尤指代价或义务。它比 imply 更正式，适用范围也更窄。

entries.definition: to hint at something delicately or indirectly. It is softer and more literary than imply.
entries.definitionCN: 委婉、间接地暗示。它比 imply 更柔和，也更书面。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases. The key contrast is fold (plicare) versus carry (ferre).
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语。关键对比是“折”（plicare）与“带”（ferre）。

normal.en: im- 'into' + plicare 'fold': to imply is to put a meaning inside the sentence without unfolding it.
normal.cn: im-“进入”+ plicare“折叠”：imply 就是把意思放进句子里而不摊开。

normal.en: The phrase as the name implies means 'as the name already contains'.
normal.cn: as the name implies 意为“正如名字本身已经包含的那样”。

normal.en: Imply and infer face opposite ways: the speaker folds in, the listener carries out.
normal.cn: imply 与 infer 方向相反：说话者折进去，听者带出来。

normal.en: Implication and implicit are the noun and adjective of the same fold; explicit is its unfolded opposite.
normal.cn: implication 与 implicit 是同一个“折”的名词与形容词；explicit 则是摊开的反面。

normal.en: Silence can imply consent because the missing words are treated as folded into the situation.
normal.cn: 沉默可以 imply 同意，因为缺失的话被当作折进了情境之中。

abstract.en: Think of a note slipped inside a book: the words are there the whole time, but only the reader who opens the page finds them.
abstract.cn: 想象夹在书里的一张纸条：字一直在那里，但只有翻开那页的读者才会发现。

abstract.en: Imply is an invitation, not a statement. It leaves a space exactly the size of the listener's understanding.
abstract.cn: imply 是邀请，不是陈述。它留下的空白，正好等于听者的理解力。

abstract.en: A logical implication has no air in it: the conclusion is packed tight inside the premise, with nothing left to guess.
abstract.cn: 逻辑蕴含里没有空气：结论被紧紧压进前提，不留任何猜测余地。

examples.en: Are you implying that I made the mistake?
examples.cn: 你是在暗示这个错误是我犯的吗？

examples.en: A high price does not necessarily imply high quality.
examples.cn: 高价并不必然意味着高质量。

examples.en: The quiet streets implied that most people had already left.
examples.cn: 安静的街道说明大多数人已经离开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬不来”——嘴上说硬不来，其实话里已经折进了“会来”的意思 → imply 暗示

root: 源自拉丁语 implicare“折进去、卷入”，由 in-“进入”+ plicare“折叠”构成；经古法语 emplier 于 14 世纪晚期进入英语，核心是“把意思含在话里”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of imply, all built on folding a meaning inward. A speaker folds, a text folds, evidence folds, and logic folds with perfect tightness.
sensesIntro.cn: imply 的九个义项都建立在“把意思向内折”上。说话者在折，文本在折，证据在折，逻辑则折得严丝合缝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a meaning folded inside a sentence, visible only when someone unfolds it.
core.cn: 核心意象：折进句子里的意思，只有被展开时才可见。

branches.en: SPEECH: the speaker folds an intention into words and leaves the hearer to open it.
branches.cn: 言语：说话者把意图折进话里，让听者自己去打开。

branches.en: NECESSITY: a premise contains its conclusion; nothing is hidden, only tightly folded.
branches.cn: 必然：前提包含着结论；没有隐藏，只是折得很紧。

branches.en: EVIDENCE AND ACTION: data, gestures and endings all carry meanings they never state.
branches.cn: 证据与行为：数据、举动与结局都携带着从未说出的意思。

branches.en: WORDS: a term folds social assumptions into its dictionary definition.
branches.cn: 词语：一个词把社会预设折进它的词典定义里。

branches.en: LITERAL WRAP: the original physical enfolding, from which every modern sense is borrowed.
branches.cn: 字面包裹：最初的物理包裹，所有现代义项都借自它。

intro.en: Imply is im- + plicare. English adds -ed, -ing, -ation and -ative, and builds the noun implication.
intro.cn: imply 是 im- + plicare。英语加上 -ed、-ing、-ation、-ative，并构成名词 implication。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is plicare 'to fold' and implicare 'to fold in'. Its English relatives include explicit, complicate, duplicate, reply and employ.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 plicare“折叠”与 implicare“折进去”。英语同族词包括 explicit、complicate、duplicate、reply、employ。

items.meaning: something implied; a likely consequence
items.meaningCN: 暗示之义；可能的后果（-ation 构成名词）
items.example: The implications of the vote are still unclear.
items.exampleCN: 这次投票的影响仍不清楚。

items.meaning: understood without being said
items.meaningCN: 隐含的；默示的
items.example: There was an implied promise in his words.
items.exampleCN: 他的话里有一个隐含的承诺。

items.meaning: suggesting indirectly while speaking
items.meaningCN: 正在暗示（现在分词）
items.example: She avoided implying that anyone was to blame.
items.exampleCN: 她避免暗示任何人该受责备。

items.meaning: carrying an implied meaning
items.meaningCN: 带有暗示意味的；蕴含的
items.example: A raised eyebrow can be implicative.
items.exampleCN: 挑一下眉也可以带出暗示。

items.meaning: folded in; understood but not stated
items.meaningCN: 含蓄的；隐含的
items.example: Implicit in the plan is a rise in taxes.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划隐含着增税。

items.meaning: unfolded; stated plainly
items.meaningCN: 明确的；摊开说明的
items.example: The contract is explicit about payment dates.
items.exampleCN: 合同对付款日期有明确规定。

items.meaning: to fold together; to make difficult
items.meaningCN: 使复杂；把东西折到一起而难以理清
items.example: New evidence complicated the case.
items.exampleCN: 新证据让案件变复杂了。

items.meaning: to use or engage; originally 'to enfold in a task'
items.meaningCN: 雇用；使用（原义“把某人卷入一项任务”）
items.example: The firm employs forty people.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司雇用了四十人。

definition_zh: 强加；施加（税、罚款、规定）；征收；打扰，勉强他人
definition_en: to officially force a rule, tax, or punishment on people, to make someone accept something, or to expect too much of someone
core_image: 把一件重物按到别人身上，让对方不得不承受
scene: The council imposed a new levy on every empty apartment in the district.
sceneCN: 这里 impose 是「强制征收」（第 1 个义项：以官方权力施加负担）；句意：议会对该区每套空置公寓强制征收了一项新税。图中可辨识物件：公告栏、税单、空置公寓。

pos.zh: 强加；施加；征收；把……落在某人身上
打扰；勉强他人（与 on／upon 连用）

collocations.zh: 打扰某人的款待；占别人便宜

derivatives.zh: 气势宏伟的；使人印象深刻的
叠加；把……放在另一物之上

senses.title: To force a rule, tax, or penalty officially
senses.titleCN: 官方强制施加：征税、禁令、处罚
senses.definition: to officially force a law, tax, punishment, or restriction on people
senses.definitionCN: 以官方权力把法律、税收、处罚或限制加在人们身上
senses.example: The government imposed a tax on imported cars.
senses.exampleCN: 政府对进口汽车征收了税。
senses.why: Latin imponere is in- 'upon' + ponere 'to place'. The image is a burden physically placed on someone's back; official power is what keeps it there.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 imponere 由 in-“在……之上”+ ponere“放置”构成。意象是一件重物被实实放在某人背上；官方权力则让它一直压着。

senses.title: To force an idea or belief on others
senses.titleCN: 把观念强加于人
senses.definition: to make others accept a belief, value, or way of doing things, whether they want it or not
senses.definitionCN: 使他人接受某种信念、价值或做事方式，不论其是否愿意
senses.example: Parents should not impose their own tastes on their children.
senses.exampleCN: 父母不该把自己的品味强加给孩子。
senses.why: The burden is now mental. One person's preference is laid on another's mind as if it were an object that could be handed over.
senses.whyCN: 这里的负担是心理上的。一个人的偏好被放到另一个人的心上，仿佛它是一件可以递过去的物件。

senses.title: To take advantage of someone
senses.titleCN: 占便宜：过度麻烦别人
senses.definition: to expect too much from someone or inconvenience them, especially in the phrase impose on
senses.definitionCN: 对别人要求过多或给其添麻烦，尤用于短语 impose on
senses.example: I hope I am not imposing on you by staying another night.
senses.exampleCN: 我希望再多住一晚不会太打扰你。
senses.why: Here the placed weight is hospitality itself. The guest puts more on the host than was offered, and the phrase records the extra load.
senses.whyCN: 这里被放上去的重量是“款待”本身。客人加在主人身上的，超过了主人所给出的，这个短语记录的正是那份额外负担。

senses.title: To place something physically on
senses.titleCN: 把某物放在上面：实物的覆压
senses.definition: to lay or place something on something else, often with force or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放或压在另一物之上，常带力量或仪式意味
senses.example: The bishop imposed his hands on the candidate.
senses.exampleCN: 主教把手按在候选人身上。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin picture: a hand, a seal, or a weight is put onto a surface. The abstract senses all borrow this downward placement.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语的字面画面：一只手、一枚印或一块重物被放到表面上。所有抽象义项都借用了这个“向下放置”的动作。

senses.title: To assign a duty or obligation
senses.titleCN: 派加义务：把责任压给某人
senses.definition: to give someone a duty, condition, or requirement that they must accept
senses.definitionCN: 把某项义务、条件或要求加给某人，使其必须接受
senses.example: The court imposed strict conditions on his release.
senses.exampleCN: 法院对他的释放施加了严格条件。
senses.why: A duty is a load that cannot be refused. The authority does not ask the person to carry it; it places the obligation and walks away.
senses.whyCN: 义务是一份无法拒绝的重负。权威并不请求此人背负，而是把义务放上去就走开。

senses.title: Printing: to arrange pages for a press sheet
senses.titleCN: 印刷拼版：把页面排到印版上
senses.definition: in printing, to arrange pages on a sheet so that they come out in the right order when folded
senses.definitionCN: 印刷中，把页面排在一张纸上，使折叠后页序正确
senses.example: The printer imposed the sixteen pages into one signature.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷工把十六页拼成一个印张。
senses.why: This is a technical survival of 'place upon': page shapes are placed onto one sheet in a calculated pattern. The word imposition names both the layout and the burden.
senses.whyCN: 这是“放到上面”的技术留存：页面形状按计算好的图样被放到一张纸上。imposition 同时指这种排版与“负担”。

senses.title: Religious: to lay on hands
senses.titleCN: 宗教仪式：按手
senses.definition: in religious ritual, to place hands on a person to bless, ordain, or heal
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教仪式中把手放在某人身上，以示祝福、按立或医治
senses.example: The priest imposed hands on the sick child.
senses.exampleCN: 神父把手按在生病的孩子身上。
senses.why: The gesture is deliberately literal: one body places its hand on another. Blessing is understood as something that passes through the contact.
senses.whyCN: 这个手势刻意保持字面意义：一个身体把手放在另一个身体上。祝福被理解为通过这次接触传递过去。

senses.title: To pass something off as genuine
senses.titleCN: 以假充真：把赝品塞给人
senses.definition: to offer a fake or inferior thing as if it were real, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中，把赝品或劣货当作真货提供给他人
senses.example: The dealer imposed a forged painting on the collector.
senses.exampleCN: 经销商把一幅赝品画卖给了这位收藏家。
senses.why: The fake is placed on the buyer as if it were the real thing. Deception is a burden laid on someone's trust, which is why impostor comes from the same root.
senses.whyCN: 赝品被当作真货放到买家身上。欺骗是一份压在他人信任上的负担，这正是 impostor 出自同一词根的原因。

senses.title: Self-imposed: a burden one chooses
senses.titleCN: 自我施加：自己给自己上的规矩
senses.definition: in the compound self-imposed, a rule or limit that a person sets for themselves
senses.definitionCN: 在复合词 self-imposed 中，指一个人为自己设定的规则或限制
senses.example: They finished the report before their self-imposed deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在自己设定的期限前完成了报告。
senses.why: The same downward placement, now with the self as both authority and bearer. No one else forces the burden, which makes the choice visible.
senses.whyCN: 还是同一个“放上去”的动作，只是此时自我既是权威也是承受者。没有别人强加这份负担，因此选择本身变得可见。

intro.en: Impose reached English through Old French imposer 'to put, place; impute, charge'. Its Latin model is imponere (in- + ponere 'place'), but the French verb poser itself is usually traced to a different Latin verb, pausare 'to rest'. This is a well-known substitution in French etymology, so the exact root path is marked as not fully certain.
intro.cn: impose 经古法语 imposer“放置；归咎、指控”进入英语。它的拉丁语范本是 imponere（in- + ponere“放置”），但法语动词 poser 本身通常被追溯到另一个拉丁动词 pausare“停息”。这是法语词源学中著名的替换现象，因此确切的词根路径只能标为“不完全确定”。

items.en: First recorded as 'to lay a crime, duty, or obligation to someone's account', from Old French imposer. The sense is already about placing something on a person.
items.cn: 最早记录为“把罪责、义务或责任记到某人账上”，来自古法语 imposer。此义已经是在把某物“放到”一个人身上。

items.en: Imposer (c. 1300) meant 'put, place; impute, charge, accuse'. It was built with in- plus poser 'to put, place'.
items.cn: imposer（约 1300 年）意为“放置；归咎、指控”。它由 in- 加法语 poser“放置”构成。

items.en: The sense model is Latin imponere 'to place upon, inflict', from in- 'upon' + ponere 'to put, place' (past participle positus). Ponere is the root that separates impose from implement (plere 'fill').
items.cn: 语义范本是拉丁语 imponere“放到……之上、施加”，由 in-“在上”+ ponere“放置”（过去分词 positus）构成。ponere 正是 impose 与 implement（plere“填满”）的分界词根。

items.en: French poser is generally traced to Late Latin pausare 'to halt, rest', which developed the transitive sense 'cause to rest, set down' and then took over the meaning of ponere. Standard references call this an extraordinary substitution, so the exact chain is source uncertain.
items.cn: 法语 poser 一般被追溯到晚期拉丁语 pausare“停下、休息”，它发展出“使停息、放下”的及物义，随后取代了 ponere 的含义。通行资料称这是一种“非同寻常的替换”，因此确切的链条标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: The sense 'apply authoritatively' appears around 1500; 'lay on as a burden, inflict by force or authority' is first recorded in the 1580s.
items.cn: “以权威施加”义约在 1500 年出现；“作为负担强加、凭武力或权威施加”最早记录于 16 世纪 80 年代。

items.en: The adjective imposing 'impressive in appearance' appears in 1786. Printing imposition and the phrase impose on someone's hospitality extend the same placing gesture into technical and social use.
items.cn: 形容词 imposing“外观令人印象深刻”出现于 1786 年。印刷术语 imposition 以及 impose on someone's hospitality 这一短语，把同一个“放置”手势延伸到技术与社交用法中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the impos- shape; the near-meaning group separates authority, deception and intrusion.
note.cn: 形近组共享 impos- 外形；近义组区分权威施加、欺骗与侵扰。

entries.definition: a person who pretends to be someone else. It comes from Latin impostor, one who 'puts it upon' others.
entries.definitionCN: 冒充他人的人。它来自拉丁语 impostor，即“把东西放到别人身上”的人。

entries.definition: the act of imposing a burden, or a burden imposed. In printing it also means the arrangement of pages.
entries.definitionCN: 施加负担的行为，或被强加的负担。印刷中还指页面的拼版。

entries.definition: impressive in size or appearance. The sense developed from 'placing oneself upon the attention'.
entries.definitionCN: 在体量或外观上令人印象深刻的。该义由“把自己放到别人的注意之上”发展而来。

entries.definition: to make a law or rule obeyed. It stresses compulsion, while impose stresses placing the rule in the first place.
entries.definitionCN: 使法律或规则被遵守。它强调强制，而 impose 强调把规则放上去的第一步。

entries.definition: to make someone suffer something unpleasant. It is narrower and always about pain or damage.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人遭受不快之事。它更窄，且总与痛苦或损害有关。

entries.definition: to officially collect a tax or fee. It is the technical word for the money case of impose.
entries.definitionCN: 官方征收税或费。它是 impose 在“收钱”这一情形下的技术词。

entries.definition: to enter where one is not wanted. It overlaps with impose on, but stresses unwanted presence.
entries.definitionCN: 进入不受欢迎的地方。它与 impose on 重叠，但更强调“不受欢迎的存在”。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases. Remember ponere 'place' for impose, plere 'fill' for implement.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语。记住 impose 是 ponere“放置”，implement 是 plere“填满”。

normal.en: in- 'upon' + ponere 'place': to impose is to place something heavy on someone.
normal.cn: in-“在上”+ ponere“放置”：impose 就是把重物放到别人身上。

normal.en: impose, position, deposit and compose all belong to the ponere 'place' family.
normal.cn: impose、position、deposit、compose 都属于 ponere“放置”词族。

normal.en: To impose on a friend is to place more weight on their hospitality than they offered.
normal.cn: impose on 一位朋友，就是把超过对方所给的重量压在他的款待上。

normal.en: A self-imposed deadline is a weight you place on your own back.
normal.cn: self-imposed deadline 是你亲手放到自己背上的重量。

normal.en: Imposing buildings look as if they place themselves on your attention.
normal.cn: imposing 的建筑看起来像把自己放到了你的注意力之上。

abstract.en: Picture a seal pressed into wax: the pressure comes from above, and the mark stays after the hand is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章压进蜡里：压力从上方来，手离开后印记仍留着。

abstract.en: Every imposed rule has two ends: an authority that presses and a person who must carry the shape.
abstract.cn: 每一条被强加的规则都有两端：一端是施压的权威，一端是必须承受这个形状的人。

abstract.en: The word can turn inward: when the presser and the pressed are the same self, the burden becomes a promise.
abstract.cn: 这个词也可以转向内部：当施压者与承受者是同一个自我时，负担就变成了承诺。

examples.en: The city imposed a fine of two hundred dollars for illegal parking.
examples.cn: 该市对违章停车处以两百美元罚款。

examples.en: Do not impose your schedule on the whole team.
examples.cn: 不要把你的时间安排强加给整个团队。

examples.en: She imposed a strict rule on herself: no phone before noon.
examples.cn: 她给自己定下严格规矩：中午之前不碰手机。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬破丝”——硬把破丝线塞给别人 → impose 强加、施加负担

root: 源自拉丁语 imponere“放到……之上、施加”，由 in-“在上”+ ponere“放置”构成；经古法语 imposer 于 14 世纪晚期进入英语，核心是“把负担按到别人身上”。
