sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of impose, all built on one downward gesture: something is placed on a person or surface. Taxes, beliefs, duties, hands and false goods are all laid on.
sensesIntro.cn: impose 的九个义项都建立在同一个向下放置的动作上：某物被放到人或表面上。税、信念、义务、手与赝品，都是被放上去的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weight pressed down onto someone who did not ask for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件重物被压到并未要求它的人身上。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: a tax, condition or duty is placed by power and cannot be refused.
branches.cn: 权威：税、条件或义务由权力放上去，无法拒绝。

branches.en: BELIEF: a mental weight, where one person's preference is laid on another's mind.
branches.cn: 信念：心理上的重量，一个人的偏好被放到另一个人的心上。

branches.en: INTRUSION: the weight exceeds what hospitality offered, and the guest becomes a burden.
branches.cn: 侵扰：重量超过了款待所给，客人本身成了负担。

branches.en: PHYSICAL PLACEMENT: hands, seals, and pages laid out for a press sheet are all literally put on something.
branches.cn: 物理放置：手、印章，以及为印版摆好的页面，都实实在在被放到某物之上。

branches.en: DECEPTION AND SELF-RULE: a fake is placed on trust; a limit is placed on oneself.
branches.cn: 欺骗与自律：赝品被放到信任之上；限制被放到自己身上。

intro.en: Impose is in- + poser (from Latin ponere 'place'). English builds with -ition, -ing, -ed, -able and the prefixes super-, re- and self-.
intro.cn: impose 是 in- + poser（来自拉丁语 ponere“放置”）。英语用 -ition、-ing、-ed、-able 以及 super-、re-、self- 等前缀构建词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is ponere 'to place' (participle positus). Relatives include position, deposit, compose, propose, expose and postpone.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 ponere“放置”（分词 positus）。同族词包括 position、deposit、compose、propose、expose、postpone。

items.meaning: the act of imposing; a burden or unfair demand
items.meaningCN: 强加；征收；负担或不合理要求
items.example: The new fee feels like an imposition.
items.exampleCN: 这项新收费让人觉得是强加于人的负担。

items.meaning: forced on someone by authority
items.meaningCN: 被强加的；由权威施加的
items.example: The imposed limit was unpopular.
items.exampleCN: 这一强制限额不受欢迎。

items.meaning: large and impressive in appearance
items.meaningCN: 宏伟的；气势逼人的
items.example: The castle has an imposing gate.
items.exampleCN: 这座城堡有一扇气势宏伟的大门。

items.meaning: able to be imposed, especially of a tax
items.meaningCN: 可征收的；可施加的
items.example: The court asked whether such a penalty was imposable.
items.exampleCN: 法院询问这样的处罚是否可以施加。

items.meaning: a person who imposes something
items.meaningCN: 施加者；强加者
items.example: The imposer of the rule was never named.
items.exampleCN: 这条规则的施加者从未被点名。

items.meaning: to place one thing over another, especially images
items.meaningCN: 叠加；把一物覆在另一物之上（尤指图像）
items.example: The software superimposes the map on the photo.
items.exampleCN: 软件把地图叠加在照片上。

items.meaning: to impose a rule or tax again after a break
items.meaningCN: 重新施加；恢复征收
items.example: The government reimposed the curfew.
items.exampleCN: 政府重新实施了宵禁。

items.meaning: set by oneself rather than by others
items.meaningCN: 自我施加的；自己设定的
items.example: He works best under self-imposed pressure.
items.exampleCN: 他在自我加压时状态最好。

items.meaning: a tax or duty; also the upper part of a column
items.meaningCN: 税款；关税；也指柱头承重的部分
items.example: The impost on imported cloth was raised.
items.exampleCN: 进口布料的关税被提高了。

definition_zh: 激励；刺激；奖励；诱因；激励性的
definition_en: something that encourages a person or organization to act, especially a reward or benefit, or an arrangement designed to produce such encouragement
core_image: 在前方放一块看得见的糖，让人愿意多走一步
scene: The manager points to the bonus table: We need an incentive that makes people want to finish early, not just one that punishes lateness.
sceneCN: 这里 incentive 是「激励、奖励」（第 1 个义项：促使行动的动力）；句意：我们需要一种让人愿意提前完成的激励，而不只是惩罚迟到的办法。图中可辨识物件：奖金表、白板、计时器。

pos.zh: 激励；奖励；诱因；刺激
激励的；起鼓励作用的（较旧用法）

forms.label: 比较级（名词性形容词，少用）

derivatives.zh: 激励化；以激励手段推动
激励（由 incentive 逆构，多为官方用语）

senses.title: Something that motivates action
senses.titleCN: 激励：促使人行动的东西
senses.definition: a thing that makes someone want to do something or work harder
senses.definitionCN: 使某人想要做某事或更努力的事物
senses.example: The chance to travel was a strong incentive to join the team.
senses.exampleCN: 有机会出差是加入这个团队的一大激励。
senses.why: Latin incentivus meant 'setting the tune'. The image is a musician striking up a melody that others then follow: the incentive starts the action, it does not push it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 incentivus 意为“定调、起调”。意象是一位乐手起了一个调子，其他人随之跟上：incentive 是启动行动，而不是推动行动。

senses.title: A money reward tied to performance
senses.titleCN: 金钱奖励：与表现挂钩的报酬
senses.definition: a bonus, commission, or payment offered for achieving a result
senses.definitionCN: 为达成结果而提供的奖金、佣金或报酬
senses.example: Sales staff receive an incentive for every contract they close.
senses.exampleCN: 销售人员每签下一份合同就能获得一笔奖励。
senses.why: The 'reward for harder work' sense entered general use in the mid-20th century through incentive payment and incentive scheme. The tune is now priced.
senses.whyCN: “为更努力工作而给的报酬”这一义项在 20 世纪中期经由 incentive payment 与 incentive scheme 进入通用语。此时“调子”被标上了价格。

senses.title: A tax or policy incentive
senses.titleCN: 税收或政策激励
senses.definition: a government measure, such as a tax break, designed to encourage particular behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 政府为鼓励特定行为而设计的措施，如税收减免
senses.example: The tax incentive made solar panels cheaper for homeowners.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税收激励让家庭安装太阳能板更便宜。
senses.why: The state cannot order people to invest, so it places a benefit in front of them instead. The incentive is a tune the policy hopes people will dance to.
senses.whyCN: 国家不能命令人们投资，于是把一项好处放在他们面前。incentive 是政策希望人们随之起舞的那个调子。

senses.title: An economic signal
senses.titleCN: 经济信号：改变选择的诱因
senses.definition: in economics, a factor that changes the cost or benefit of a choice and therefore behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中改变某一选择成本或收益、从而改变行为的因素
senses.example: Higher prices create an incentive to use less fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 更高的价格形成了少用燃料的激励。
senses.why: Economists treat incentives as signals in a system of choices. A price is not an order, but it changes what people want to do next.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把激励看作选择系统里的信号。价格不是命令，却改变了人们接下来想做什么。

senses.title: A spur to effort: the challenge itself
senses.titleCN: 激发干劲：挑战本身也是激励
senses.definition: anything that stimulates effort, including a difficult task, a prize, or a rival
senses.definitionCN: 任何激发努力的事物，包括困难任务、奖品或对手
senses.example: The rival team's speed was an incentive to train harder.
senses.exampleCN: 对手的速度成了更刻苦训练的动力。
senses.why: The motivating thing need not be pleasant or paid. A challenge sets a tune as effectively as a bonus, because it makes a better performance imaginable.
senses.whyCN: 激励之物不必令人愉快，也不必付费。挑战和奖金一样能定调，因为它让更好的表现变得可以想象。

senses.title: An incentive scheme or programme
senses.titleCN: 激励方案：制度化的奖励安排
senses.definition: an organized system of rewards used by an employer or organization
senses.definitionCN: 雇主或组织采用的有组织的奖励制度
senses.example: The company introduced an incentive scheme for safety suggestions.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为安全建议推出了一套激励方案。
senses.why: One incentive is a nudge; a scheme is a standing orchestra. The tune plays regularly so that behaviour keeps time with it.
senses.whyCN: 单个 incentive 是一次推动；scheme 则是一支常设乐队。调子定期奏响，使行为持续跟上节拍。

senses.title: A perceived benefit in decision-making
senses.titleCN: 被感知的好处：行为选择的依据
senses.definition: in behavioural economics, the benefit a person believes they will gain from an option
senses.definitionCN: 行为经济学中，一个人认为从某个选项中将获得的好处
senses.example: People respond to the incentive they perceive, not always the one intended.
senses.exampleCN: 人们回应的是自己所感知的激励，而不总是设计者所意图的那个。
senses.why: An incentive works only if it is seen. What matters is the benefit as the chooser imagines it, which is why the same reward can motivate one person and not another.
senses.whyCN: 激励只有被看见才起作用。关键是选择者想象中的好处，这正是同一份奖励能激励一个人却激励不了另一个人的原因。

senses.title: Adjective: inciting or encouraging
senses.titleCN: 形容词义：起激励作用的
senses.definition: in older use, serving to incite, excite, or encourage
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中，指起煽动、激发或鼓励作用的
senses.example: Milton used incentive in the sense of 'incendiary'.
senses.exampleCN: 弥尔顿曾用 incentive 表示“煽动性的”。
senses.why: The adjective came first in this branch, around 1600, and meant 'provocative, exciting'. It survives mostly inside the noun's modern sense of encouragement.
senses.whyCN: 这一支的形容词义约在 1600 年先行出现，意为“煽动性的、令人兴奋的”。它如今主要存留在名词“鼓励”这一现代义项里。

intro.en: Incentive is a Late Latin adjective turned noun. Its stated root is incinere 'to strike up, begin to sing', but the 'inciting' sense is generally thought to have been influenced by incendere 'to kindle'. The deeper PIE root *kan- 'to sing' is reconstructed, so the exact semantic path is marked as probable rather than certain.
intro.cn: incentive 是一个由晚期拉丁语形容词转来的名词。其明载词根是 incinere“起调、开始唱”，但“煽动”这一含义一般被认为是受了 incendere“点燃”的影响。更深的原始印欧语词根 *kan-“唱”属于重构，因此确切语义路径只能标为“一般认为”，而非确定。

items.en: First recorded as 'that which moves the mind or stirs the passion', from Late Latin incentivum, a noun use of the neuter adjective incentivus.
items.cn: 最早记录为“推动心智或激起情感之物”，来自晚期拉丁语 incentivum，即中性形容词 incentivus 的名词化用法。

items.en: Incentivus meant 'setting the tune', and in Late Latin 'inciting'. It came from the past-participle stem of incinere 'strike up, begin to sing'.
items.cn: incentivus 意为“定调的”，在晚期拉丁语中又指“煽动的”。它来自 incinere“起调、开始唱”的过去分词词干。

items.en: Incinere is in- 'in, into' + canere 'to sing', from PIE *kan- 'to sing'. A singer who begins sets the pitch that others follow, which is the core of the metaphor.
items.cn: incinere 是 in-“进入”+ canere“唱”，后者来自原始印欧语 *kan-“唱”。起唱的歌手定下音高，其他人跟随，这就是该比喻的核心。

items.en: The 'inciting' sense is generally thought to have been influenced in Late Latin by incendere 'to kindle'. That influence is described as apparent rather than proven, so this link is source uncertain.
items.cn: “煽动”义一般被认为在晚期拉丁语中受了 incendere“点燃”的影响。这种影响被描述为“似乎如此”，而非已证实，因此这一联系标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: The adjective is recorded with the sense 'provocative, exciting, encouraging'. Milton uses it in the stronger sense 'setting fire, incendiary'.
items.cn: 形容词被记录为“煽动性的、令人兴奋的、鼓励性的”。弥尔顿用过更强的“点火、煽动性”义。

items.en: Incentive as a system of rewards first appears in the jargon of the U.S. war economy in 1943; 'rewards meant to encourage harder work' is recorded from 1948, short for incentive payment.
items.cn: 作为奖励制度的 incentive 于 1943 年首先出现在美国战时经济用语中；“为鼓励更努力工作而给的报酬”这一义项自 1948 年有记录，是 incentive payment 的缩略。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the incent- shape; the near-meaning group separates the spur from the reward and the motive.
note.cn: 形近组共享 incent- 外形；近义组区分“刺激物”“报酬”与“内在动机”。

entries.definition: to use rewards to encourage behaviour. It is the verb built on incentive, common in business writing.
entries.definitionCN: 用奖励鼓励行为。它是建立在 incentive 上的动词，常见于商业写作。

entries.definition: something that discourages action. It is dis- 'opposite of' + incentive.
entries.definitionCN: 抑制行动的事物。它由 dis-“相反”+ incentive 构成。

entries.definition: designed to cause fires, or tending to stir conflict. It comes from incendere 'to kindle', the word that influenced incentive's meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 用于纵火的，或易于煽动冲突的。它来自 incendere“点燃”，正是影响 incentive 词义的那个词。

entries.definition: the reason or desire that makes someone act. It can be internal, while an incentive is usually an external offer.
entries.definitionCN: 促使人行动的理由或愿望。它可以是内在的，而 incentive 通常是外部提供之物。

entries.definition: something offered to persuade someone to act. It is close to incentive but sounds more like a lure.
entries.definitionCN: 为说服某人行动而提供之物。它接近 incentive，但更像“诱饵”。

entries.definition: something given in return for good behaviour or work. It is the concrete thing, while incentive is the reason the thing is offered.
entries.definitionCN: 因良好行为或工作而给予之物。它是具体的东西，而 incentive 是提供这份东西的理由。

entries.definition: something that causes a reaction or increased activity. It is broader and often biological or economic.
entries.definitionCN: 引起反应或增加活动的事物。它范围更广，常用于生物或经济语境。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real terms; the key image is a musician striking up a tune.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实术语；关键意象是乐手起调。

normal.en: Latin incinere 'to strike up a song' gives incentive: the reward sets the tune others follow.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 incinere“起唱一首歌”给出 incentive：奖励定下调子，其他人跟着走。

normal.en: incentive, incentivize and disincentive share one stem; disincentive is the tune that makes people stop.
normal.cn: incentive、incentivize、disincentive 共享一个词干；disincentive 是让人停下的那个调子。

normal.en: A tax incentive is a benefit placed in front of a choice, not a command.
normal.cn: tax incentive 是放在选择面前的一项好处，而不是一道命令。

normal.en: An incentive scheme is a standing arrangement, while a single bonus is one note played once.
normal.cn: incentive scheme 是常设安排，而单笔奖金只奏响一个音符。

normal.en: In economics, incentives change the price of a choice, and people follow the changed price.
normal.cn: 经济学中，incentive 改变一个选择的“价格”，人们则跟随改变后的价格。

abstract.en: Picture a carrot on a stick held just ahead of a walker: the carrot does not push, it makes the next step worth taking.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绑在棍子上的胡萝卜，举在行人前方不远处：胡萝卜并不推人，它只是让下一步值得走。

abstract.en: An incentive is a tuning fork: it produces one clear note, and a whole group of actions fall into rhythm with it.
abstract.cn: incentive 是一把音叉：它发出一个清晰的音，一整组行动便随之落入节奏。

abstract.en: The same reward can be a gift or an insult, depending on who is listening to the tune.
abstract.cn: 同一份奖励可以是礼物，也可以是侮辱，取决于谁在听这个调子。

examples.en: Flexible hours are a stronger incentive than a small pay rise for many parents.
examples.cn: 对许多父母来说，弹性工时比小幅加薪更有吸引力。

examples.en: The subsidy was designed as an incentive to insulate old houses.
examples.cn: 这项补贴被设计为鼓励人们给老房子做隔热的激励。

examples.en: Without an incentive, the extra paperwork will simply not get done.
examples.cn: 没有激励，这些额外文书工作根本不会有人做。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬森体武”——硬是精神抖擞地练武，因为有好奖励 → incentive 激励、奖励

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 incentivus“定调的、煽动的”，来自 incinere“起调、开始唱”，由 in-“进入”+ canere“唱”构成；核心是“先起一个调，让别人跟着动”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of incentive, all built on one image: something sets a tune and makes the next action worth taking. The tune may be money, policy, a rival, or a perceived benefit.
sensesIntro.cn: incentive 的八个义项都建立在同一个意象上：某物起了一个调，让下一步行动值得走。这个调可以是金钱、政策、对手，或一个人所感知的好处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear note is struck ahead of the listener, and the listener's next move falls into step with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：在听者前方奏响一个清晰的音，听者的下一步便随之合拍。

branches.en: DRAWING FORWARD: a nudge, a challenge or a chance can start action without paying for it.
branches.cn: 向前牵引：一次推动、一个挑战或一个机会，不必付钱也能启动行动。

branches.en: PAID REWARD: the tune is priced and, in a scheme, played on a regular schedule.
branches.cn: 付费奖励：调子被标价；在方案中，它按固定日程反复奏响。

branches.en: POLICY AND MARKET: a tax break or a price change alters what behaviour is worth.
branches.cn: 政策与市场：税收优惠或价格变化改变某种行为的“值不值得”。

branches.en: PERCEPTION: only the benefit the chooser sees can move the chooser.
branches.cn: 感知：只有选择者看见的好处，才能推动选择者。

branches.en: INCITEMENT: the older adjective sense, where the tune is fiery rather than encouraging.
branches.cn: 煽动：较旧的形容词义，此时的调子是火热的，而非鼓励性的。

intro.en: Incentive is a complete Latin adjective, so English adds -ize, -ization and the negative prefix dis-. The internal in- belongs to Latin and cannot be removed.
intro.cn: incentive 是一个完整的拉丁形容词，因此英语只加 -ize、-ization 与否定前缀 dis-。内部的 in- 属于拉丁语，不可拆掉。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is canere 'to sing' and incinere 'to strike up'. Relatives include chant, canticle, incantation and the musical term cantata.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 canere“唱”与 incinere“起唱”。同族词包括 chant、canticle、incantation，以及音乐术语 cantata。

items.meaning: to encourage behaviour by offering rewards
items.meaningCN: 以奖励鼓励行为；使有动力（-ize 表示“使……化”）
items.example: The policy incentivizes companies to hire local workers.
items.exampleCN: 该政策激励企业雇用本地工人。

items.meaning: the act of making something reward-driven
items.meaningCN: 激励化；以奖励机制推动的过程
items.example: Incentivization of the sales team raised short-term numbers.
items.exampleCN: 对销售团队实行激励化提高了短期数字。

items.meaning: something that discourages an action
items.meaningCN: 抑制因素；反激励（dis- 表示相反）
items.example: High parking fees are a disincentive to driving downtown.
items.exampleCN: 高额停车费是抑制开车进市中心的因素。

items.meaning: to provide an incentive (official jargon, late 20c.)
items.meaningCN: 给予激励（由 incentive 逆构，20 世纪后期官方用语）
items.example: The scheme was designed to incent recycling.
items.exampleCN: 该方案旨在激励回收。

items.meaning: encouraged by an incentive (jargon)
items.meaningCN: 受到激励的（行话）
items.example: Incented employees filed more claims.
items.exampleCN: 受激励的员工提交了更多申请。

items.meaning: given a reward structure
items.meaningCN: 被纳入奖励机制的
items.example: The incentivized loan offered a lower rate for repairs.
items.exampleCN: 这项激励性贷款为维修提供较低利率。

items.meaning: organized around rewards rather than rules
items.meaningCN: 以奖励为基础的
items.example: They replaced fines with an incentive-based system.
items.exampleCN: 他们用奖励制取代了罚款制。

items.meaning: designed so that individual self-interest supports the intended outcome
items.meaningCN: 激励相容的（设计使个人利益与预期结果一致）
items.example: The auction was incentive-compatible for bidders.
items.exampleCN: 这场拍卖对竞拍者是激励相容的。

latinEntries.meaning: to strike up, begin to sing

definition_zh: 事件；事故；事变；插曲；（物理）入射的
definition_en: an event or occurrence, especially one that is unusual, unpleasant, or connected with a larger situation, or (of light or a ray) falling on a surface
core_image: 一件事落到人身上、落进原本平稳的进程里
scene: The safety officer writes on the board: The incident happened at the loading bay, and nobody reported it for two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 incident 是「事故、事件」（第 1 个义项：发生的（常为不快的）事件）；句意：这起事故发生在装卸区，两个小时都没人上报。图中可辨识物件：装卸台、事故记录板、监控画面。

pos.zh: 事件；事故；事变；插曲
入射的；附带的；易发生的（多用于物理与正式语境）

senses.title: An event, often unpleasant
senses.titleCN: 事件：发生的（常为不快的）事
senses.definition: an event or occurrence, especially one that is unusual, unexpected, or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 发生的事情，尤指不寻常、出乎意料或不快的
senses.example: The police are investigating a serious incident at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正在调查车站发生的一起严重事件。
senses.why: Latin incidere means 'to fall upon'. An incident is something that falls into a situation from outside, which is why the word carries a sense of interruption rather than plan.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 incidere 意为“落到……之上”。incident 就是从外部落进某个情境的事情，因此这个词带有“打断计划”的意味。

senses.title: A separate occurrence in a story
senses.titleCN: 插曲：叙事中的一个片段
senses.definition: a single event or episode within a longer story or series of events
senses.definitionCN: 较长故事或一连串事件中的单个事件或片段
senses.example: The novel begins with a childhood incident that shapes everything after.
senses.exampleCN: 小说以一个塑造了后续一切的童年插曲开篇。
senses.why: A story is a stream of events, and an incident is one stone dropped into it. The word marks a distinct episode without claiming it is the whole plot.
senses.whyCN: 故事是一串事件，而 incident 是投入其中的一块石头。这个词标记一个独立片段，并不声称它就是全部情节。

senses.title: A hostile or political confrontation
senses.titleCN: 事变：敌对或政治性的冲突
senses.definition: a violent or political event, especially one that threatens relations between groups or countries
senses.definitionCN: 暴力或政治性事件，尤指威胁群体或国家关系者
senses.example: The border incident almost led to war.
senses.exampleCN: 这起边境事件几乎引发战争。
senses.why: The euphemistic sense 'event that might trigger a crisis' is recorded from 1913. Diplomats use the neutral word for something too dangerous to name directly.
senses.whyCN: “可能引发危机的事件”这一委婉义自 1913 年有记录。外交官用这个中性的词来指过于危险、不便直呼其名的事。

senses.title: A workplace safety incident
senses.titleCN: 工作场所事故：安全记录上的事
senses.definition: an accident, near miss, or safety-related event at work that must be reported
senses.definitionCN: 工作中发生、必须上报的事故、险情或安全相关事件
senses.example: Every incident at the plant is logged within the hour.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂里每一起事故都要在一小时内记录。
senses.why: Institutions need a countable unit for things that go wrong. The incident report turns a messy event into a record with a time, a place and a cause.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个可计数的单位来记录出错的事。incident report 把混乱的事件变成一条带有时间、地点与原因的记录。

senses.title: An insurance incident
senses.titleCN: 保险事故：可触发理赔的事件
senses.definition: an event that may give rise to a claim under an insurance policy
senses.definitionCN: 可能根据保单引发理赔的事件
senses.example: Report the incident to your insurer within seven days.
senses.exampleCN: 请在七天内向保险公司报告该事故。
senses.why: Insurance defines the moment when risk becomes a claim. That moment is an incident: something happened, and the policy now has to respond.
senses.whyCN: 保险界定风险变成理赔的那一刻。那一刻就是 incident：某事发生了，保单现在必须作出回应。

senses.title: Physics: incident light or a ray
senses.titleCN: 物理：入射光或入射线
senses.definition: of light, sound, or a ray, falling on a surface rather than leaving it
senses.definitionCN: 指光、声或射线落在表面上，而不是离开表面
senses.example: The angle of the incident ray equals the angle of reflection.
senses.exampleCN: 入射角等于反射角。
senses.why: This is the Latin verb made visible: a ray falls upon a surface. The adjective keeps the original downward motion that the noun has largely lost.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁动词的可见化：一条射线落在表面上。形容词保留了名词大多已失去的“向下落到”的动作。

senses.title: Incident to: naturally attached
senses.titleCN: 附带于：性质上随之而来的
senses.definition: in the phrase incident to, existing as a natural or necessary part of something
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 incident to，表示作为某物的自然或必要部分而存在
senses.example: Certain risks are incident to working at height.
senses.exampleCN: 某些风险是高空作业本身附带的。
senses.why: If an event falls upon a situation reliably, it can be treated as belonging to it. The adjective shifts from 'happening' to 'attached by nature'.
senses.whyCN: 如果某件事总是落在某种情境上，它就可以被视为属于该情境。形容词义由此从“发生”转为“性质上附带”。

senses.title: Archaic: likely to happen
senses.titleCN: 古义：可能发生的
senses.definition: in older usage, liable or likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中，指易于发生或可能发生的
senses.example: In the old chronicle, such storms were incident in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部旧编年史里，这样的风暴在秋天时有发生。
senses.why: The adjective was recorded in the late 15c. as 'likely to happen'. It weakened into the modern 'incidental' while the noun took over the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 该形容词在 15 世纪晚期被记录为“可能发生的”。它后来弱化为现代的“附带的”，而事件本身则由名词承担。

senses.title: A subordinate circumstance
senses.titleCN: 附属情况：随主事而来的细节
senses.definition: a circumstance that occurs in connection with something else and is treated as secondary
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事相关联、被视为次要的情况
senses.example: The report lists the main events and their incidents.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了主要事件及其附属情况。
senses.why: Mid-15c. usage treated an incident as something occurring casually in connection with something else. It is the small event that travels beside the large one.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中期的用法把 incident 视为与另一事偶然相关联而发生的事。它是伴随大事而行的小事。

intro.en: Incident is the present participle of Latin incidere 'to fall upon', from in- 'on' + cadere 'to fall'. Its closest English relative is accident, which uses ad- 'to' instead of in-; both describe something befalling someone.
intro.cn: incident 是拉丁语 incidere“落到……之上”的现在分词，由 in-“在上”+ cadere“落下”构成。它最亲近的英语亲属是 accident，后者用 ad-“向”而不是 in-；两者都描述某事降临到人身上。

items.en: First recorded as 'something which occurs casually in connection with something else', from Old French incident and directly from Latin incidentem.
items.cn: 最早记录为“与另一事偶然相关联而发生的事”，来自古法语 incident，并直接来自拉丁语 incidentem。

items.en: Incidere meant 'to fall in, fall, find the way; light upon, fall in with; occur, happen, befall'. The root image is something dropping onto a path.
items.cn: incidere 意为“落入、落下、找到路；碰到、遇见；发生、降临”。其词根意象是某物掉落在一条路上。

items.en: In- 'on' + cadere 'to fall', from PIE *kad- 'to fall'. The same cadere gives accident, cadence, occasion and decadent.
items.cn: in-“在上”+ cadere“落下”，后者来自原始印欧语 *kad-“落下”。同一个 cadere 还给出 accident、cadence、occasion、decadent。

items.en: The broader sense 'an occurrence viewed as a separate circumstance' is recorded. The word can now name any distinct event, not only a chance one.
items.cn: 更宽的义项“被视为独立情况的一次发生”被记录。此时这个词能指任何独立事件，而不只是偶然之事。

items.en: The adjective appears as 'likely to happen', then shifts to 'occurring as a subordinate' by the 1620s and to the literal 'falling upon' by the 1660s.
items.cn: 形容词先出现“可能发生”义，17 世纪 20 年代转为“作为附属而发生”，17 世纪 60 年代再转为字面的“落在……之上”。

items.en: The euphemistic sense 'event that might trigger a crisis or political unrest' is first attested. The neutral word becomes useful precisely because it names without judging.
items.cn: 委婉义“可能引发危机或政治动荡的事件”最早见于 1913 年。这个中性词之所以有用，正因为它命名而不评判。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -cid- shape and the cadere root; the near-meaning group ranges from neutral occurrence to serious affair.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -cid- 外形与 cadere 词根；近义组从中性“发生”延伸到严重“事件”。

entries.definition: the rate at which something occurs, especially disease. It is how often events fall, not the event itself.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的频率，尤指疾病发生率。它指事件落下的频次，而不是事件本身。

entries.definition: happening as a minor part of something larger. It is the adjective form, not another noun.
entries.definitionCN: 作为更大事物次要部分而发生的。它是形容词形式，不是另一个名词。

entries.definition: an unintended event causing damage. It uses ad- 'to' instead of in- 'on', but the same cadere 'fall'.
entries.definitionCN: 造成损害的非故意事件。它用 ad-“向”而非 in-“在上”，但共享同一个 cadere“落下”。

entries.definition: anything that happens, especially something important. It is neutral, while incident often hints at trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 发生的任何事情，尤指重要之事。它语气中性，而 incident 常暗示麻烦。

entries.definition: one event in a series, especially in a story or illness. It stresses being one part of a longer whole.
entries.definitionCN: 一连串事件中的一个，尤指故事或病程中的一段。它强调是较长整体的一部分。

entries.definition: something that happens or takes place. It is the most neutral and most abstract of these words.
entries.definitionCN: 发生或出现的事情。它是这些词中最中性、最抽象的一个。

entries.definition: a situation or matter, often one of public or private concern. It is broader and vaguer than incident.
entries.definitionCN: 一种情况或事务，常涉及公共或私人关切。它比 incident 更宽、更含糊。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases; cadere 'to fall' is the thread through the whole family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语；cadere“落下”是贯穿整个词族的线索。

normal.en: in- 'on' + cadere 'to fall': an incident is something that falls onto a situation.
normal.cn: in-“在上”+ cadere“落下”：incident 就是掉落到某个情境之上的事。

normal.en: accident, incident and incidence all come from cadere; only the prefix changes the direction of the fall.
normal.cn: accident、incident、incidence 都出自 cadere；只是前缀改变了落下的方向。

normal.en: The phrase without incident means the journey went on with nothing falling onto it.
normal.cn: without incident 意为旅程继续前行，没有任何事落到它上面。

normal.en: An incident report is the form that turns a fall into a fixed record.
normal.cn: incident report 是把一次“落下”变成固定记录的那张表。

normal.en: In physics, the incident ray is the ray that falls on the surface before it reflects.
normal.cn: 物理中，incident ray 是先落在表面、随后被反射的那条射线。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped into a calm pond: the water was going one way, and now there is a circle spreading from where it landed.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头落进平静的池塘：水面原本朝一个方向流动，现在从落点向外散开一圈波纹。

abstract.en: An incident is a date the calendar did not plan for. It becomes part of the story only afterward, when someone tells it.
abstract.cn: incident 是日历没有计划到的那个日期。它只有在事后被人讲述时，才成为故事的一部分。

abstract.en: The same fall can be called an accident, an incident or an incidence: a wound, a story, a rate.
abstract.cn: 同一次“落下”可以被称为 accident、incident 或 incidence：一道伤口、一个故事、一个频率。

examples.en: The flight landed without incident despite the strong wind.
examples.cn: 尽管风很大，航班还是平安降落。

examples.en: A small incident at the border grew into a diplomatic dispute.
examples.cn: 边境上的一起小事件发展成了外交争端。

examples.en: The incident was reported to the safety office the same afternoon.
examples.cn: 这起事故当天下午就报告给了安全办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬吸灯”——硬吸着灯看，结果灯掉下来砸到人 → incident 事件、事故

root: 源自拉丁语 incidere“落到……之上、发生”的现在分词 incidens，由 in-“在上”+ cadere“落下”构成，核心是“某事落到原本平稳的进程里”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of incident, all built on something falling onto a situation. A story episode, a border clash, a safety report and an incident ray are all versions of that fall.
sensesIntro.cn: incident 的九个义项都建立在“某物落到某个情境之上”。故事插曲、边境冲突、安全报告与入射线，都是这次“落下”的不同版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something drops onto a path that was already going somewhere else.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物落在一条原本正通往别处的路上。

branches.en: TROUBLE: a workplace accident or an insured loss is an event that demands a report.
branches.cn: 麻烦：工作场所事故或保险损失，都是必须被报告的事件。

branches.en: NARRATIVE: an episode or subordinate circumstance is one stone in the stream of a larger story.
branches.cn: 叙事：插曲或附属情况，是更大故事之流中的一块石头。

branches.en: POLITICS: a neutral word for a dangerous confrontation, chosen precisely because it does not accuse.
branches.cn: 政治：对危险冲突的中性称呼，选择它正因为它不作指控。

branches.en: PHYSICS: a ray falls on a surface, the literal motion the noun has mostly lost.
branches.cn: 物理：射线落在表面上，这是名词大多已失去的字面动作。

branches.en: ATTACHMENT: what reliably falls on a situation becomes something incident to it.
branches.cn: 附着：总是落在某种情境上的事，就变成该情境“附带”的性质。

intro.en: Incident is a Latin present participle, so English adds -al, -ally and -ence rather than a live prefix. The internal in- is part of the Latin verb.
intro.cn: incident 是拉丁语现在分词，因此英语只加 -al、-ally、-ence，而不加活的前缀。内部的 in- 是拉丁动词的一部分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is cadere 'to fall' and incidere 'to fall upon'. Relatives include accident, cadence, occasion, decadent and the medical term incidence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 cadere“落下”与 incidere“落到……之上”。同族词包括 accident、cadence、occasion、decadent，以及医学术语 incidence。

items.meaning: the rate or range of occurrence of something
items.meaningCN: 发生率；影响范围（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: The incidence of the disease has fallen.
items.exampleCN: 这种病的发生率已经下降。

items.meaning: happening as a minor accompaniment
items.meaningCN: 附带的；偶然发生的
items.example: The delay was incidental to the main problem.
items.exampleCN: 延误只是主要问题的附带情况。

items.meaning: by the way; as a minor related fact
items.meaningCN: 顺便提一句；偶然地
items.example: Incidentally, the same engineer designed both bridges.
items.exampleCN: 顺便说一句，两座桥都是同一位工程师设计的。

items.meaning: to happen at the same time or occupy the same space
items.meaningCN: 同时发生；位置重合（co- 表示“共同”）
items.example: The festival coincides with the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 这个节日与收获季同时到来。

items.meaning: a striking occurrence of two things at once by chance
items.meaningCN: 巧合；两事同时发生的偶然
items.example: By coincidence, they booked the same flight.
items.exampleCN: 巧的是，他们订了同一班飞机。

items.meaning: occurring together in time or space
items.meaningCN: 同时发生的；位置重合的
items.example: The two events were coincident but unrelated.
items.exampleCN: 这两件事同时发生，却并无关联。

items.meaning: with no incidents occurring
items.meaningCN: 无事故的；平安无事的
items.example: The plant completed an incident-free year.
items.exampleCN: 工厂度过了无事故的一年。

items.meaning: following an incident
items.meaningCN: 事件之后的
items.example: A post-incident review changed the safety rules.
items.exampleCN: 事后复盘改变了安全规则。

definition_zh: 收入；收益；所得；（旧）进入，到来
definition_en: the money a person or organization receives regularly from work, business, or investments, or in older use the act of coming in
core_image: 钱像水流一样，按周期流进同一个口袋
scene: The tenant shows the bank two months of payslips: They want proof that my income is steady before they approve the loan.
sceneCN: 这里 income 是「收入」（第 1 个义项：定期得到的钱）；句意：他们要求证明我的收入稳定，才会批准贷款。图中可辨识物件：工资单、银行柜台、贷款申请表。

pos.zh: 收入；收益；所得

forms.label: 复数（名词，多指多笔收入来源）

derivatives.zh: 支出（与 income 相对的日常用语）

senses.title: Money received regularly
senses.titleCN: 定期收入：按周期流进来的钱
senses.definition: the money a person receives regularly from work, business, or investments
senses.definitionCN: 个人从工作、生意或投资中定期得到的钱
senses.example: Her income covers rent but leaves little for travel.
senses.exampleCN: 她的收入够付房租，但剩不下多少去旅行。
senses.why: Income is literally 'that which comes in'. c. 1600 English began using the word for money arriving as payment, treating it as a flow into the household.
senses.whyCN: income 字面就是“进来之物”。约 1600 年起，英语开始用它指作为报酬而到来的钱，把它当作流入家庭的一股流。

senses.title: Business revenue
senses.titleCN: 企业收益：经营流入的钱
senses.definition: the money a company receives from selling goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 公司通过出售商品或服务得到的钱
senses.example: The firm's income rose with the new contract.
senses.exampleCN: 公司收入随着新合同而上升。
senses.why: A company also has a mouth into which money comes. The same flow metaphor is applied to sales receipts, though accounting distinguishes income from revenue.
senses.whyCN: 公司也有一个钱流进来的“口”。同一股流被用于销售收款，不过在会计上 income 与 revenue 仍有区分。

senses.title: National income
senses.titleCN: 国民收入：整个经济的流入总量
senses.definition: the total money earned within a country's economy over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一国经济在一段时间内所赚到的总金额
senses.example: National income grew faster than the population.
senses.exampleCN: 国民收入的增长快于人口增长。
senses.why: Scale the household up to a country and the same inflow becomes an economic aggregate. Economists measure the sum of all incomes as the size of the economy.
senses.whyCN: 把家庭放大到国家，同一股流入就成了经济总量。经济学家把所有收入之和作为经济体量的度量。

senses.title: Disposable income
senses.titleCN: 可支配收入：交完税后能花的钱
senses.definition: the money left after tax and essential costs, available to spend or save
senses.definitionCN: 扣除税费与必要开支后可用于消费或储蓄的钱
senses.example: Disposable income fell as energy bills rose.
senses.exampleCN: 随着能源账单上涨，可支配收入下降了。
senses.why: Of all the money that comes in, some is already claimed by tax. What remains is the part the household may actually dispose of as it likes.
senses.whyCN: 流进来的钱中，有一部分已被税收预先占去。剩下的部分才是家庭真正可以随意支配的。

senses.title: Earned income: wages
senses.titleCN: 劳动所得：工资与薪水
senses.definition: money received in return for work, including wages, salaries, and bonuses
senses.definitionCN: 因工作而得到的钱，包括工资、薪金与奖金
senses.example: Most of their income is earned income from two jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的收入大部分来自两份工作的劳动所得。
senses.why: This is the flow with a visible cause: hours of work go out and money comes in. Tax systems separate it from money that arrives without labour.
senses.whyCN: 这是原因可见的一股流：工时出去，钱进来。税制把它与不经劳动就到来的钱区分开来。

senses.title: Unearned income: rents and returns
senses.titleCN: 非劳动所得：租金与投资收益
senses.definition: money received from investments, rent, or other sources not requiring current work
senses.definitionCN: 来自投资、租金或其他不要求当下劳动来源的钱
senses.example: Unearned income is taxed at a different rate.
senses.exampleCN: 非劳动所得按不同税率征税。
senses.why: Money can also come in while no one works: a tenant pays, a share pays a dividend. The flow continues without the household's labour.
senses.whyCN: 没人工作时钱也可以流进来：租客付租，股票派息。这股流不依赖家庭的劳动而继续。

senses.title: Household income
senses.titleCN: 家庭收入：以一个户为单位的统计
senses.definition: the combined income of all members of a household, used as a measure in policy and statistics
senses.definitionCN: 一户中所有成员收入之和，用作政策与统计指标
senses.example: Household income is adjusted for the number of children.
senses.exampleCN: 家庭收入会按子女数量进行调整。
senses.why: Statistics need a container, not a person. The household becomes the unit, and all the separate inflows are added into one figure.
senses.whyCN: 统计需要一个容器，而不是一个人。家庭成为单位，所有分开的流入被加成一个数字。

senses.title: Accounting: the income statement
senses.titleCN: 会计：收入表所衡量的东西
senses.definition: in accounting, the profit-related figure reported in an income statement over a period
senses.definitionCN: 会计中，收入表在一段期间内报告的与利润相关的数字
senses.example: The income statement shows a small loss this quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 收入表显示本季度有小幅亏损。
senses.why: Accounting turns the flow into a report. The income statement lines up what came in against what went out so that a period can be judged.
senses.whyCN: 会计把这股流变成一份报告。收入表把流入与流出对齐，使一段时间可以被评判。

senses.title: Archaic: an entrance or arrival
senses.titleCN: 古义：进入、到来
senses.definition: the original sense of a coming in or arrival, now obsolete
senses.definitionCN: 最初表示“进入、到来”的义项，现已废弃
senses.example: The old record marks the income of the new abbot.
senses.exampleCN: 旧记录标明了新院长的到任。
senses.why: c. 1300 income simply meant 'entrance, arrival'. The money sense is a later metaphor: what arrives is what comes in.
senses.whyCN: 约 1300 年时 income 只表示“进入、到来”。金钱义是后来的比喻：到来的东西，就是进来的东西。

intro.en: Income is an English compound of in and come, first meaning 'entrance, arrival' around 1300. The money sense is about 1600. It may be a noun use of the late Old English verb incuman 'come in', though the exact formation is not fully documented.
intro.cn: income 是 in 与 come 的英语复合词，约 1300 年最初表示“进入、到来”。金钱义约在 1600 年出现。它可能是晚期古英语动词 incuman“进来”的名词化用法，不过确切构词过程并没有完整文献记录。

items.en: Recorded as 'entrance, arrival', literally 'a coming in'. The word was a plain compound, not a Latin borrowing.
items.cn: 记录为“进入、到来”，字面就是“一次进来”。这个词是朴素的英语复合词，并非拉丁语借词。

items.en: Perhaps a noun use of the late Old English verb incuman 'come in, enter'. The written record is thin, so the precise derivational step is source uncertain.
items.cn: 可能是晚期古英语动词 incuman“进来、进入”的名词化用法。书面记录稀少，因此确切的派生步骤标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: In is the Old English preposition/adverb of entering; come is from Old English cuman, from Proto-Germanic *kwem- and PIE *gwa- 'to go, come'. Together they describe motion inward.
items.cn: in 是古英语表示“进入”的介词/副词；come 来自古英语 cuman，可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *kwem- 与原始印欧语 *gwa-“走、来”。两者合起来描述向内的运动。

items.en: The sense 'money made through business or labor' appears: that which 'comes in' as payment for work or business. German einkommen and Swedish inkomst have the same logic.
items.cn: “通过生意或劳动赚到的钱”这一义项出现：作为工作或生意报酬而“进来”的东西。德语 einkommen 与瑞典语 inkomst 有同样的构词逻辑。

items.en: Income tax is recorded, introduced in Britain during the Napoleonic wars and re-introduced in 1842. The phrase fixed income as a public financial category.
items.cn: income tax 被记录，英国在拿破仑战争期间引入，1842 年重新实施。这一短语把 income 固定为公共财政范畴。

items.en: The word now spans personal earnings, business revenue, national aggregates and accounting statements. The original 'entrance' sense has disappeared from ordinary use.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖个人所得、企业收益、国家总量与会计报表。最初“进入”的义项已从日常使用中消失。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the in-/come shape; the near-meaning group separates the money received from the money earned or kept.
note.cn: 形近组共享 in-/come 结构；近义组区分“收到的钱”与“赚到的钱、留下的钱”。

entries.definition: coming in or about to take office. It keeps the original motion sense of income.
entries.definitionCN: 进来的；即将到任的。它保留了 income 最初的“进入”动作义。

entries.definition: a person who has recently moved into an area, especially one with money. It is income + -er, but means a person, not money.
entries.definitionCN: 新近搬入某地区的人，尤指有财力者。它是 income + -er，却指人，不指钱。

entries.definition: a result or consequence. It is out + come, the mirror image of income's inward motion.
entries.definitionCN: 结果；后果。它是 out + come，与 income 向内运动的方向正好相反。

entries.definition: money earned from work or business. It stresses the effort that produced the money.
entries.definitionCN: 通过工作或生意赚到的钱。它强调产生这笔钱的劳动。

entries.definition: the total money received by a company or government before costs. It is broader and more institutional than income.
entries.definitionCN: 公司或政府在扣除成本前收到的总金额。它比 income 更宽，也更机构化。

entries.definition: a fixed regular payment for professional work. It is one kind of income, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 为专业工作定期支付的固定报酬。它是一种收入，而不是整个类别。

entries.definition: what remains after costs are subtracted from revenue. Income can exist before costs; profit cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 从收益中扣除成本后剩下的部分。income 可以在成本之前存在；profit 不能。

normalIntro.en: Real compounds and real contrasts; the word is simply 'what comes in'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实复合词与真实对比；这个词就是“进来的东西”。

normal.en: in + come: income is literally what comes in, first an entrance, later money.
normal.cn: in + come：income 字面上就是“进来的东西”，先指进入，后指钱。

normal.en: outcome is its mirror: what comes out of a process rather than what comes into a purse.
normal.cn: outcome 是它的镜像：从过程中出来的结果，而不是流进钱包的东西。

normal.en: income tax is a tax on the flow that comes in, introduced in Britain in 1790.
normal.cn: income tax 是对“流入”征的税，1790 年在英国引入。

normal.en: Disposable income is the part of the inflow left after tax has taken its share.
normal.cn: disposable income 是税收取走一份之后剩下的那部分流入。

normal.en: Earned income comes from work; unearned income comes from what one already owns.
normal.cn: earned income 来自劳动；unearned income 来自已经拥有的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a house with a door: money enters through the door at intervals, and the word for the house's total inflow is income.
abstract.cn: 想象一座有门的房子：钱按间隔从门进来，而这所房子总流入的名称就是 income。

abstract.en: Income is a river, not a lake. What matters for a household is not how full it is today but how steadily it keeps flowing.
abstract.cn: income 是一条河，不是一座湖。对家庭而言，重要的不是今天有多满，而是它流得有多稳。

abstract.en: Every income has a direction and a source; remove the source and the flow becomes a memory.
abstract.cn: 每一笔收入都有方向与来源；抽掉来源，这股流就变成回忆。

examples.en: The family lives on a single income.
examples.cn: 这个家庭靠一份收入生活。

examples.en: Tourism provides most of the island's income.
examples.cn: 旅游业提供了岛上大部分收入。

examples.en: After tax, their disposable income barely covers the rent.
examples.cn: 交完税后，他们的可支配收入勉强够付房租。

dict_mnemonic.text: “印康”——每月工资印在卡上，康康（看看）就来了 → income 收入

root: 由英语 in“进入”+ come“来”复合而成，约 1300 年先指“进入、到来”，约 1600 年转指“作为报酬流进来的钱”，核心是“定期流进同一处的钱”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of income, all built on one motion: money coming in. The same inflow is viewed as personal pay, business revenue, a national total, or a line in an accounting report.
sensesIntro.cn: income 的九个义项都建立在同一个动作上：钱流进来。同一股流入可以被看作个人工资、企业收益、国家总量，或会计报表中的一行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: money entering through one door at regular intervals.
core.cn: 核心意象：钱按固定间隔从同一扇门进来。

branches.en: ARRIVAL: the oldest sense, where income is simply an entrance or a coming.
branches.cn: 到来：最古老的义项，income 只表示进入或到来。

branches.en: PERSONAL FLOW: wages and salaries arrive in return for work.
branches.cn: 个人流入：工资与薪金作为劳动的回报到来。

branches.en: BUSINESS AND ASSETS: sales, rents and returns flow in, and accounting arranges them into a statement.
branches.cn: 企业与资产：销售、租金与投资回报流入，会计把它们排成报表。

branches.en: AGGREGATES: households and whole economies are counted as containers of many inflows.
branches.cn: 总量：家庭与整个经济被当作容纳许多流入的容器来计算。

branches.en: WHAT REMAINS: after tax claims its share, the rest is the part one may dispose of.
branches.cn: 剩余：税收取走一份后，剩下的才是可支配的部分。

intro.en: Income is a native English compound, not a prefixed Latin word. Its family is built from in, come, -ing, -er and fixed compounds such as income tax.
intro.cn: income 是英语本族复合词，不是拉丁语前缀词。它的词族由 in、come、-ing、-er 以及 income tax 这类固定复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root behind income. The comparable Latin-based word would be revenue, from Latin revenire 'to come back', which is a different formation.
latinIntro.cn: income 背后没有拉丁词根。意思相近的拉丁来源词是 revenue，来自拉丁语 revenire“回来”，构词路径完全不同。

items.meaning: arriving or entering; about to take office
items.meaningCN: 进来的；即将到任的
items.example: The incoming tide covered the path.
items.exampleCN: 涨潮淹没了小路。

items.meaning: a newcomer to an area
items.meaningCN: 新来者；移入者（-er 表示人）
items.example: The village has many incomers from the city.
items.exampleCN: 这个村子有许多从城里搬来的人。

items.meaning: a tax on money received
items.meaningCN: 所得税
items.example: Income tax is deducted from each payslip.
items.exampleCN: 每张工资单都会扣除所得税。

items.meaning: a financial report of revenue and expenses over a period
items.meaningCN: 损益表；收入表
items.example: The income statement shows a profit for the year.
items.exampleCN: 收入表显示该年度有盈利。

items.meaning: state financial help for people with very low income
items.meaningCN: 低收入补助（国家提供的经济援助）
items.example: She applied for income support after losing her job.
items.exampleCN: 失业后她申请了低收入补助。

items.meaning: having little money coming in
items.meaningCN: 低收入的
items.example: The clinic serves low-income families.
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所为低收入家庭服务。

items.meaning: income before tax and deductions
items.meaningCN: 总收入；税前收入
items.example: Gross income is higher than take-home pay.
items.exampleCN: 税前总收入高于到手工资。

items.meaning: income after costs, tax, and deductions
items.meaningCN: 净收入；税后收入
items.example: Net income rose despite flat sales.
items.exampleCN: 尽管销售持平，净收入仍上升了。

definition_zh: 合并；纳入；把……并入；成立公司；体现；混合
definition_en: to combine separate things into one whole, to include something as part of a larger group, or to form a company as a legal body
core_image: 把几个分散的部分收进同一个身体里
scene: The chef folds the beaten egg into the warm sauce: You incorporate it slowly, or the sauce will split.
sceneCN: 这里 incorporate 是「拌入、使混合」（第 5 个义项：把一种成分混进另一物质）；句意：要慢慢把它拌进去，否则酱汁会分离。图中可辨识物件：打蛋碗、酱汁锅、搅拌勺。

pos.zh: 合并；纳入；使并入；体现
合并的；组成公司的（多用于 incorporated 形式）

derivatives.zh: 组成公司的；合并的（缩写 Inc.）
重新并入；重新注册成立

senses.title: To combine into one whole
senses.titleCN: 合成整体：把分开的东西并成一个
senses.definition: to combine separate elements so that they form a single unified whole
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的要素合并，使其成为一个统一整体
senses.example: The design incorporates stone, glass, and steel.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计把石头、玻璃和钢材融为一个整体。
senses.why: Latin incorporare is in- 'into' + corpus 'body'. The parts are not merely placed side by side; they are taken into one body, which is why the result is a whole rather than a pile.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 incorporare 是 in-“进入”+ corpus“身体”。各部分不只是并排摆放，而是被收进同一个身体，因此结果是一个整体，而不是一堆。

senses.title: To include as part of a larger thing
senses.titleCN: 纳入：作为更大事物的一部分
senses.definition: to make something a part of a larger group, system, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 使某物成为更大群体、系统或计划的一部分
senses.example: The new edition incorporates the latest research.
senses.exampleCN: 新版纳入了最新研究。
senses.why: The body here is a book, a plan or a system. What is incorporated becomes an organ inside it rather than an outside attachment.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“身体”是一本书、一项计划或一个系统。被 incorporate 的东西成为其中的器官，而不是外挂的附件。

senses.title: To form a legal corporation
senses.titleCN: 设立公司：让人群成为一个法人身体
senses.definition: to establish a business or organization as a legal corporation
senses.definitionCN: 把企业或组织设立为法律上的公司法人
senses.example: The founders incorporated the business in Delaware.
senses.exampleCN: 创始人在特拉华州注册成立了这家公司。
senses.why: The legal sense, recorded from the mid-15c., is startlingly literal: several persons are united into one 'body' that can act as a single person.
senses.whyCN: 这一法律义自 15 世纪中期有记录，字面得惊人：若干人被联合成一个“身体”，可以像一个人那样行动。

senses.title: To embody an idea or quality
senses.titleCN: 体现：让抽象之物有了身体
senses.definition: to give concrete form to an idea, quality, or principle
senses.definitionCN: 使观念、品质或原则获得具体形态
senses.example: The building incorporates the values of the community that paid for it.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑体现了出资社区的价值观。
senses.why: An idea has no body until something houses it. To incorporate is to give the abstraction a corpus—walls, words, or habits—so it can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 观念没有身体，直到某物容纳它。incorporate 就是给抽象之物一个 corpus（身体）——墙、文字或习惯——让它可见。

senses.title: To mix an ingredient into a substance
senses.titleCN: 拌入：把一种成分混进另一物质
senses.definition: to mix one substance into another so that they are evenly combined
senses.definitionCN: 把一种物质混入另一种，使其均匀结合
senses.example: Incorporate the butter a little at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 一点一点地把黄油拌进去。
senses.why: The oldest English use was medical and culinary: 'to put something into the body or substance of something else, blend; absorb, eat'. Mixing is a small act of embodiment.
senses.whyCN: 英语最古的用法是医学与烹饪的：“把某物放进另一物的身体或实质中，混合；吸收、吃下”。混合就是一次小规模的“赋体”。

senses.title: Incorporated: formed as a legal body
senses.titleCN: （形容词）组成法人的
senses.definition: as an adjective, legally formed into a corporation, often written Inc. after a company name
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词时指依法组成公司法人，常以 Inc. 写在公司名后
senses.example: Kestrel Design Incorporated opened a second office.
senses.exampleCN: 凯斯特雷尔设计股份有限公司开设了第二间办公室。
senses.why: The participle has become a legal label. A name followed by Inc. announces that the entity has been given a corporate body.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词变成了法律标签。公司名后跟 Inc.，就宣告该实体已被赋予一个法人身体。

senses.title: To absorb nutrients into the body
senses.titleCN: 吸收：把养分收进身体
senses.definition: in biology and medicine, to take a substance into the body or an organ
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学与医学中，把某物质摄入身体或某个器官
senses.example: The gut incorporates nutrients from digested food.
senses.exampleCN: 肠道从消化后的食物中吸收养分。
senses.why: Here the body is literal. A nutrient is taken into the organism and becomes part of its substance, which is the original medical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这里的身体是字面意义的。养分被摄入生物体，成为其实质的一部分，这正是最初的医学义。

senses.title: To merge one organization into another
senses.titleCN: 并入：一个组织被另一个吸收
senses.definition: to combine one company or group into another, often losing the first identity
senses.definitionCN: 把一家公司或团体并入另一家，常使其原有身份消失
senses.example: The small studio was incorporated into a larger publisher.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小工作室被并入一家更大的出版社。
senses.why: One body absorbs another until only one body remains. The smaller organization becomes a part rather than a partner.
senses.whyCN: 一个身体吸收另一个，最后只剩一个身体。较小的组织成为“部分”，而不是“伙伴”。

senses.title: To give legal form to a group
senses.titleCN: 赋予团体法律形式
senses.definition: to give a group, such as a charity or club, a formal legal identity
senses.definitionCN: 给慈善机构、俱乐部等团体一个正式的法律身份
senses.example: The trustees incorporated the charity to protect its members.
senses.exampleCN: 受托人把这家慈善机构注册为法人，以保护其成员。
senses.why: A group without legal form cannot own, sue, or be sued. Incorporation gives the group a single body in law, and with it a capacity to act.
senses.whyCN: 没有法律形式的团体无法拥有财产、起诉或被起诉。incorporation 给团体一个法律上的单一身体，也给了它行动能力。

intro.en: Incorporate comes from Late Latin incorporare 'to unite into one body': in- 'into' + corpus 'body'. The word is literally about bodies, and every modern sense—from mixing batter to registering a company—keeps that bodily core.
intro.cn: incorporate 来自晚期拉丁语 incorporare“联合成一个身体”：in-“进入”+ corpus“身体”。这个词字面上就是关于身体的，所有现代义项——从拌面糊到注册公司——都保留了这个身体核心。

items.en: Recorded as 'to put something into the body or substance of something else, blend; absorb, eat', often in medical writing. It also meant 'solidify, harden'.
items.cn: 记录为“把某物放进另一物的身体或实质中，混合；吸收、吃下”，常见于医学文献。它也曾表示“使凝固、变硬”。

items.en: Incorporare 'unite into one body, embody, include' is in- 'into' + a verb from corpus (genitive corporis) 'body'.
items.cn: incorporare“联合成一个身体、体现、包括”由 in-“进入”+ 来自 corpus（属格 corporis）“身体”的动词构成。

items.en: Corpus 'body, living or dead' comes from PIE *kwrpes, from root *kwrep- 'body, form, appearance'. The same root gives corporeal, corpse and corps.
items.cn: corpus“身体，活体或遗体”来自原始印欧语 *kwrpes，根 *kwrep-“身体、形态、外表”。同一词根给出 corporeal、corpse、corps。

items.en: The legal sense 'to form a body politic with perpetual succession and power to act as one person' appears. The company becomes a legal body.
items.cn: “组成具有永久继承权、能像一个自然人一样行动的政治实体”这一法律义出现。公司成了一个法律身体。

items.en: The intransitive sense 'unite with another body so as to become part of it' is recorded, which leads to the modern merger sense.
items.cn: 不及物义“与另一个身体联合而成为其一部分”被记录，这导向现代的“并入”义。

items.en: The word now covers mixing ingredients, including research in a book, absorbing nutrients, and registering a company. The common thread is still one body taking others inside itself.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖拌入食材、把研究纳入书中、吸收养分以及注册公司。共同线索仍然是：一个身体把其他东西收进自身。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the corpor- 'body' root; the near-meaning group separates combining from including and embodying.
note.cn: 形近组共享 corpor-“身体”词根；近义组区分“合并”“包含”与“体现”。

entries.definition: relating to a large company. It is the adjective from corpus, not a form of incorporate.
entries.definitionCN: 与大公司有关的。它是来自 corpus 的形容词，不是 incorporate 的变形。

entries.definition: the act of combining into one body, or the legal formation of a company.
entries.definitionCN: 合并成一个身体的行为，或公司的依法设立。

entries.definition: relating to a physical body. It makes the body root visible without the in- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 与物理身体有关的。它不带 in- 前缀，直接显出“身体”词根。

entries.definition: to bring parts together into a working whole. It stresses functioning together, while incorporate stresses membership in one body.
entries.definitionCN: 把各部分合成一个能运作的整体。它强调协同运作，而 incorporate 强调成为同一身体的成员。

entries.definition: to have something as a part. It is broader and weaker than incorporate, which suggests real fusion.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物作为一部分包含在内。它比 incorporate 更宽、更弱，后者暗示真正的融合。

entries.definition: to combine two organizations into one. It is common in business and less bodily than incorporate.
entries.definitionCN: 把两个组织合并为一个。它常用于商业，身体意象不如 incorporate 强。

entries.definition: to give a visible or concrete form to an idea. It overlaps with sense 04 but is more literary.
entries.definitionCN: 给观念一个可见或具体的形式。它与第 4 个义项重叠，但更书面。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases; corpus 'body' is the thread through every sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语；corpus“身体”是贯穿所有义项的线索。

normal.en: in- 'into' + corpus 'body': to incorporate is to bring something into one body.
normal.cn: in-“进入”+ corpus“身体”：incorporate 就是把某物收进一个身体。

normal.en: corpus, corpse, corps and corporeal are all body words; incorporate is the verb that makes many bodies one.
normal.cn: corpus、corpse、corps、corporeal 都是“身体”词；incorporate 是把多个身体变成一个的动词。

normal.en: Incorporated, abbreviated Inc., marks a company that has been given a legal body.
normal.cn: Incorporated（缩写 Inc.）标记一家被赋予法律身体的公司。

normal.en: A recipe that says incorporate the butter means bring the butter into the body of the mixture.
normal.cn: 食谱里说 incorporate the butter，意思是把黄油收进混合物的“身体”里。

normal.en: When a small studio is incorporated into a publisher, one body absorbs the other.
normal.cn: 当小工作室被 incorporated into 一家出版社时，一个身体吸收了另一个。

abstract.en: Picture many threads twisted into one rope: each thread keeps its colour, but none can be pulled out without fraying the whole.
abstract.cn: 想象许多线拧成一根绳：每根线保留自己的颜色，但抽出一根就会让整体散开。

abstract.en: A corporation is a body made of people the way a body is made of cells; the law pretends the many are one.
abstract.cn: 公司是一个由人组成的身体，正如身体由细胞组成；法律假装“多”就是“一”。

abstract.en: To embody an idea is to build a house for something that had no walls.
abstract.cn: 体现一个观念，就是为某个原本没有墙的东西建一座房子。

examples.en: The report incorporates comments from more than fifty readers.
examples.cn: 这份报告纳入了五十多位读者的意见。

examples.en: They incorporated the charity so that it could hold property.
examples.cn: 他们把这家慈善机构注册为法人，以便持有财产。

examples.en: Fold the flour into the batter until fully incorporated.
examples.cn: 把面粉拌进面糊，直到完全混合。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因靠破雷特”——因为靠破雷特地把零件拼进一个机身 → incorporate 合并、纳入

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 incorporare“联合成一个身体”，由 in-“进入”+ corpus“身体”构成，过去分词 incorporatus，核心是“把分散部分收进同一个身体”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of incorporate, all built on one body: parts are taken inside a whole. A recipe, a book, a company and a charity are all bodies that can receive others.
sensesIntro.cn: incorporate 的九个义项都建立在同一个“身体”上：部分被收进整体。一道菜、一本书、一家公司、一个慈善机构，都是可以接收其他东西的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate pieces are gathered and enclosed inside one body.
core.cn: 核心意象：分散的部件被收拢、包进同一个身体。

branches.en: PHYSICAL BODY: ingredients and nutrients are literally taken into a substance or organism.
branches.cn: 物理身体：食材与养分被实实在在地摄入某物质或生物体。

branches.en: CONTAINER BODY: a book, plan, or organization receives parts and holds them as its own.
branches.cn: 容器身体：书、计划或组织接收部分，并把它们当作自身的一部分。

branches.en: LEGAL BODY: people are united into a corporation that can act as one person.
branches.cn: 法律身体：人们被联合成一家公司，可以像一个自然人那样行动。

branches.en: ABSTRACT BODY: an idea receives a concrete form, so it can be seen and shared.
branches.cn: 抽象身体：观念获得具体形式，因而可见、可共享。

branches.en: ABSORPTION: one organization swallows another, leaving a single body.
branches.cn: 吸收：一个组织吞并另一个，最后只剩一个身体。

intro.en: Incorporate is in- + corpor- + -ate. English adds -ation, -or, -ed and re-; the internal corpus remains the meaning-bearing root.
intro.cn: incorporate 是 in- + corpor- + -ate。英语加 -ation、-or、-ed 与 re-；内部的 corpus 仍是承载意义的词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is corpus 'body'. Relatives include corporeal, corporation, corpse, corps and the Latin-derived corporal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 corpus“身体”。同族词包括 corporeal、corporation、corpse、corps，以及拉丁来源的 corporal。

items.meaning: the act of combining into one body or forming a company
items.meaningCN: 合并；纳入；公司设立（-ion 构成过程名词）
items.example: Incorporation protects the owners from personal liability.
items.exampleCN: 公司化使所有者免于承担个人责任。

items.meaning: legally formed as a corporation
items.meaningCN: 已组成公司法的；合并的
items.example: The firm is incorporated in Singapore.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司在新加坡注册成立。

items.meaning: a person who formally establishes a corporation
items.meaningCN: 公司发起人；设立人
items.example: The incorporator signed the charter.
items.exampleCN: 发起人签署了公司章程。

items.meaning: tending to absorb or combine
items.meaningCN: 有合并倾向的；吸收性的
items.example: The language has an incorporative way of building verbs.
items.exampleCN: 这种语言有一种把成分并入动词的构词方式。

items.meaning: to incorporate again, especially in a new jurisdiction
items.meaningCN: 重新并入；在新管辖区重新注册
items.example: The company reincorporated in another state.
items.exampleCN: 公司在另一个州重新注册。

items.meaning: not formed as a legal corporation
items.meaningCN: 未组成法人的
items.example: An unincorporated club cannot own land in its own name.
items.exampleCN: 未注册为法人的俱乐部不能以自己的名义拥有土地。

items.meaning: a company treated as a single legal person
items.meaningCN: 公司；被当作单一法律人格的组织
items.example: The corporation employs three thousand people.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司雇用了三千人。

items.meaning: relating to a physical body
items.meaningCN: 肉体的；有形身体的
items.example: Corporeal punishment is banned in the school.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校禁止体罚。

items.meaning: a organized body of troops or a group with a shared role
items.meaningCN: 军团；具有共同职能的团体
items.example: The medical corps arrived first.
items.exampleCN: 医疗队最先抵达。

latinEntries.meaning: body, living or dead; physical substance
latinEntries.meaningCN: 身体，活体或遗体；物质实体

latinEntries.meaning: to unite into one body, embody, include
latinEntries.meaningCN: 联合成一个身体；体现；包括
被联合成一个身体的；被体现的

definition_zh: 表明；显示；指出；暗示；指示（方向）
definition_en: to show or point out something, to be a sign of it, or to suggest that a particular action is needed
core_image: 伸出一根手指，把注意力准确地指向一个点
scene: The gauge needle moved into the red zone, and the technician said: That indicates a blocked filter, not a broken pump.
sceneCN: 这里 indicate 是「表明、显示」（第 2 个义项：作为迹象说明某事）；句意：那表明过滤器堵了，而不是泵坏了。图中可辨识物件：仪表盘、红色刻度区、过滤器。

pos.zh: 表明；显示；指出；暗示
指示（方向或信号）

derivatives.zh: 表明的；指示性的；陈述的

senses.title: To point out
senses.titleCN: 指出：把注意力指向某物
senses.definition: to show or point to something so that others can see it
senses.definitionCN: 显示或指向某物，使他人能看见它
senses.example: The guide indicated the oldest tree in the park.
senses.exampleCN: 向导指出了公园里最古老的那棵树。
senses.why: Latin indicare is in- 'toward' + dicare 'proclaim, make known'. The core gesture is a finger extended: a thing is singled out and named.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 indicare 由 in-“朝向”+ dicare“宣告、使知晓”构成。核心手势是伸出一根手指：某物被单独指认出来。

senses.title: To be a sign of something
senses.titleCN: 表明：作为迹象说明某事
senses.definition: to be evidence or a sign that something is true or is happening
senses.definitionCN: 作为证据或迹象，说明某事为真或正在发生
senses.example: The test results indicate a mild infection.
senses.exampleCN: 检测结果表明显度感染。
senses.why: A sign does the pointing for us. Since 1706 indicate has meant 'to give suggestion of, be reason for inferring', so the finger becomes evidence.
senses.whyCN: 迹象替我们指出了方向。自 1706 年起，indicate 意为“给出提示、构成推断理由”，于是手指变成了证据。

senses.title: To express indirectly
senses.titleCN: 示意：用动作或语气表达
senses.definition: to express a feeling, intention, or answer indirectly rather than in words
senses.definitionCN: 用间接方式，而非言语，表达感受、意图或回答
senses.example: She indicated her agreement with a small nod.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻点头，表示同意。
senses.why: The gesture is still a pointing, but now it points at an inner state. A nod indicates agreement the way an arrow indicates north.
senses.whyCN: 这仍然是一种指向，只是指向内在状态。点头表明同意，正如箭头指示北方。

senses.title: Medical: to be a reason for treatment
senses.titleCN: 医学指征：说明该做某项处理
senses.definition: in medicine, for a condition to justify or require a particular treatment
senses.definitionCN: 医学中，指某种病情足以证明或需要某项治疗
senses.example: The scan indicates surgery rather than medication.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描结果说明需要手术，而不是药物治疗。
senses.why: Clinical signs point toward a course of action. What is indicated is not merely true but appropriate, so the word acquires a prescriptive edge.
senses.whyCN: 临床体征指向一条行动路线。被 indicate 的不只是事实，还有“应当如此”，因此这个词带上了一点规定意味。

senses.title: Of an instrument: to register a value
senses.titleCN: 仪表读数：显示某个数值
senses.definition: of a gauge, meter, or display, to show a particular measurement
senses.definitionCN: 指仪表、计量器或显示屏显示某个测量值
senses.example: The thermometer indicates eighteen degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 温度计显示十八度。
senses.why: An instrument is a mechanical finger. It does not argue; it points at a number and lets the reader interpret.
senses.whyCN: 仪器是一根机械手指。它不论证，只指向一个数字，让读者自行解释。

senses.title: Traffic: to signal a turn
senses.titleCN: 交通示意：打转向灯
senses.definition: to signal an intention to turn or change lanes, especially in a vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 示意打算转向或变道，尤指驾驶时
senses.example: Indicate before you leave the roundabout.
senses.exampleCN: 驶出环岛前要打转向灯。
senses.why: The driver's intention is invisible, so a lamp is made to point left or right. The signal indicates what the vehicle is about to do.
senses.whyCN: 驾驶者的意图看不见，于是用一盏灯指向左或右。信号表明车辆即将做什么。

senses.title: To state briefly or formally
senses.titleCN: 简要说明：正式地提到
senses.definition: to state or mention something briefly, especially in a formal or official context
senses.definitionCN: 简要陈述或提及某事，尤用于正式或官方语境
senses.example: Please indicate your name and address on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 请在表格上填写姓名和地址。
senses.why: Old forms ask you to 'indicate' rather than 'write' because the word originally meant to make known. The blank is a place where a fact must be pointed out.
senses.whyCN: 旧表格要求你 indicate 而不是 write，因为这个词本义是“使知晓”。空白处就是必须指出事实的位置。

senses.title: To represent by a symbol
senses.titleCN: 符号表示：用一个记号代表
senses.definition: for a symbol, letter, or mark to stand for a quantity or category
senses.definitionCN: 指符号、字母或记号代表某个量或类别
senses.example: In the formula, x indicates the unknown quantity.
senses.exampleCN: 公式中，x 表示未知量。
senses.why: A symbol points without touching. It indicates a value the way a name indicates a person, by standing in for it in a system.
senses.whyCN: 符号不接触也能指向。它表明一个数值，正如名字表明一个人，通过在系统中代表它。

senses.title: To suggest a likely diagnosis
senses.titleCN: 提示诊断：症状指向某种病
senses.definition: for symptoms or findings to point toward a particular diagnosis
senses.definitionCN: 指症状或检查结果指向某种特定诊断
senses.example: These symptoms indicate a viral infection rather than a bacterial one.
senses.exampleCN: 这些症状提示病毒感染，而非细菌感染。
senses.why: Diagnosis is inference from signs. Several small pointers—fever, fatigue, a rash—together indicate one condition, and the finger becomes a direction of reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 诊断是从体征推断。若干小指针——发热、疲乏、皮疹——共同指向一种病症，手指于是变成了推理的方向。

intro.en: Indicate is a back-formation from indication, or directly from Latin indicatus, past participle of indicare 'to point out'. Its root is dicare 'proclaim', not ducere 'lead' and not dividere 'divide'.
intro.cn: indicate 由 indication 逆构而来，或直接来自拉丁语 indicare“指出”的过去分词 indicatus。其词根是 dicare“宣告”，不是 ducere“引导”，也不是 dividere“分开”。

items.en: First recorded as 'to point out', either back-formed from indication or taken from Latin indicatus.
items.cn: 最早记录为“指出”，或由 indication 逆构，或直接取自拉丁语 indicatus。

items.en: Indicare meant 'to point out, show', from in- 'into, on, upon' + dicare 'proclaim'. Dicare and dicere 'say' are presumed to have been originally the same word.
items.cn: indicare 意为“指出、显示”，由 in-“向、在……之上”+ dicare“宣告”构成。dicare 与 dicere“说”被推测原本是同一个词。

items.en: Dicare is reconstructed from PIE *deik- 'to show, pronounce solemnly'. The same root gives diction, digit, and the Latin index.
items.cn: dicare 可重构自原始印欧语 *deik-“显示、郑重宣告”。同一词根给出 diction、digit，以及拉丁语 index。

items.en: The sense 'to give a suggestion of, be reason for inferring' is recorded. The word moves from pointing at things to pointing at conclusions.
items.cn: “给出提示、构成推断理由”这一义项被记录。这个词从“指向事物”转向“指向结论”。

items.en: Technical uses multiply: instruments indicate readings, signals indicate turns, and symbols indicate quantities. The finger becomes mechanical and abstract.
items.cn: 技术用法增多：仪表 indicate 读数，信号 indicate 转向，符号 indicate 数量。手指变得机械化、抽象化。

items.en: Keep three roots apart: dicare 'proclaim' gives indicate and index; ducere 'lead' gives induce and introduce; dividere 'divide' gives individual. Shared in- does not make them relatives.
items.cn: 要分清三个词根：dicare“宣告”给出 indicate 与 index；ducere“引导”给出 induce 与 introduce；dividere“分开”给出 individual。共享 in- 并不使它们成为同族。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dic- 'proclaim' root; the near-meaning group ranges from literal pointing to logical evidence.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dic-“宣告”词根；近义组从字面指向延伸到逻辑证据。

entries.definition: a sign, gauge, or measure that shows a condition. It is the thing that indicates.
entries.definitionCN: 显示某种状况的迹象、仪表或指标。它是进行指示的那个东西。

entries.definition: serving as a sign of something; also the grammatical mood of plain statement.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某事的；也指语法中的陈述语气。

entries.definition: an alphabetical list or a numerical measure. It comes from Latin index 'pointer, indicator', from dicare.
entries.definitionCN: 按字母排序的列表，或数值指标。它来自拉丁语 index“指示者、指针”，源自 dicare。

entries.definition: to make something visible or clear. It is the broad everyday word, while indicate is more formal and often about signs.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物可见或清楚。它是最宽的日常词，而 indicate 更正式，且多与迹象有关。

entries.definition: to send a deliberate sign. It stresses intention, while indicate can be involuntary evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 发出刻意的信号。它强调意图，而 indicate 可以是不由自主的证据。

entries.definition: to hint or give reason to think. It is softer and less definite than indicate.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示或给出思考理由。它比 indicate 更柔和，也更不确定。

entries.definition: to stand for something, especially as a symbol. It is narrower and more technical than indicate.
entries.definitionCN: 代表某物，尤指作为符号。它比 indicate 更窄，也更技术化。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real terms. The key is dicare 'proclaim', not ducere or dividere.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实术语。关键是 dicare“宣告”，不是 ducere 或 dividere。

normal.en: in- 'toward' + dicare 'proclaim': to indicate is to point at something and make it known.
normal.cn: in-“朝向”+ dicare“宣告”：indicate 就是指向某物并使之被知晓。

normal.en: index and indicate share dicare; both are about pointing, one with a finger and one with a list.
normal.cn: index 与 indicate 共享 dicare；两者都与“指向”有关，一个用手指，一个用列表。

normal.en: A gauge indicates a number; a nod indicates agreement; a red sky indicates a coming storm.
normal.cn: 仪表 indicate 一个数值；点头 indicate 同意；红天 indicate 暴风雨将至。

normal.en: As indicated above is the polite way of pointing back at a line already written.
normal.cn: as indicated above 是礼貌地回指上文已经写明的那一行。

normal.en: An indicator is the thing that does the indicating, from a speedometer to a species that reveals water quality.
normal.cn: indicator 是执行指示的那个东西，从速度表到能揭示水质的物种。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow drawn on a map: it does not move you, but it tells you which way movement would make sense.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画着的一支箭头：它不推动你，却告诉你往哪个方向走才合理。

abstract.en: A sign is a finger with no hand attached: the world points, and the observer supplies the meaning.
abstract.cn: 迹象是一只没有连着手的手指：世界在指，意义由观察者补上。

abstract.en: Indicate keeps its distance from induce and individual: pointing is neither leading nor dividing.
abstract.cn: indicate 与 induce、individual 保持距离：指向既不是引导，也不是分开。

examples.en: Please indicate on the map where you felt the shaking.
examples.cn: 请在地图上标出你感到晃动的位置。

examples.en: Early results indicate that the vaccine is working.
examples.cn: 早期结果表明疫苗正在起效。

examples.en: He indicated the door with a tilt of his head.
examples.cn: 他歪了歪头，示意门口的方向。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬地开它”——在硬地上打开它，伸手指给大家看 → indicate 指出、表明

root: 源自拉丁语 indicare“指出、显示”，由 in-“朝向”+ dicare“宣告、使知晓”构成，过去分词 indicatus，核心是“用手指向并说出来”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of indicate, all built on pointing. A finger, a needle, a signal lamp, a symbol and a symptom are five different pointers aimed at the same task: making something known.
sensesIntro.cn: indicate 的九个义项都建立在“指向”上。手指、指针、信号灯、符号与症状，是五种不同的指针，指向同一个任务：使某事被知晓。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger extends toward one point so that everyone else looks there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指伸向一个点，让其他人也看向那里。

branches.en: LITERAL POINTING: a guide points at a tree; a form points at a blank to be filled.
branches.cn: 字面指向：向导指向一棵树；表格指向一个待填的空白。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: test results and symptoms point at a condition without stating it.
branches.cn: 证据：检测结果与症状指向某种病情，却不直接说出。

branches.en: GESTURE AND SIGNAL: a nod or a turn lamp points at an intention.
branches.cn: 手势与信号：点头或转向灯指向某种意图。

branches.en: CLINICAL POINTING: what the signs point at becomes what should be done.
branches.cn: 临床指向：体征所指的东西，变成了应当采取的处理。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS AND SYMBOLS: a needle or a letter points at a value.
branches.cn: 仪表与符号：指针或字母指向一个数值。

intro.en: Indicate is in- + dic- + -ate. English builds with -ion, -or, -ive and the Latin-derived noun index.
intro.cn: indicate 是 in- + dic- + -ate。英语用 -ion、-or、-ive 以及拉丁来源名词 index 构建词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is dicare 'proclaim' and indicare 'point out'. Relatives include index, diction, dictate and dedicate; the same *deik- root also gives digit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 dicare“宣告”与 indicare“指出”。同族词包括 index、diction、dictate、dedicate；同一 *deik- 词根还给出 digit。

items.meaning: a sign or piece of evidence; the act of pointing out
items.meaningCN: 指示；迹象；表明的行为
items.example: There is no indication that the storm will return.
items.exampleCN: 没有迹象表明风暴会再来。

items.meaning: a device or measure that shows a condition
items.meaningCN: 指示器；指标；指示物
items.example: The indicator on the dashboard turned red.
items.exampleCN: 仪表盘上的指示灯变红了。

items.meaning: showing or suggesting something
items.meaningCN: 表明的；指示性的
items.example: A long silence is indicative of doubt.
items.exampleCN: 长时间的沉默表明有疑虑。

items.meaning: in a way that shows something
items.meaningCN: 以表明的方式；指示性地
items.example: The figures are indicatively useful, not final.
items.exampleCN: 这些数字有指示意义，但不是最终结果。

items.meaning: serving as a sign (rare)
items.meaningCN: 作为指示的（较少用）
items.example: The early frost was indicatory of a hard winter.
items.exampleCN: 早霜预示着一个严冬。

items.meaning: an alphabetical list or a numerical measure
items.meaningCN: 索引；指数；指标
items.example: Look up the term in the index.
items.exampleCN: 在索引里查这个词。

items.meaning: to be a reason not to use a treatment
items.meaningCN: 禁忌：构成不使用某疗法的理由
items.example: Pregnancy contraindicates the drug.
items.exampleCN: 怀孕是该药的禁忌。

items.meaning: the choice and use of words
items.meaningCN: 措辞；用词方式
items.example: The diction of the speech was plain and direct.
items.exampleCN: 这篇演讲的措辞朴素直接。

definition_zh: 个人的；单独的；独特的；个人；个体
definition_en: relating to one single person or thing, separate and distinct, or a single human being considered on their own
core_image: 一件不能再被切开的东西：切到它这里就到底了
scene: The coach points at each player in turn: Every individual on this team has to know the plan, not just the captain.
sceneCN: 这里 individual 是「个人、个体」（第 4 个义项：作为单个人来看的人）；句意：队里每一个个人都必须了解计划，不只是队长。图中可辨识物件：战术板、逐个点名的手指、球员。

pos.zh: 个人的；单独的；独特的；单个的
个人；个体；单个人或事物

collocations.zh: 私人（普通个人，非官方身份）

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Single and separate
senses.titleCN: 单独的：作为一个单位分开看
senses.definition: relating to one single person or thing, considered separately from the group
senses.definitionCN: 指单个的人或物，从群体中分开来看
senses.example: Each individual case must be judged on its own facts.
senses.exampleCN: 每个单独的案件都必须依其自身事实判断。
senses.why: Latin individuus is in- 'not' + dividuus 'divisible'. An individual is the point at which division stops, so the first sense is simply 'one that cannot be split further'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 individuus 由 in-“不”+ dividuus“可分的”构成。individual 就是“分割停止的那一点”，因此第一个义项就是“无法再被切开的一个”。

senses.title: Distinctive and personal
senses.titleCN: 独特的：带有个人印记的
senses.definition: having a quality or style that is clearly one's own and different from others
senses.definitionCN: 具有明显属于自己、区别于他人的品质或风格
senses.example: The room has an individual character that no catalogue could copy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间有一种目录册无法复制的独特气质。
senses.why: Once a thing is separated from the group, its differences become visible. The word moves from 'single' to 'uniquely marked'.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物从群体中分开，它的差异就变得可见。这个词于是从“单个”转为“带有独特标记”。

senses.title: Intended for one person
senses.titleCN: 供一人用的：按个人配置
senses.definition: designed or intended for one person rather than for a group
senses.definitionCN: 为一个人而非一群人所设计或准备的
senses.example: The airline serves individual portions of ice cream.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司提供单人份的冰淇淋。
senses.why: This sense is recorded from 1889. The unit of distribution becomes one person, so the portion is cut to the size of an individual.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项自 1889 年有记录。分配单位变成了一个人，于是份额被切到“个体”的大小。

senses.title: A single human being
senses.titleCN: 个人：作为单个人来看的人
senses.definition: one human being, especially when considered apart from a group or society
senses.definitionCN: 一个人，尤指与群体或社会分开来看时
senses.example: The law protects the individual as well as the community.
senses.exampleCN: 法律既保护个人，也保护社群。
senses.why: The noun sense, recorded from the 1640s, applies the 'indivisible unit' idea to a person. Each person is a unit that cannot be dissolved into the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 名词义自 17 世纪 40 年代有记录，把“不可分的单位”这一观念用到了人身上。每个人都是无法被溶解进人群的单位。

senses.title: A biological individual
senses.titleCN: 生物个体：一个独立的生命单位
senses.definition: in biology, a single organism considered as a distinct unit
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中，作为独立单位看待的单个生物体
senses.example: The study tracked one hundred individual birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追踪了一百只单独的鸟。
senses.why: Biology needs a countable unit below the species and above the cell. The individual is that unit: one life that can be observed and counted.
senses.whyCN: 生物学需要一个低于物种、高于细胞的计数单位。individual 就是那个单位：一条可被观察与计数的生命。

senses.title: Informal: a person of a certain kind
senses.titleCN: （口语）某个家伙：带评价色彩的人
senses.definition: in colloquial use, a person, often with mildly negative or ironic judgement
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法中指一个人，常带轻微贬义或讽刺评价
senses.example: A rather odd individual was asking about you.
senses.exampleCN: 有个挺奇怪的家伙在打听你。
senses.why: The colloquial 'person' sense is attested from 1742. Calling someone 'an individual' distances them, as if viewing them as a specimen rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 口语“人”义自 1742 年有记录。把某人称作 an individual 会产生距离感，仿佛把他当作标本而不是人来看。

senses.title: Relating to one member's rights
senses.titleCN: 涉及个人权利的
senses.definition: relating to the rights, duties, or liberties of one person rather than a collective
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人的权利、义务或自由，而非集体的
senses.example: Individual rights must be balanced against public safety.
senses.exampleCN: 个人权利必须与公共安全相权衡。
senses.why: Political thought uses the word to mark the boundary between the person and the collective. The indivisible unit is also the unit that holds rights.
senses.whyCN: 政治思想用这个词标记个人与集体之间的边界。那个不可分的单位，也是持有权利的单位。

senses.title: An indivisible particle
senses.titleCN: 不可分的单元：原子式的个体
senses.definition: in older philosophy, an indivisible entity or atom
senses.definitionCN: 较旧哲学中，一个不可分的实体或原子
senses.example: The old philosophers argued that every body is made of individuals.
senses.exampleCN: 古代哲学家论证说，每个物体都由不可分的单元构成。
senses.why: Latin individuum as a noun meant 'an atom, an indivisible particle'. The atom is the limiting case of the word's literal meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 individuum 意为“原子、不可分的微粒”。原子正是这个词字面意义的极限情形。

senses.title: A distinct entity in a system
senses.titleCN: 系统中的独立实体
senses.definition: one distinct item treated as a unit within a larger system, such as a record or an account
senses.definitionCN: 在更大系统中被当作单位处理的一个独立项目，如一条记录或一个账户
senses.example: Each individual account is audited once a year.
senses.exampleCN: 每个单独的账户每年审计一次。
senses.why: The unit idea travels beyond people. Any system that must keep parts separate marks each one as an individual, whether it is a person, a record, or a cell.
senses.whyCN: “单位”观念可以走出人。任何必须把部分保持分开的系统，都会把每一项标记为 individual，不论是人、记录还是细胞。

intro.en: Individual is the negative of divisible: Latin in- 'not' + dividere 'divide'. Its first English use was theological, about the indivisible Trinity; the modern 'single person' sense is only about 400 years old.
intro.cn: individual 是 divisible 的否定式：拉丁语 in-“不”+ dividere“分开”。它最早的英语用法是神学的，指不可分的三位一体；现代“单个人”的义项只有约四百年历史。

items.en: First recorded as 'one and indivisible, inseparable', with reference to the Trinity. This original sense is now obsolete.
items.cn: 最早记录为“单一且不可分、不可分离”，用于指三位一体。这一最初义项如今已废弃。

items.en: Individualis was formed from Latin individuus 'indivisible', from in- 'not' + dividuus 'divisible'. The word was rare before c. 1600; the 15c. example may be an outlier.
items.cn: individualis 由拉丁语 individuus“不可分的”构成，后者来自 in-“不”+ dividuus“可分的”。这个词在 1600 年前并不常见；15 世纪的用例可能只是孤例。

items.en: Dividere 'to force apart, cleave, distribute' is dis- 'apart' + -videre 'to separate', from PIE *(d)uid- 'to separate, distinguish'. Individual therefore contains the idea of division by negating it. The roots must not be confused: indicare uses dicare 'proclaim', induce uses ducere 'lead', and individual uses dividere 'divide'.
items.cn: dividere“分开、劈开、分配”由 dis-“分开”+ -videre“分离”构成，来自原始印欧语 *(d)uid-“分开、区分”。因此 individual 是通过否定“分割”而包含分割观念的。这些词根不可混淆：indicate 用 dicare“宣告”，induce 用 ducere“引导”，individual 用 dividere“分开”。

items.en: The sense 'single, separate, of but one person or thing' appears. The word now answers the question 'which one, apart from the rest?'
items.cn: “单个的、分开的、只属于一个人或物的”义项出现。此时这个词回答的是“哪一个，与其余分开来看？”

items.en: The noun means 'a single human being' as opposed to a group. Latin individuum had already meant 'an atom, indivisible particle'.
items.cn: 名词指“单个人”，与群体相对。拉丁语 individuum 早已表示“原子、不可分的微粒”。

items.en: The sense 'intended for one person' is recorded in 1889. Individualism as a social philosophy dates from the mid-19c., and individual rights become a central political phrase.
items.cn: “供一人使用的”义项自 1889 年有记录。作为社会哲学的个人主义始于 19 世纪中期，individual rights 则成为核心政治短语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the divid- root; the near-meaning group separates 'one unit' from 'one person' and 'unique'.
note.cn: 形近组共享 divid- 词根；近义组区分“一个单位”“一个人”与“独特”。

entries.definition: impossible to divide. It shows the root meaning that individual has largely left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 无法分割的。它显出 individual 已大体遗落的词根本义。

entries.definition: the quality of being a distinct person with a character of one's own.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一个有自身性格的独立个体的性质；个性。

entries.definition: a social outlook that gives the individual priority over the collective.
entries.definitionCN: 把个人置于集体之上的社会观念；个人主义。

entries.definition: one only, not one of a group. It is simpler and does not carry the 'indivisible' idea.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一个，不是群体中的一员。它更简单，不带“不可分”的观念。

entries.definition: existing apart from others. It stresses distance, while individual stresses being a distinct unit.
entries.definitionCN: 与他人分开存在的。它强调距离，而 individual 强调是一个独立单位。

entries.definition: one specific person or thing rather than any other. It stresses selection rather than separateness.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的人或物，而非其他。它强调“选定”，而不是“分离”。

entries.definition: a human being. It is the ordinary word, while individual can sound formal or slightly distancing.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人。它是最普通的词，而 individual 可能显得正式或略带距离感。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases; the in- here means 'not', not 'into'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语；这里的 in- 是“不”，不是“进入”。

normal.en: in- 'not' + dividere 'divide': an individual is the unit that cannot be divided further.
normal.cn: in-“不”+ dividere“分开”：individual 就是无法再被分割的单位。

normal.en: divide, division and individual share the same root, but individual negates it.
normal.cn: divide、division、individual 共享同一词根，但 individual 对它作了否定。

normal.en: Individual rights treat each person as a unit that cannot be dissolved into the crowd.
normal.cn: individual rights 把每个人当作无法被溶解进人群的单位。

normal.en: An individual portion is cut to the size of one unit rather than the group.
normal.cn: individual portion 是按“一个单位”而非群体切分的份量。

normal.en: Calling someone an individual instead of a person adds a little distance, as if observing a specimen.
normal.cn: 把某人称作 individual 而不是 person，会加一点距离感，仿佛在观察一个标本。
