abstract.en: Picture a loaf that can be sliced until only one crumb is left; the crumb that cannot be halved again is the individual.
abstract.cn: 想象一条面包可以被切片，直到只剩一粒碎屑；那粒无法再对半切的碎屑就是 individual。

abstract.en: Every crowd is an optical illusion: lower your eyes far enough and you see only individuals.
abstract.cn: 每一片人群都是一种错觉：把视线降得足够低，你只会看见一个又一个 individual。

abstract.en: Individuality is the scar left by separation: what makes you one thing also makes you unlike the others.
abstract.cn: individuality 是分离留下的印记：让你成为“一个”的东西，也让你不同于其他。

examples.en: The teacher gives individual attention to each learner.
examples.cn: 老师给每个学习者单独的关照。

examples.en: Each individual has a different reason for joining the course.
examples.cn: 每个人加入这门课的理由都不同。

examples.en: The survey interviews individuals rather than households.
examples.cn: 这项调查采访的是个人，而不是家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬地微丢”+“啊”——硬在地上微微丢了一块，只剩单个个体 → individual 个人、个体

root: 源自中世纪拉丁语 individualis“不可分的”，来自拉丁语 individuus（in-“不”+ dividere“分开”），核心是“切分到这里就停止的单一单位”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of individual, all built on one unit that cannot be divided further. That unit can be a person, an organism, a record, or an atom.
sensesIntro.cn: individual 的九个义项都建立在同一个“无法再被分割的单位”上。这个单位可以是人、生物体、记录，或原子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole that cannot be cut again without ceasing to be itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个整体，再切一刀就不再是它自己。

branches.en: ATOM: the literal limit case, an entity with no possible further division.
branches.cn: 原子：字面上的极限情形，一个无法再分的实体。

branches.en: COUNTABLE UNIT: biology, records and cases each need one unit that can be counted.
branches.cn: 可数单位：生物学、记录与案件都需要一个可计数的单位。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the unit is a human being, and that unit is the bearer of rights.
branches.cn: 人：这个单位是一个人，而这个人正是权利的持有者。

branches.en: ONE-PERSON USE: portions and arrangements are cut to the size of one unit.
branches.cn: 单人使用：份额与安排被切到一个单位的大小。

branches.en: DISTINCTION: separation makes difference visible, for praise or for ironic distance.
branches.cn: 区别：分离让差异可见，既可用于赞赏，也可用于讽刺性的距离。

intro.en: Individual is in- 'not' + divid- 'divide' + -ual. English adds -ity, -ism, -ist, -ize and -ly; the prefix here is privative, not locative.
intro.cn: individual 是 in-“不”+ divid-“分开”+ -ual。英语加 -ity、-ism、-ist、-ize、-ly；这里的前缀是否定性的，不是方位性的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is dividere 'to divide' and individuus 'indivisible'. Relatives include divide, division, dividend and subdivide.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 dividere“分开”与 individuus“不可分的”。同族词包括 divide、division、dividend、subdivide。

items.meaning: the quality of being a distinct person or thing
items.meaningCN: 个性；个体性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The school encourages individuality rather than uniformity.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校鼓励个性而非一律。

items.meaning: a belief that the individual takes priority over the group
items.meaningCN: 个人主义；认为个人优先于群体的观念
items.example: Individualism shapes much of the country's law.
items.exampleCN: 个人主义塑造了这个国家的大部分法律。

items.meaning: a person who acts independently or believes in individualism
items.meaningCN: 个人主义者；独立行事的人
items.example: She was an individualist who disliked committees.
items.exampleCN: 她是个不喜欢委员会的个人主义者。

items.meaning: marked by independent or self-directed behaviour
items.meaningCN: 个人主义的；强调独立自主的
items.example: The team culture was too individualistic for joint work.
items.exampleCN: 这种团队文化过于个人主义，不适合协作。

items.meaning: to make personal or suited to one person
items.meaningCN: 使个性化；使适应个人
items.example: The software individualizes each exercise.
items.exampleCN: 这款软件会为每道练习定制内容。

items.meaning: the process of making something personal
items.meaningCN: 个性化；个别化的过程
items.example: Individualization of treatment improves outcomes.
items.exampleCN: 治疗的个体化能改善结果。

items.meaning: one by one; separately
items.meaningCN: 逐个地；单独地
items.example: Each file was checked individually.
items.exampleCN: 每个文件都被逐一检查。

items.meaning: to distinguish one thing from others; to become a separate self
items.meaningCN: 使区分；使成为独立个体（心理学术语）
items.example: Children individuate slowly from their parents.
items.exampleCN: 孩子会慢慢从父母那里形成独立自我。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a distinct individual
items.meaningCN: 个体化过程；成为独立个体的过程
items.example: Jung described individuation as a lifelong task.
items.exampleCN: 荣格把个体化描述为一项终身任务。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 不可分的；无法被分割的

definition_zh: 诱导；劝使；引起；导致；归纳；感应
definition_en: to persuade someone to do something, to cause something to happen, or to produce an effect by influence rather than direct force
core_image: 在前面引路的手：不推你，只在前面招手，让你自己走过去
scene: The doctor explains that the drug may induce drowsiness, so the patient should not drive after taking it.
sceneCN: 这里 induce 是「引起、导致」（第 3 个义项：使某种状态发生）；句意：医生说这种药可能引起困倦，因此病人服药后不应开车。图中可辨识物件：药瓶、说明书、方向盘、打哈欠的病人。

pos.zh: 诱导；劝使；引起；导致；归纳；感应

senses.title: Lead by persuasion
senses.titleCN: 劝使：用说服把人引过去
senses.definition: to persuade or influence someone to do something, especially something they might not choose on their own
senses.definitionCN: 说服或影响某人做某事，尤指其原本未必会做的选择
senses.example: Nothing could induce him to leave the house before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 什么也无法劝使他在中午前离开家。
senses.why: Latin inducere is in- 'into' + ducere 'to lead'. The image is a guide walking ahead, not a hand pushing from behind; the person follows because the way has been made attractive.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 inducere 是 in-“进入”+ ducere“引导”。意象是在前面带路的人，而不是从背后推的手；人之所以跟随，是因为这条路被说得有吸引力。

senses.title: Bring about a physical reaction
senses.titleCN: 引起生理反应
senses.definition: to cause a physical response such as vomiting, sleep, or pain
senses.definitionCN: 引起呕吐、睡眠或疼痛等生理反应
senses.example: The syrup is used to induce vomiting after poisoning.
senses.exampleCN: 这种糖浆用于中毒后催吐。
senses.why: Medicine took the 'bring about' sense early: the drug does not persuade the body, it leads a reaction into existence.
senses.whyCN: 医学很早就采用了“使发生”这一义：药物并不说服身体，而是把一种反应引导出来、使其出现。

senses.title: Cause a state or condition
senses.titleCN: 导致某种状态
senses.definition: to cause a situation, feeling, or condition to begin to exist
senses.definitionCN: 使某种情况、感受或状态开始存在
senses.example: Uncertainty can induce stress in even experienced workers.
senses.exampleCN: 不确定性会给即使经验丰富的员工也带来压力。
senses.why: Once 'lead in' is extended from people to events, the object becomes a state: the cause leads the effect into being.
senses.whyCN: 当“引入”从人扩展到事件，宾语就变成一种状态：原因把结果引导出来、使之存在。

senses.title: Start labour medically
senses.titleCN: 引产：用医学手段启动分娩
senses.definition: to start the process of childbirth by medical means
senses.definitionCN: 用医学手段启动分娩过程
senses.example: The baby was induced two weeks early because of the risk.
senses.exampleCN: 由于存在风险，婴儿提前两周被引产。
senses.why: Here the body's own process is led into starting. The doctor does not force the birth directly but triggers the mechanism that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 这里是让身体自身的过程被“引入”启动。医生并不直接强行分娩，而是触发那个会产生分娩的机制。

senses.title: Derive a general rule from particular cases
senses.titleCN: 归纳：从个别推出一般
senses.definition: to reach a general principle by reasoning from specific observations
senses.definitionCN: 从具体观察出发，通过推理得到一般原理
senses.example: From these samples we can induce a general law of growth.
senses.exampleCN: 从这些样本中，我们可以归纳出一条普遍的生长规律。
senses.why: The 1560s logic sense treats reasoning as a path: individual cases are led into a general conclusion. This is induction, the mirror image of deduction.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 60 年代产生的逻辑义把推理看成一条路：个别事例被引导到一个一般结论。这就是归纳，与演绎正好相反。

senses.title: Produce a current by electromagnetic induction
senses.titleCN: 电磁感应：产生感应电流
senses.definition: to produce an electric current or voltage in a conductor by changing a magnetic field
senses.definitionCN: 通过改变磁场，在导体中产生电流或电压
senses.example: A changing magnetic field induces a current in the coil.
senses.exampleCN: 变化的磁场会在线圈中产生感应电流。
senses.why: The 1777 electrical sense keeps the same structure: no direct push, only influence at a distance, and the current is 'led into' the wire.
senses.whyCN: 1777 年出现的电学义保持同一结构：没有直接推力，只有隔空的影响，电流被“引入”导线。

senses.title: Give an object an induced charge or magnetism
senses.titleCN: 使物体产生感应电荷或磁性
senses.definition: to give a material a charge, magnetization, or polarization through the influence of a nearby field
senses.definitionCN: 借附近场的影响，使材料带上电荷、磁性或极化
senses.example: The rod induces a positive charge on the near side of the sphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这根棒使球体靠近的一侧产生正电荷。
senses.why: Induction is influence without contact. One body's field leads charges or domains in another body to rearrange, so the effect appears without being carried in.
senses.whyCN: 感应是不接触的影响。一个物体的场引导另一个物体中的电荷或磁畴重新排列，因此效应出现却没有被直接搬运进去。

senses.title: Bring a biological state into being
senses.titleCN: 诱导生物状态：分化或表达
senses.definition: in biology, to cause cells, genes, or organisms to enter a particular state
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中，使细胞、基因或生物体进入某种特定状态
senses.example: The protein induces the stem cells to become nerve cells.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蛋白质诱导干细胞变成神经细胞。
senses.why: Developmental biology borrows the causative sense again: a signal leads a cell down one path rather than pushing it there.
senses.whyCN: 发育生物学再次借用“使发生”义：信号把细胞引向某条路径，而不是把它推过去。

senses.title: Lead in; introduce (archaic literal sense)
senses.titleCN: 古义：引入、带进
senses.definition: in older usage, to lead or bring someone into a place, state, or office
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中，把某人引入某地、某种状态或职位
senses.example: The rite was said to induce the novice into the order.
senses.exampleCN: 据说那仪式会把新人引入该修道会。
senses.why: This is the Latin sense almost unchanged. Modern English usually replaced it with introduce or induct, but it explains why every other sense contains 'lead into'.
senses.whyCN: 这几乎是未变的拉丁本义。现代英语通常用 introduce 或 induct 取代它，但它解释了为什么其他每个义项都含“引入”这一成分。

intro.en: Induce comes from Latin inducere 'to lead into'. Its history is a single image carried across persuasion, medicine, logic and electricity. The critical root contrast is ducere 'lead' versus dicare 'proclaim' and dividere 'divide'.
intro.cn: induce 来自拉丁语 inducere“引入、引导”。它的历史是同一个意象被带到说服、医学、逻辑与电学中。关键要区分 ducere“引导”、dicare“宣告”与 dividere“分开”。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'to lead by persuasions or inducements'. The subject leads another person's will, not their body.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“用说服或诱因引导”。动作的主体引导的是他人的意愿，而不是他人的身体。

items.en: The sense 'to bring about, cause' appears, first in medical writing and then in general use. From here come induce sleep and induce vomiting.
items.cn: “使发生、引起”的义项出现，先用于医学写作，再进入一般用法。induce sleep 与 induce vomiting 都由此而来。

items.en: Inducere is in- 'into' + ducere 'to lead, draw'. Ducere is about guiding a path; dicare (in indicate) is about proclaiming; dividere (in individual) is about splitting. Imply uses plicare 'fold', impose uses ponere 'place', implement uses plere 'fill'.
items.cn: inducere 是 in-“进入”+ ducere“引导、牵引”。ducere 关乎带路；indicate 中的 dicare 关乎宣告；individual 中的 dividere 关乎分开。imply 用 plicare“折”，impose 用 ponere“放”，implement 用 plere“填满”。

items.en: The logical sense 'to infer by reasoning' is recorded, together with induction: particulars lead the mind to a general rule.
items.cn: 逻辑义“通过推理得出”有记录，同时出现 induction：个别事例把心灵引向一般规律。

items.en: The electrical sense appears: a changing magnetic field induces a current. Faraday's law of 1831 later gave the effect its exact form, but the verb came first.
items.cn: 电学义出现：变化的磁场会感应出电流。1831 年法拉第定律后来给出这一效应的精确形式，但动词用法在先。

items.en: Medicine induces labour and biology induces differentiation or gene expression. Inducer and inducible become standard technical terms.
items.cn: 医学上用 induce labour（引产），生物学上用 induce 表示诱导分化或基因表达。inducer 与 inducible 成为标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the duc- root; the near-meaning group separates persuasion, causation and generation.
note.cn: 形近组共享 duc- 词根；近义组区分“劝”“致”“生”。

entries.definition: to install someone formally in an office or group. It is the concrete 'lead in' sense that induce has mostly lost.
entries.definitionCN: 正式使某人就职或加入某团体。它是 induce 已大体失去的“引入”本义的具体版本。

entries.definition: the act of inducting; reasoning from particulars to a rule; or the production of current by a changing field.
entries.definitionCN: 就职；归纳推理；或由变化磁场产生电流。

entries.definition: something offered to persuade a person to act.
entries.definitionCN: 诱因；用来劝使某人行动的东西。

entries.definition: to make someone agree or decide by giving reasons. It stresses argument; induce stresses the attraction of the offered path.
entries.definitionCN: 通过给出理由使某人同意或决定。它强调论证；induce 强调所提供路径的吸引力。

entries.definition: to cause someone to do something, often suddenly. It stresses the spark rather than the guidance.
entries.definitionCN: 促使某人做某事，常指突然触发。它强调火花，而不是引导。

entries.definition: to make something happen. It is the neutral general word; induce often implies influence rather than direct force.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事发生。它中性而笼统；induce 常暗示影响而非直接施力。

entries.definition: to produce or create something, especially energy or a result. It stresses output, not the leading of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 产生或创造某物，尤指能量或结果。它强调产出，而不是对过程的引导。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases; the in- here means 'into', not 'not'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语；这里的 in- 是“进入”，不是“不”。

normal.en: ducere 'lead': induce is to lead someone into doing something, not to push them.
normal.cn: ducere“引导”：induce 是把某人引向做某事，而不是推他。

normal.en: The in- of induce is 'into', unlike the negative in- of individual.
normal.cn: induce 的 in- 是“进入”，不同于 individual 的否定前缀 in-。

normal.en: Conduct, produce, reduce and deduce all contain ducere 'lead'; induce adds 'into'.
normal.cn: conduct、produce、reduce、deduce 都含 ducere“引导”；induce 只是加上“进入”。

normal.en: Induce vs indicate: dicare 'proclaim' points with the voice, ducere 'lead' walks ahead.
normal.cn: induce 与 indicate：dicare“宣告”用声音指向，ducere“引导”则在前面走。

normal.en: Induction climbs from cases to a rule; deduction walks back down from the rule.
normal.cn: induction 从个案爬上规则；deduction 从规则往下走。

abstract.en: Picture a shepherd walking ahead of the flock, never driving from behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一个牧人在羊群前面走，从不从后面驱赶。

abstract.en: Influence at a distance: the wire never touches the magnet, yet the current appears.
abstract.cn: 隔空的影响：导线从未碰到磁铁，电流却出现了。

abstract.en: A good teacher induces curiosity: nothing is pushed, something is led out.
abstract.cn: 好老师会诱导好奇心：没有东西被推，只有东西被引出来。

examples.en: The advertisement is designed to induce people to buy on impulse.
examples.cn: 这则广告旨在诱导人们冲动购买。

examples.en: Certain drugs can induce drowsiness within an hour.
examples.cn: 某些药物能在一小时内引起困倦。

examples.en: From these cases the researchers induced a general pattern.
examples.cn: 研究者从这些案例中归纳出一个普遍模式。

dict_mnemonic.text: “引道士”——请来一位道士，先在前头引路，再劝你跟他走，路上还施法引起变化 → induce 引导、劝使、引起

root: 源自拉丁语 inducere“引入、引导”，由 in-“进入”+ ducere“引导”构成，过去分词 inductus；核心是“在前面带路，而不是从后面推”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of induce, all built on 'lead into'. A person is led by persuasion, a body is led into a reaction, a mind is led to a rule, and a wire is led into carrying current.
sensesIntro.cn: induce 的九个义项都建立在“引入”上。人被说服引过去，身体被引向某种反应，心灵被引向一条规律，导线则被引到载流状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a guide walks ahead and the other person chooses to follow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个引路人在前面走，另一个人选择跟上。

branches.en: PERSUASION: the path is made attractive so that the will follows it.
branches.cn: 说服：路被说得有吸引力，意愿便跟着走。

branches.en: CAUSATION: a drug, a stressor or a doctor leads a physical process into starting.
branches.cn: 因果：药物、压力源或医生把一个生理过程引向启动。

branches.en: LOGIC: particular cases lead the mind to a general rule.
branches.cn: 逻辑：个别事例把心灵引向一般规律。

branches.en: PHYSICS: a field leads charges or current into motion without contact.
branches.cn: 物理：场在不接触的情况下把电荷或电流引向运动。

branches.en: STATE AND PLACE: a signal leads a cell into a state; an old rite leads a person into a group.
branches.cn: 状态与地点：信号把细胞引入某种状态；旧仪式把人引入某个团体。

intro.en: Induce is in- + duc- + -e. The -duce family is large: conduct, produce, reduce, deduce, introduce. English builds inducement, induction, inductive, inductor, inducible and inducer.
intro.cn: induce 是 in- + duc- + -e。-duce 词族很大：conduct、produce、reduce、deduce、introduce。英语另加 -ment、-ion、-ive、-or、-ible、-er 构成派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin inducere 'lead in' and ducere 'lead'. Relatives include duct, duke, ductile and educate (ducere + ex- 'out').
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 inducere“引入”与 ducere“引导”。同族词包括 duct、duke、ductile、educate（ducere + ex-“出”）。

items.meaning: something that persuades a person to act
items.meaningCN: 诱因；劝使某人行动的事物
items.example: The company offered a bonus as an inducement.
items.exampleCN: 公司提供奖金作为诱因。

items.meaning: the act of inducting; reasoning from cases; magnetic or electric induction
items.meaningCN: 就职；归纳；磁感应或电感应
items.example: Induction begins with observed cases, not with a rule.
items.exampleCN: 归纳从观察到的个案开始，而不是从规则开始。

items.meaning: based on induction, or relating to electrical induction
items.meaningCN: 归纳的；归纳性的；电感的
items.example: The study uses inductive reasoning rather than a fixed model.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究使用归纳推理，而不是固定模型。

items.meaning: by reasoning from particular cases
items.meaningCN: 以归纳方式地
items.example: The theory was built inductively from field notes.
items.exampleCN: 这一理论是从田野笔记归纳建立起来的。

items.meaning: a component that stores energy in a magnetic field
items.meaningCN: 电感器；感应元件
items.example: The circuit needs a larger inductor to smooth the current.
items.exampleCN: 这个电路需要更大的电感器来平稳电流。

items.meaning: the property of a circuit that opposes changes in current
items.meaningCN: 电感；抵抗电流变化的性质
items.example: Inductance is measured in henries.
items.exampleCN: 电感以亨利为单位测量。

items.meaning: to lead in, persuade, or bring about
items.meaningCN: 引入；劝使；引起
items.example: The signal induces the cell to divide.
items.exampleCN: 这一信号诱导细胞分裂。

items.meaning: able to be induced or activated
items.meaningCN: 可诱导的；可被激活的
items.example: The gene is inducible by heat shock.
items.exampleCN: 这个基因可被热激诱导。

items.meaning: a substance or signal that induces a state
items.meaningCN: 诱导物；诱导者
items.example: The sugar acts as an inducer of the enzyme.
items.exampleCN: 这种糖充当该酶的诱导物。

items.meaning: to bring a person or thing into a place or group
items.meaningCN: 介绍；引入；引进
items.example: She introduced the new method to the team.
items.exampleCN: 她向团队介绍了这种新方法。

a leading, drawing; the perfect participle 'led'

definition_zh: 不可避免的；必然发生的；必然的；不可避免的事
definition_en: certain to happen and impossible to avoid or prevent
core_image: 一条已经走到尽头的路：所有岔路都被封住，只剩这一个方向
scene: The referee checks the clock and signals: with ten seconds left and a two-goal lead, the result is now inevitable.

senses.title: Impossible to avoid
senses.titleCN: 无法避免：躲不开
senses.definition: impossible to escape or prevent, no matter what one does
senses.definitionCN: 无论怎么做都无法逃脱或阻止
senses.example: With the road flooded, a delay was inevitable.
senses.exampleCN: 道路被淹，延误已无法避免。
senses.why: The word is the negation of evitable 'avoidable'. Latin evitabilis comes from evitare 'to shun'. To call something inevitable is to say that every route of avoidance is closed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 evitable“可避免的”的否定式。拉丁语 evitabilis 来自 evitare“躲避”。称某事 inevitable，就是说每一条躲避的路都已关闭。

senses.title: Certain to happen
senses.titleCN: 必然发生：时间到了就会来
senses.definition: sure to happen at some point, even if the exact time is unknown
senses.definitionCN: 在某个时点必定发生，即使具体时间未知
senses.example: Some conflict is inevitable when two teams share one budget.
senses.exampleCN: 两个团队共用一份预算时，某些冲突必然发生。
senses.why: Avoidance concerns a person's power; certainty concerns the event's arrival. The same word covers both because a thing that cannot be prevented is also a thing that will certainly come.
senses.whyCN: “躲避”关乎人有没有能力；“必然”关乎事件会不会到来。同一个词覆盖两者，因为无法被阻止的事，也就是必定会来的事。

senses.title: Logically necessary
senses.titleCN: 逻辑必然：由前提必然推出
senses.definition: following necessarily from the premises or the stated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 由前提或已陈述的条件必然推出
senses.example: If every voter must be counted, a recount is inevitable.
senses.exampleCN: 如果每一张选票都必须被计入，重新计票就是必然的。
senses.why: Logic turns the word from physical prevention to entailment: given the premises, no other conclusion can be drawn. This is necessity in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把这个词从“物理上阻止”转为“蕴含”：给定前提，就得不出别的结论。这是严格意义上的必然性。

senses.title: Predictable and routine
senses.titleCN: 意料之中：老一套、不出所料
senses.definition: so habitual or expected that it can be predicted with confidence
senses.definitionCN: 如此习惯或可预期，以至于能很有把握地预测
senses.example: The inevitable question came: who will pay for it?
senses.exampleCN: 那个意料之中的问题来了：谁来付钱？
senses.why: Here necessity is weakened into habit. The event is not logically forced, but experience makes it feel as if it could not be otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 这里“必然”被弱化成习惯。事件并非逻辑上被迫发生，但经验让它感觉仿佛不可能有别的样子。

senses.title: An unavoidable event (noun)
senses.titleCN: （名词）不可避免的事
senses.definition: as a noun, an event or outcome that cannot be avoided
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时，指无法避免的事件或结果
senses.example: They prepared for the inevitable rather than pretending it would not come.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为不可避免的事做准备，而不是假装它不会来。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun by 1850. English often turns an adjective into a name for the thing that carries the quality, so 'the inevitable' is 'that which is inevitable'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 1850 年前已可作名词。英语常把形容词变成具有该性质之物的名称，因此 the inevitable 就是“那个不可避免的东西”。

senses.title: Death, as the inevitable
senses.titleCN: 委婉语：死亡这一必然结局
senses.definition: in euphemistic usage, death, viewed as the one event no one escapes
senses.definitionCN: 委婉用法中指死亡，被视为无人能逃脱的那件事
senses.example: When the inevitable finally came, the family was ready.
senses.exampleCN: 当那不可避免的结局终于到来时，家人已经做好了准备。
senses.why: The noun use allows speakers to avoid the word death. The euphemism works because the adjective already says everything: it cannot be avoided, so it need not be named.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法让说话者避开“死亡”一词。这个委婉语之所以成立，是因为形容词已经说尽了一切：它无法避免，因此不必点名。

senses.title: Philosophically unchangeable
senses.titleCN: 哲学意义上的不可更改
senses.definition: in philosophy, describing what cannot be otherwise, especially under determinism or fate
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中描述不可能另有状态的事，尤在决定论或宿命论语境下
senses.example: The argument claims that every choice is inevitable in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 该论证声称，每一个选择事先都是必然的。
senses.why: Philosophy pushes the word to its limit: not merely unpreventable by us, but fixed in the structure of causes. Here inevitable approaches 'fated'.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把这个词推到极限：不只是我们无法阻止，而是在因果结构中被固定。此处 inevitable 接近“命中注定”。

senses.title: Unavoidably accompanying something
senses.titleCN: 必然伴随：代价无法剥离
senses.definition: always present as a cost or side effect of a chosen course
senses.definitionCN: 作为某项选择过程的代价或副作用而始终存在
senses.example: Some noise is inevitable in any city-centre flat.
senses.exampleCN: 任何市中心的公寓都不可避免地会有一些噪音。
senses.why: The word can attach to a drawback rather than an event: if you take the benefit, the accompanying cost cannot be separated from it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以附着在缺点而非事件上：如果你要那份好处，伴随的代价就无法从中剥离。

intro.en: Inevitable is a Latin negative built on evitare 'to avoid'. Its first English uses were about unavoidable outcomes; the noun and the death euphemism are 19c developments. The deepest origin of vitare is uncertain.
intro.cn: inevitable 是建立在 evitare“避开”之上的拉丁否定式。它最早的英语用法指无法避免的结果；名词用法与指死亡的委婉语是 19 世纪的发展。vitare 的更早来源并不确定。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'unavoidable, that cannot be evaded'. The earliest context is general predication, not yet a fixed noun.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“无法避免、无法躲开的”。最早的语境是一般性陈述，尚未固定为名词。

items.en: Inevitabilis is in- 'not' + evitabilis 'avoidable'. The prefix is privative: it denies the ability named by the adjective.
items.cn: inevitabilis 是 in-“不”+ evitabilis“可避免的”。这个前缀是否定性的：它否定形容词所指的能力。

items.en: Evitare 'to shun, avoid' is ex- 'out of' + vitare 'shun'. The ex- marks moving out of the way; the whole verb pictures stepping aside from something.
items.cn: evitare“躲避、避开”是 ex-“离开”+ vitare“躲避”。ex- 表示移出原来的路径；整个动词描绘的正是从某物旁边让开。

items.en: The further origin of vitare is uncertain. Standard etymological references treat it as unclear; older guesses linking it to via 'way' or to a root meaning 'away' are not established. Marked source uncertain.
items.cn: vitare 的更早来源不确定。通行词源资料将其视为不清楚；把它联系到 via“道路”或某个意为“离开”的词根的旧猜测并未得到确认。故标为来源不确定。

items.en: The noun use 'an inevitable thing' is recorded by 1850. English can nominalize the adjective with the definite article: the inevitable.
items.cn: 名词用法“不可避免之事”在 1850 年前已有记录。英语可用定冠词把形容词名词化：the inevitable。

items.en: The inevitable becomes a euphemism for death, and inevitability a key term in philosophy and in narratives of history. Inevitably spreads as the everyday adverb.
items.cn: the inevitable 成为指死亡的委婉语，inevitability 成为哲学与历史叙事中的关键术语。inevitably 则作为日常副词广泛使用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the evit- root; the near-meaning group separates 'cannot be avoided' from 'certain' and 'fated'.
note.cn: 形近组共享 evit- 词根；近义组区分“无法避免”“确定”与“命中注定”。

entries.definition: avoidable. It is rare but shows the positive form that inevitable negates.
entries.definitionCN: 可避免的。它虽少见，却显出被 inevitable 否定的肯定形式。

entries.definition: in a way that cannot be avoided; necessarily.
entries.definitionCN: 不可避免地；必然地。

entries.definition: the quality or state of being impossible to avoid.
entries.definitionCN: 必然性；不可避免的性质或状态。

entries.definition: impossible to avoid. It says the same thing with a native prefix and is less formal than inevitable.
entries.definitionCN: 无法避免的。它用本族语前缀表达同一意思，比 inevitable 更不正式。

entries.definition: impossible to escape or evade. It stresses being trapped rather than the certainty of an event.
entries.definitionCN: 无法逃脱的。它强调被困住，而不是事件本身的确定性。

entries.definition: sure to happen. It states confidence; inevitable adds that no prevention is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的；必定发生的。它陈述把握；inevitable 另加“无法阻止”之意。

entries.definition: fixed by fate or destiny. It is mythological or literary, while inevitable can be purely logical.
entries.definitionCN: 由命运注定的。它带神话或文学色彩，而 inevitable 可以纯粹是逻辑的。

normalIntro.en: Real prefixes and real contrasts; in- here is 'not', and evitable is the positive word being denied.
normalIntro.cn: 真实前缀与真实对比；这里的 in- 是“不”，evitable 是被否定的肯定词。

normal.en: in- 'not' + evitable 'avoidable': inevitable is simply the denial of avoidability.
normal.cn: in-“不”+ evitable“可避免的”：inevitable 就是否定“可避免性”。

normal.en: Evitare contains vitare 'shun', not vita 'life'; the word has nothing to do with life.
normal.cn: evitare 含 vitare“躲避”，不是 vita“生命”；这个词与“生命”无关。

normal.en: Compare evitable, inevitably and inevitability: one root, one negative prefix, three parts of speech.
normal.cn: 对比 evitable、inevitably、inevitability：一个词根、一个否定前缀、三种词性。

normal.en: -able means 'can be': evitable = can be avoided; inevitable = cannot be avoided.
normal.cn: -able 意为“能被”：evitable＝能被避免；inevitable＝不能被避免。

normal.en: The noun the inevitable often means death, because death is the event no one avoids.
normal.cn: 名词 the inevitable 常指死亡，因为死亡是无人能避开的事件。

abstract.en: Picture doors closing one by one until only one remains open.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇扇门依次关上，最后只剩一扇还开着。

abstract.en: An equation whose result was fixed before you began solving.
abstract.cn: 一道在你开始求解之前结果就已固定的方程。

abstract.en: The future as a corridor whose side doors have already been sealed.
abstract.cn: 未来是一条走廊，两侧的门早已被封死。

examples.en: Given the shortage of staff, some delays are inevitable.
examples.cn: 鉴于人手短缺，一些延误是不可避免的。

examples.en: The committee treated the merger as inevitable and stopped debating it.
examples.cn: 委员会把合并视为必然，便停止了争论。

examples.en: Inevitably, the cheapest option failed first.
examples.cn: 不可避免地，最便宜的方案最先失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因爱我·逃不脱”——因为爱，我逃不脱，结局不可避免 → inevitable 不可避免的

root: 源自拉丁语 inevitabilis“无法避免的”，由 in-“不”+ evitabilis“可避免的”构成；evitabilis 来自 evitare“避开”，由 ex-“出、离开”+ vitare“躲避”构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of inevitable, all built on one closed route. The closure may be physical, logical, habitual, philosophical, or the final closure of death.
sensesIntro.cn: inevitable 的八个义项都建立在“一条被封闭的路”上。这种封闭可以是物理的、逻辑的、习惯性的、哲学性的，也可以是死亡那最后的封闭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every side road is closed, so only one direction remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：每条岔路都被封住，只剩一个方向。

branches.en: NO ESCAPE AND CERTAINTY: what cannot be prevented is also what will surely arrive.
branches.cn: 无路可躲与确定：无法被阻止的事，也必定会到来。

branches.en: NECESSITY: premises force a conclusion; a causal system leaves no alternative.
branches.cn: 必然性：前提迫使结论成立；因果系统不留别的可能。

branches.en: HABIT: experience makes an outcome feel fixed before it happens.
branches.cn: 习惯：经验让某个结果在发生前就显得已经固定。

branches.en: THE THING ITSELF: an unavoidable event, or a cost that cannot be separated from a benefit.
branches.cn: 事物本身：一个无法避免的事件，或无法与好处剥离的代价。

branches.en: DEATH: the one appointment no diplomacy can cancel.
branches.cn: 死亡：唯一无法通过任何周旋取消的约定。

intro.en: Inevitable is in- 'not' + evitabilis 'avoidable', from evitare 'avoid'. English adds -ably, -ability, -ableness, and keeps the rare positive evitable.
intro.cn: inevitable 是 in-“不”+ evitabilis“可避免的”，后者来自 evitare“避开”。英语加 -ably、-ability、-ableness，并保留少见的肯定形式 evitable。

latinIntro.en: Latin evitare 'shun, avoid' (ex- + vitare) and evitabilis 'avoidable'. Note that vitare is not vita 'life', though the forms look close.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 evitare“躲避、避开”（ex- + vitare）与 evitabilis“可避免的”。注意 vitare 不是 vita“生命”，尽管词形相近。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be avoided; necessarily
items.meaningCN: 不可避免地；必然地
items.example: Inevitably, the news spread faster than the official statement.
items.exampleCN: 不可避免地，消息比官方声明传得更快。

items.meaning: the quality of being impossible to avoid
items.meaningCN: 必然性；不可避免的性质
items.example: The report questions the inevitability of the collapse.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告质疑崩溃的必然性。

items.meaning: the state of being unavoidable (less common)
items.meaningCN: 不可避免的状态（较少用）
items.example: The inevitableness of the change silenced the room.
items.exampleCN: 变革的不可避免让全场沉默。

items.meaning: avoidable; able to be shunned
items.meaningCN: 可避免的；能够被躲开的
items.example: The loss was evitable, but no one acted in time.
items.exampleCN: 这次损失本可避免，但没人及时行动。

items.meaning: in a way that can be avoided (rare)
items.meaningCN: 可避免地（很少用）
items.example: Such errors are evitably caused by haste.
items.exampleCN: 这类错误是可以通过不急躁而避免的。

items.meaning: the quality of being avoidable (rare)
items.meaningCN: 可避免性（较少用）
items.example: Philosophers still debate the evitability of the outcome.
items.exampleCN: 哲学家仍在争论这一结果是否可避免。

items.meaning: impossible to avoid; a native-prefix parallel to inevitable
items.meaningCN: 无法避免的；用本族语前缀构成的同义平行形式
items.example: The overlap in duties was unavoidable.
items.exampleCN: 职责上的重叠无法避免。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be avoided
items.meaningCN: 不可避免地
items.example: The meeting unavoidably ran into lunchtime.
items.exampleCN: 会议不可避免地拖到了午饭时间。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 可避免的；能够被躲开的
躲避；避开（更早来源不确定）

definition_en: to reach a conclusion from evidence or reasoning rather than from direct statement
core_image: 把线索装进篮子带进屋，再从屋里把结论带出来
scene: The detective looks at the wet umbrella and the dry coat and infers that the visitor arrived by car.
sceneCN: 这里 infer 是「推断、推知」（第 1 个义项：根据证据得出结论）；句意：侦探看着湿漉漉的伞和干燥的外套，推断来访者是坐车到的。图中可辨识物件：湿伞、干外套、门口的水迹、侦探的笔记本。

pos.zh: 推断；推论；推知
作推断；下结论

senses.title: Reach a conclusion from evidence
senses.titleCN: 由证据推断：从线索得出结论
senses.definition: to reach a conclusion about something using the evidence available rather than being told directly
senses.definitionCN: 利用现有证据得出关于某事的结论，而不是被直接告知
senses.example: From the wet umbrella we inferred that it had rained.
senses.exampleCN: 从湿伞我们推断出下过雨。
senses.why: Latin inferre is in- 'into' + ferre 'carry'. The mind carries the facts in, and carries a conclusion out. Evidence is the load; inference is the transport.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 inferre 是 in-“进入”+ ferre“携带”。心灵把事实运进来，再把结论运出去。证据是货物，推断是运输。

senses.title: Derive logically from premises
senses.titleCN: 逻辑推出：由前提推出结论
senses.definition: to derive a conclusion from premises by valid reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 通过有效推理从前提得出一个结论
senses.example: From 'all mammals breathe' and 'whales are mammals' we infer that whales breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 从“所有哺乳动物都呼吸”与“鲸是哺乳动物”，我们推出鲸会呼吸。
senses.why: Logic narrows the word to entailment: the conclusion is carried by the premises and cannot be dropped without contradiction.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把这个词收窄为“蕴含”：结论由前提承载，若丢掉它就会产生矛盾。

senses.title: Read what is not said
senses.titleCN: 听出言外之意
senses.definition: to understand a meaning that the speaker suggests without stating it
senses.definitionCN: 理解说话者暗示却没有明说之意
senses.example: When she said 'fine', we inferred that she was not fine at all.
senses.exampleCN: 当她说“没事”时，我们推断她根本没事才怪。
senses.why: This is the hearer's side of implicature. The speaker folds meaning in (imply, from plicare 'fold'); the hearer carries it out (infer, from ferre 'carry').
senses.whyCN: 这是“会话含义”中听者的一侧。说话者把意思折进去（imply，来自 plicare“折”）；听者把它运出来（infer，来自 ferre“携带”）。

senses.title: Judge from signs or symptoms
senses.titleCN: 由迹象判断：从体征看出病情
senses.definition: to judge a condition from observable signs, such as symptoms or readings
senses.definitionCN: 从可观察的迹象（如症状或读数）判断某种状况
senses.example: The rash led the doctor to infer an allergic reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 皮疹使医生推断为过敏反应。
senses.why: Clinical signs are evidence carried into the mind. The diagnosis is not seen directly; it is carried out from what is visible.
senses.whyCN: 临床体征是被运进心灵的证据。诊断并不是直接看见的，而是从可见之物中被运出来的。

senses.title: Surmise; make an educated guess
senses.titleCN: 推测：作出有根据的猜测
senses.definition: to form a probable opinion without complete proof
senses.definitionCN: 在没有完整证明的情况下形成一种可能为真的看法
senses.example: We can only infer what happened after the lights went out.
senses.exampleCN: 灯灭之后发生了什么，我们只能推测。
senses.why: The word loosens from strict logic to plausible guessing. The carrying still happens, but the load may be light.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从严格逻辑放宽到合理猜测。运输仍然发生，只是货物可能很轻。

senses.title: Draw a statistical inference
senses.titleCN: 统计推断：从样本推及总体
senses.definition: in statistics, to generalize from sample data to a wider population
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中，从样本数据推广到更大总体
senses.example: From this sample we infer that the average price has fallen.
senses.exampleCN: 从这个样本我们推断平均价格已经下降。
senses.why: Statistics formalizes the same movement: observed cases are carried into a model, and a claim about the population is carried out.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把同一运动形式化：观察到的个案被运进模型，关于总体的断言被运出来。

senses.title: Bring in (archaic literal sense)
senses.titleCN: 古义：带入、运进
senses.definition: in older usage, to bring or carry something into a place
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中，把某物带进或运进某地
senses.example: The old text speaks of inferring the harvest into the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇旧文说到把收成运进谷仓。
senses.why: This is the Latin literal sense of inferre, 'carry in'. It survives mainly in the derived noun inference, but it explains the physical image behind the mental one.
senses.whyCN: 这是 inferre 的拉丁本义“运进去”。它主要残留在派生名词 inference 中，却解释了心理义背后的物理意象。

senses.title: Bring about or inflict (obsolete)
senses.titleCN: 古义：招致、施加（已废弃）
senses.definition: in obsolete usage, to bring about, cause, or inflict something on someone
senses.definitionCN: 已废弃用法中，招致、引起或把某物施加于某人
senses.example: The chronicle records the war he inferred upon the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史记述了他强加于沿海的战争。
senses.why: Latin inferre also meant 'to inflict, wage'. English briefly used infer in this way, but the meaning died out and only the reasoning sense survived.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 inferre 还表示“施加、发动”。英语曾短暂这样使用 infer，但该义后来消失，只留下推理义。

senses.title: Intransitive: to draw conclusions
senses.titleCN: 不及物：进行推断
senses.definition: to make inferences as an activity, without naming what is inferred
senses.definitionCN: 把推断作为一项活动来进行，不点明所推断的内容
senses.example: Readers infer constantly, even when the text says nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 读者一直在推断，即使文本什么也没说。
senses.why: The intransitive use, recorded by the 1570s, treats inference as something the mind does rather than something done to a particular claim.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法自 16 世纪 70 年代有记录，把推断视为心灵所做之事，而不是针对某个特定断言所做的操作。

intro.en: Infer comes from Latin inferre 'to carry in'. It first meant 'bring about', then 'draw a conclusion'; the modern hearer's sense is defined against imply, which uses a different root (plicare 'fold').
intro.cn: infer 来自拉丁语 inferre“运进去”。它先表示“招致、引起”，再表示“得出结论”；现代“听者推断”的义项则与 imply 相对，后者用的是另一个词根（plicare“折”）。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'to bring about, lead to; to deduce'. The reasoning sense is present from the start alongside the causative one.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录，义为“招致、导致；推出”。推理义从一开始就与使役义并存。

items.en: Inferre is in- 'into' + ferre 'to carry, bear'. Literally 'carry in', it also developed the senses 'bring forward, introduce, inflict, wage (war)'. The English verb inherits the mental and the military possibilities.
items.cn: inferre 是 in-“进入”+ ferre“携带、承载”。字面为“运进去”，也发展出“提出、引入、施加、发动（战争）”等义。英语动词同时继承了心理义与军事义的可能。

items.en: Ferre is suppletive: its perfect is tuli and its participle latus, so Latin-derived words like relate and translate do not look like ferre. English relatives include transfer, refer, prefer, offer, confer, differ and suffer.
items.cn: ferre 是异根动词：完成式为 tuli，分词为 latus，因此 relate、translate 等拉丁来源词看起来不像 ferre。英语同族词包括 transfer、refer、prefer、offer、confer、differ、suffer。

items.en: The intransitive sense 'make inferences' is recorded. Inference becomes the standard noun for the act and the result.
items.cn: 不及物义“进行推断”有记录。inference 成为表示该行为及其结果的标准名词。

items.en: Logic and science make inference a technical term. Illation, from Latin illatus (the suppletive participle of inferre), names the same act in formal style.
items.cn: 逻辑与科学使 inference 成为术语。illation 来自拉丁语 illatus（inferre 的异根分词），在正式文体中指同一行为。

items.en: Usage handbooks insist on the direction: the speaker implies (folds meaning in, plicare), the hearer infers (carries it out, ferre). Confusing the two reverses who does the work.
items.cn: 用法手册强调方向：说话者 imply（把意思折进去，plicare），听者 infer（把它运出来，ferre）。混淆两者会颠倒“谁在做这项工作”。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the fer- root from the unrelated infernal; the near-meaning group marks the direction of reasoning.
note.cn: 形近组把 fer- 词根与无关的 infernal 分开；近义组标出推理的方向。

entries.definition: a conclusion reached from evidence; the act of inferring.
entries.definitionCN: 从证据得出的结论；推断的行为。

entries.definition: relating to hell; awful. It comes from Latin infernus 'lower, hellish', not from inferre.
entries.definitionCN: 地狱的；糟糕透顶的。它来自拉丁语 infernus“下方的、地狱的”，并非来自 inferre。

entries.definition: to send someone to a source, or to mention. It is re- 'back' + ferre 'carry'.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人转介到某处；提及。它是 re-“回”+ ferre“携带”。

entries.definition: to reach a conclusion by strict logical deduction. It is narrower and more formal than infer.
entries.definitionCN: 通过严格的逻辑演绎得出结论。它比 infer 更窄、更正式。

entries.definition: to decide or believe something after considering the evidence. It names the end of the process; infer names the carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 在考虑证据后决定或相信某事。它命名过程的终点；infer 命名“运送”。

entries.definition: to understand or believe something from hints. It is conversational where infer is neutral or formal.
entries.definitionCN: 从暗示中理解或相信某事。它偏口语，而 infer 中性或正式。

entries.definition: to suppose something without strong evidence. It is weaker and more literary than infer.
entries.definitionCN: 在没有强证据的情况下猜想。它比 infer 更弱、更文学化。

entries.definition: to suggest without stating, from the speaker's side. The speaker folds meaning in (plicare); the hearer infers it out (ferre).
entries.definitionCN: 从说话者一侧暗示而不明说。说话者把意思折进去（plicare）；听者把它推断出来（ferre）。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real contrasts; ferre 'carry' is the core, and the in- is 'into'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实对比；核心是 ferre“携带”，in- 是“进入”。

normal.en: ferre 'carry': the hearer carries a conclusion out of the evidence.
normal.cn: ferre“携带”：听者从证据里把结论运出来。

normal.en: in- 'into' + ferre 'carry': facts are carried in, a conclusion is carried out.
normal.cn: in-“进入”+ ferre“携带”：事实被运进来，结论被运出去。

normal.en: Imply folds meaning in; infer carries it out. Same event, opposite directions.
normal.cn: imply 把意思折进去；infer 把它运出来。同一件事，方向相反。

normal.en: Transfer, refer, prefer and confer all carry something; infer carries a conclusion.
normal.cn: transfer、refer、prefer、confer 都在运东西；infer 运的是结论。

normal.en: In logic the premises are the load, and the inference is the carrying.
normal.cn: 在逻辑中，前提是货物，推断是运输。

abstract.en: Picture a basket of clues carried into a closed room; what you carry out is the conclusion.
abstract.cn: 想象一篮线索被运进一间关着的屋子；你运出来的东西就是结论。

abstract.en: The speaker leaves footprints; the listener follows them backwards.
abstract.cn: 说话者留下脚印；听者沿着脚印往回走。

abstract.en: A conclusion is not in the sentence the way a coin is in a pocket; it is carried in by the reader.
abstract.cn: 结论并不像硬币在口袋里那样藏在句子里；它是被读者运进去的。

examples.en: From the broken glass, the police inferred that someone had forced a window.
examples.cn: 警方从碎玻璃推断有人强行开过窗。

examples.en: We can infer from the data that the trend is slowing.
examples.cn: 我们可以从数据推断这一趋势正在放缓。

examples.en: She did not say no, but everyone inferred her answer.
examples.cn: 她没有说“不”，但每个人都推断出了她的答案。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因佛”——因为佛前留下了脚印，便推断有人来过 → infer 推断

root: 源自拉丁语 inferre“带入、运进；推论”，由 in-“进入”+ ferre“携带”构成；核心是“把线索运进来，再把结论运出去”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of infer, all built on carrying. Evidence is carried in and a conclusion is carried out; the load may be strict proof, a symptom, or a hint.
sensesIntro.cn: infer 的九个义项都建立在“运送”上。证据被运进来，结论被运出去；货物可以是严格证明、一个症状，或一句暗示。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clues are carried into the mind, and a conclusion is carried out.
core.cn: 核心意象：线索被运进心灵，结论被运出来。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: an umbrella, a rash or a reading carries a conclusion that is not directly seen.
branches.cn: 证据：一把伞、一片皮疹或一个读数，承载着并未直接被看见的结论。

branches.en: LOGIC: the premises carry the conclusion; dropping it would contradict them.
branches.cn: 逻辑：前提承载结论；丢掉结论就会与前提矛盾。

branches.en: IMPLICATURE: the hearer carries out what the speaker folded in.
branches.cn: 会话含义：听者把说话者折进去的意思运出来。

branches.en: WEAKER INFERENCE: guessing, and inference as a general mental activity.
branches.cn: 较弱推断：猜测，以及作为一般心理活动的推断。

branches.en: EXTENSIONS: statistics formalizes the carry; the archaic senses keep the literal and causative Latin meanings.
branches.cn: 延伸：统计学把这种运送形式化；古义保留了拉丁语的字面义与使役义。

intro.en: Infer is in- + fer- + -r. The -fer family is one of the most productive in English: transfer, refer, prefer, confer, offer, suffer, differ.
intro.cn: infer 是 in- + fer- + -r。-fer 词族是英语中产量最高的词族之一：transfer、refer、prefer、confer、offer、suffer、differ。

latinIntro.en: Latin inferre 'carry in' and ferre 'carry, bear'. Ferre is suppletive: perfect tuli, participle latus, which is why illation and translate do not look like ferre.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 inferre“运进”与 ferre“携带、承载”。ferre 是异根动词：完成式 tuli、分词 latus，因此 illation 与 translate 看起来不像 ferre。

items.meaning: a conclusion drawn from evidence; the act of inferring
items.meaningCN: 推断；推论；推断结果
items.example: The inference was based on two independent clues.
items.exampleCN: 这一推断基于两条独立线索。

items.meaning: relating to inference rather than direct observation
items.meaningCN: 推断的；推论性的
items.example: The claim is inferential, not observational.
items.exampleCN: 这一主张是推断性的，而非观察性的。

items.meaning: by means of inference
items.meaningCN: 以推断方式地
items.example: The link was established inferentially.
items.exampleCN: 这一联系是以推断方式建立的。

items.meaning: able to be inferred
items.meaningCN: 可推断的
items.example: The meaning is inferable from context.
items.exampleCN: 这个意思可以从上下文推断出来。

items.meaning: concluded from evidence; not directly stated
items.meaningCN: 被推断出的；非直接陈述的
items.example: The inferred value is shown in brackets.
items.exampleCN: 推断出的数值显示在括号中。

items.meaning: the activity of drawing conclusions
items.meaningCN: 推断（动名词）
items.example: Inferring is what readers do between the lines.
items.exampleCN: 推断正是读者在字里行间所做的事。

items.meaning: one who infers; a system that draws inferences
items.meaningCN: 推断者；进行推断的系统
items.example: A logic engine is an automatic inferrer.
items.exampleCN: 逻辑引擎是一个自动推断器。

items.meaning: the act of inferring; a conclusion (formal)
items.meaningCN: 推论；推断（正式用语）
items.example: The old logic text uses illation for inference.
items.exampleCN: 那本旧逻辑教材用 illation 表示推断。

items.meaning: relating to inference, especially in grammar
items.meaningCN: 推论的；（语法）表示推论结果的
items.example: Some languages mark an illative case.
items.exampleCN: 有些语言标记“推论格”。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry in, bring in; to deduce; to inflict
